`rm -rf *` and `build/*` run and `.g*` is git's own; what a command writes (`CommandAnalysis.WriteTargets`) - its output redirects,
and each path a writer's words name, a copy's destination however an option names it (GNU's `-t`
and `--target-directory` in every spelling, else the last word, each writer's options that take a
value known by its own table, `CommandAnalysis.Getopt` over `CpOptions`, `InstallOptions`,
`LnOptions`, `RsyncOptions`, and an option it does not know making every operand but the first a
destination; `Copy-Item`'s `-Destination` by any prefix or glued, else its second word), and the
output a program's option or operand names (`CommandAnalysis.OutputsOf`, one owner per program:
`curl -o`, `wget -O`, `tar`'s archive and the directory it extracts into (`-C`, `--one-top-level`),
`unzip -d`, `zip`, `7z -o`, `sort -o`, `patch -o` and the directory `patch -d` writes in, xxd's
output file, sed's `w`, robocopy's and xcopy's destination, `dotnet -o`, a compiler's
`-o`, `cmake -B`, `git format-patch -o`, `ssh-keygen -f`, `openssl -out`, `Invoke-WebRequest -OutFile`,
`Expand-Archive -DestinationPath`, `Export-Csv`, `Tee-Object`, `Start-Transcript`) - meets the refusals every ground keeps on a write, a
pattern within a root of the agent's own that stands inside the state its own place; and a command that runs a program which fetches from the network
(`curl`, `wget`, `Invoke-WebRequest` and `Invoke-RestMethod` with `iwr` and `irm`, `http`, `https`,
`gh api`) is decided as a web request too, by each address it names and each host it reaches (a
proxy, curl's `--connect-to` and `--resolve` targets, the proxy of its environment), under the
`Web(...)` rules and `agentPolicy.webDomains` - the list of the pages an agent reads and the
results a search gives, a search source's own requests held to the `Web(...)` rules alone -
refused where the step has no web, and refused where
the web is held to any rule when it reads what it reaches from a file. What it does not see is said
in help and README - the policy reads words and is no sandbox: the inside of a script file a command
runs, the code an interpreter is given (`python -c`, `perl -e`, `node -e`, awk's `system`), a build
file `make`, `ninja` or `cmake` runs, what an archive or a patch holds, a path a command computes
(`$(printf ...)`), and what a process apart from the agent's tree does. The worktree rules
(`agentPolicy.worktreeRules`, on unless turned off) refuse git's state-writing verbs and the forms of its other
commands that write the same (`AgentPolicy.GitStateForms`, each option met wherever it stands, by `AgentPolicy.Meets`: a
word the shell expands held as one that may be the option where its expansion may give it - a word it begins, quoted
or not, one after a start the option's own may have, or one the shell may split into words of their own where it stands
unquoted (`AgentPolicy.MaySplit`: a variable or a substitution in the open, every positional parameter and array
element by any spelling bash or zsh takes - `$@`, `${@...}`, `${!name@}`, a `[@]`, zsh's `$name[@]` and flag groups -
read of the expansion's own text, cmd's percent and
delayed names), the refusal of one only such a split makes so saying that quoting it lets it through
(`AgentPolicy.QuoteTheExpansion`) - never a quoted one inside a word that begins otherwise, as `--depth="$n"` or a quoted
refspec a variable names, nor a pattern, whose every match begins with what stands before it, as `refs/heads/*`), the
`gh` commands that run them
or write gh's own configuration (`AgentPolicy.GhStateCommands`; gh's own aliases read as the commands they name,
`CommandAnalysis.GhAliases`, and a place gh reads its configuration from set for a command read as `gh config set`),
and the merges
and CI starts of `gh` - each endpoint and GraphQL mutation that merges or starts CI with the `gh`
commands that reach it, one list (`AgentPolicy.GhCiReaches`) that `AgentPolicy.NeverCiCommands`
(`gh pr merge`, `gh pr update-branch`, `gh repo sync`, `gh workflow run`, `gh run rerun`, `gh pr create`,
`gh release create`, `gh release edit`), `AgentPolicy.GhApiEndpoints` (each word's path read to its first `?` or `#`,
for gh's client sends no fragment), `AgentPolicy.GhApiWriteEndpoints` (a ref, a
file, a pull request or a release written: refused where `CommandAnalysis.GhApiWrites` says the request writes) and
`AgentPolicy.GhApiMutations` are read from, and `gh alias set` (a `gh` command named by none of gh's own,
`gh extension exec` among them, is refused on every ground, above) - keep git's own files unwritten whatever
`protectedPaths` says (`AgentPolicy.GitsOwnRule`: a `.git` segment at any depth beneath each tree the agent
touches, `AgentPolicyGround.Trees` - its roots and the main checkout a worktree was made from - in any case, so a
nested repository's hooks and the hooks every worktree runs are as safe as the root's), and hold the tool's own
policy and what the next launch loads unwritten by any agent; its own state
(`HarnessLayout.StatePaths`, the one owner of where that state is, under each tree the agent touches) is held so
whatever any switch says, a writable root standing inside it - the agent's worktree under the worktrees root,
its work directory under the run's records, and a pattern within either - the one exception; the
tool's own verbs (`AgentPolicy.ToolVerbs`, each the command's own name as its service declares it)
and `run-side-task` are refused, run by any program the policy reads or from a response file, whatever the switch
says, and so are the `gh` commands that hand the work to another agent or install what the next launch loads
(`AgentPolicy.GhOutOfStepCommands`) and the commands that print a credential
(`AgentPolicy.CredentialPrintingCommands`, pinned by a test and printed by `help agent-clients`:
gh's token by itself, by `gh auth status --show-token`, by gh as git's credential helper and by
gh's configuration, and git's credential helpers' `get` and `fill`, any helper's by `credential-*` -
each its program and its command, then the words that make it print met anywhere after its command
(`AgentPolicy.Meets`), options before or between them, a short option by any cluster
holding its letter, and any word the shell expands among them held as one that may be them, wherever the expansion stands
in it, for an unquoted one is split where its value holds a blank and cmd reads a percent's value before a quote - a
credential leaves its slot only by the key store that holds it, never through
an agent's words). An alias given a command line is read as that command where it is given -
`git config`'s setting of a key git runs (`CommandAnalysis.ConfigSetting` beside `-c`'s), and
`gh alias set`'s expansion - for the command that later calls it does so by a name no rule reads,
and `gh alias import`, whose aliases are in a file, is undecided; an alias another program writes
into a file is the inside of that program, unseen as help says. The rule a refusal names is the one
that decided: a rule the command certainly is before one it may be, and of the may-bes the
person's own restrictions first, then the worktree rules, then the tool's own refusals. The protected paths (`agentPolicy.protectedPaths`) are Claude Code's own list written out once
as rules (`AgentPolicy.ProtectedPathRules`), pinned by a test and printed by `help agent-clients`,
refused on every client; a step's `writes` is the one source that narrows - a write, and a delete
but of what the step made itself (`AgentPolicy.Delete`): a path of its worktree git does not track
that the record of the step's start does not hold (`AgentPolicyGround.StepStart`,
`Agents\Policy\AgentStepStart`). That record is the worktree's untracked files as git lists them
(`IGitClient.ListWorkingFilesAsync`), taken by `ReasonStepRunner` before the step's agent first starts
and kept in the step's directory (`OrchestratorLayout.StepUntrackedFileName`), so every later
attempt, answer and resume reads the one its first start took; held without regard to case, a
directory held where a path in it is, for it only ever keeps a path from being taken back. The tool
runtime asks git, as each call is decided, which of the files a call takes away - a file deleted,
every file of a directory deleted, a move's source - git lists untracked now (neither tracked nor
ignored), and hands that to the policy, which decides alone; a directory passes where nothing of the
record lies at or beneath it, each path it holds decided on its own. So what a step's commands made
anywhere in its worktree - a build's outputs, which a fold under `foldOutside: fail` would otherwise
stop on - the step may take back on every client, by the one runtime both reach; a path git tracks
or ignores, one the record holds, and a write over the step's own making stay narrowed, and the
refusal says what may be taken back (`AgentPolicy.OwnMakingSaid`). The reporter's reads
are narrowed to the run's directory alone (`AgentPolicyGround.ReporterRoot`: no command, no write,
no web). For Claude Code the policy is rendered, never re-decided, into the launch's settings
(`Agents\Policy\ClaudeSettings`): an ask rule for every tool the launch has, a read of each
credential slot and Claude Code directory, and of each place the user keeps credentials in (all a
directory holds, a file itself), as a deny rule - which Claude Code applies to its searches
too - and the restriction rules as deny rules, absolute once for each root, but where a rule's
pattern there would cover a root the launch writes, each path in the POSIX form Claude Code matches
(`//c/x` for `C:\x`) and a `Write` rule as an `Edit` rule, for Claude Code holds every file tool to
its `Read` and `Edit` rules alone - a second layer, for the engine is asked about
every other call and answers from the same policy in its own
process; a call these rules refuse first is Claude Code's own denial, told by a
`system/permission_denied` line or, for a file tool's call refused as Claude Code reads its input,
by its result alone (`ClaudeLine.CallResult.RefusedByRule`), and counted and recorded once. Where the policy cannot decide a call it denies it, never
allows - nothing runs while the host that would answer is silent or gone. The first client that
asks it is `Agents\ClaudeCode\ClaudeCodeClient`, the `IAgentClient` of `claude-code`: each
launch a new session (`ClaudeLaunch` builds its one argument list and its environment - what
every child of an agent has (`AgentChildEnvironment`), nothing of a Claude Code session the tool
was started in but a name `agentPolicy.keepEnvironment` gives back, every name `ClaudeSettings.LaunchedWith`
sets, in its settings' `env` as in its environment: the names `ClaudeSettings.Launched` sets -
`MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` among them (`ClaudeSettings.McpOutputTokens`, three times `PageRoom.ModelAnswer`),
so Claude Code never cuts a page of the engine's tool server's answer - the two cache lifetimes
(`ClaudeSettings.CacheTtlVariables`) at `agentClients.claude-code.cacheTtl` (`ClaudeSettings.CacheTtlOf`),
and every other name Claude Code caches by (`ClaudeSettings.CacheOverrideVariables`) off, so the
configured lifetime is the one say on a launch's caching whatever the person's environment or settings
hold - and the one credential an `AgentCredential` gives), streamed both ways and read line by line as
`ClaudeLine`s (every kind the probe's recordings hold), each `can_use_tool` it asks decided by
`ClaudeToolDecider` through the policy, the tools it is given - and what a call of each is of - from
the one table `ClaudeCodeTools` holds; an answer held to a schema checked by `StructuredOutputGate`
and sent back while it does not read; a message to an agent at work, a handoff's interrupt and its
turn (its prompt and its refusal `AgentHandoffSignal`'s, every client's; the agent asked once every
message the engine wrote was taken or dropped - each with an id of its own, by which the
interrupt's receipt names those it dropped), the model each message names, and a key reported
invalid moved past with a new launch, all in one launch's loop that the stored stream
(`AgentRunner`) records as it runs. The run's turns are the model's answers, as on the API clients
and as Claude Code counts the turns its `--max-turns` holds: each response a launch writes, counted
as its first line arrives over every launch of the run (`ClaudeLine.Assistant.Id`, which every line of
one response names; a line that names none an answer of its own, a message Claude Code wrote itself
none), so a launch cut before its turn's result still counts what it answered
(`AgentRunResult.Turns`) - never the engine's own exchanges with the launch, which number the turns'
events (`TurnStarted`, `TurnFinished`) and may each hold many answers, as each one's end says
(`TurnFinished.Answers`). The run's end says the result's count (`RunFinished.Turns`), which a step's
measure reads (`AgentRunSpend.TurnsTaken`), as a side-task's record reads each exchange's answers.
A step with the web takes the harness's own fetch and search from the engine's tool server, `Agents\Runtime\AgentToolServer`: one MCP server of type `sdk`
(`ClaudeLaunch.McpConfiguration`, the step's `claude-mcp.json`, which `--mcp-config` names beside
`--strict-mcp-config`), whose every message Claude Code sends its host as an `mcp_message` control
request - the probe found it does so for a host that is no SDK on every version taken, its
`initialize`, `notifications/initialized` and `tools/list` before the launch's init, and each
`tools/call` after the engine allowed the call, naming it in `_meta` (`claudecode/toolUseId`). The
server is the subset of MCP a server of tools needs, our own code over `System.Text.Json`:
`AgentToolServer.Read` sorts a message into one answered at once, a call, or a call's cancellation,
and `AgentToolServer.CallAsync` runs a call by the runtime. The client's loop answers each message, runs a call in the
background only where the engine was asked about it and allowed it, once - one it was not refuses
and fails the step - cancels one its client cancels, and holds each turn's init to the server:
connected, every tool of it taken, no other server (`ClaudeCodeTools.ServerTools`,
`ClaudeCodeTools.ServedName`; a call of one runs by the harness, `AgentToolRunner.Harness`). Its tools' names stand beside
`--tools`, each with an ask rule, and `ClaudeToolDecider` allows a call of one as asked: its rules
are its tool's, each address decided and recorded as it runs, as on the API clients, and what the
runtime refused and asked of the web is counted in the step's result. Once a launch has ended, however it ended, a session file it
left is removed, and what its end could not reach or end where the runner hands its end back
(`ProcessResult.Uncontained`) is said and kept in the result's `uncontained`; a call the engine's
own deciding fails on is a denial like any other, by the rule `undecided`. The client holds each
launch to the protocol in the same loop: the user's settings read first by `ClaudeUserSettings` (a
credential they would give refuses the run, as a configuration that is wrong; the file and its
digest named in the launch's start, the hooks off), the `initialize` answer and the launch's own
end once its input was closed waited on through `Waits`, told every `Waits.SaidEvery` and ended
only by the step's own time, its stop or an ending at once, an init said
before any work and its tools and credential source (`ClaudeLaunch.ApiKeySources`) held to the launch's, and every call
that ran (`ClaudeLine.CallResult.Ran`) one the engine was asked about and allowed; a decline is
`Refused` and an account at its limit (`ClaudeLine.RateLimit`, or the turn's error) `RateLimited`
with an `AgentAccountLimit`, and each moves the step to its next entry - on this client every move
is a new launch, the engine's walk of the step's order. Each client's denials, requests of the web and answers too large for
their events are recorded by the one `AgentCallRecords` (`denials.jsonl`, `web.jsonl`,
`tool-results/`). The harness's own tools, `Agents\Runtime\AgentToolRuntime`, are built for the
API clients - `claude-api` and `glm` - each run's opened by `AgentToolHost.Open`, and serve
the `claude-code` client every one of them through the engine's tool server (`AgentToolServer`, opened by
`AgentToolHost.Serve` for one launch: the server's tools alone, written to the launch's own
`AgentCallRecords`, each call answered by `AgentToolRuntime.ServeAsync`, whose end the launch's
stream tells; `ClaudeCodeTools.ServerTools`, `Served`): the
tools are the one
table `AgentTools` holds (what a step is offered, what help prints and what runs); each call is
held to its tool's schema (`JsonSchemaSubset`), each path to the agent's roots by `ConfinedPaths` -
its spelling, its links followed, a write through no link below its root - before the policy is
asked; reads and searches go through `AgentFiles` (git's listing in a work tree, a walk elsewhere),
which reads every file's bytes through the file as it was opened (`AgentFiles.ReadAsync`), where the
open file stands - `IFileSystem.FinalPathOf`, over `OpenedFiles`: `GetFinalPathNameByHandleW` on
Windows, `/proc/self/fd` on Linux, libproc's `proc_pidfdinfo` on macOS - decided again by the same
rule before a byte passes, the file opened never to wait (`IFileSystem.OpenRead`: on Linux and macOS
opened non-blocking and refused before a byte unless it is a regular file, so a pipe put there hangs
nothing) and read to the bound alone; and every write, made directory, move and removal relative to
its directory held from the writable root it was decided in (`AgentFiles.Write`, `UnfollowedFiles`
over `IFileSystem.Hold`, `HeldDirectory`), every entry on the way opened as itself, so a link put in
place after the check, or swapped in while the tool acts, reaches nothing and the call is refused
naming it (`AgentFiles.Linked`, by `ConfinedPaths.LinksRule`); a directory listed goes by its path,
so what a link put in place of one leads to is listed by name, never a byte of a file read through it,
edits through `EditedText` over `EncodedText` (the encoding rule the graph's `CodeFileText` reads
by too, its lines cut by `CodeFileText.Spans`), a command through `PhaseRunner` as a contained
phase - its environment `AgentChildEnvironment`'s, every name the configuration appoints and every
secret-shaped one gone but those `agentPolicy.keepEnvironment` gives back, its time the call's
`timeout_seconds`, else `agentPolicy.commandTimeoutSeconds` where given, else none of its own
(`AgentCommandSettings`; `maxCommandTimeoutSeconds` retired, refused by `MisplacedKeys`) - and a page through `Web\HarnessFetch`,
which decides every address before it is asked and gives it its turn (`WebFetchGate`: the decision, the record, the
reader's pace, waited for outside the step's stall bound, which measures an answer's silence alone), asks only the `http` and `https` addresses of public hosts
`WebAddresses` allows - checked on the lookup and again on the connection made - and reduces HTML to text by
`WebPageText` over AngleSharp; its redirects a chain (`Walks\Chain`) that ends at its first revisit, an answer read while it moves
(`Waits.WhileMovingAsync`) and streamed whole into the writer its asker gives it (`WebFetchAsk.Into`,
`WebBlocks.PageAsync`), a protocol's own most - a sitemap's 50 MiB - the one size it is held to.
`ResultLines.Writer` (`ResultLinesWriter`) writes text into a call's answer as lines;
`ResultLines.RewriteAsync` puts a kept page inside its block where it lies, and `WebBlocks.Page(TextWriter,
address, status, Action<TextWriter>)` writes the block into a writer. A turn runs its reads together, as many at once as
`AgentToolRuntime.MostTogether` says - one of every `CodebaseGraphService.ReadShare` of the machine's processors, one at
the least - a write or a run alone between them, every call answered in its order. A call's whole result kept in `tool-results/`
(`AgentCallRecords.ResultFile`) is read back by `read_result` through `Agents\Runtime\KeptResults`, a page
at a time: its pages laid by `Pages\TextPages` - the file streamed once, in constant memory, by the encoding rule
`EncodedText` reads by and the line ends `CodeFileText.Spans` cuts at, each page whole lines and a line wider than
a page given in pieces by the one rule `Pages\Paging` cuts a piece by - and only where each page begins kept, by
`Pages\KeptAnswers` in the step's `graph-pages/` beside the graph's pages (`PageKey.OfCall`, a key the graph's
never is), for the conversation's life; a file that changed since its pages were laid is laid again, the page
saying so (`TextPages.Relaid`). A writer of an answer says which of its lines head a block and which belong to one
(`ResultLines.HeadAsync`, `ResultLines.BlockLineAsync`), and an answer past a page keeps its blocks beside its file in
the same pass (`TextBlocks.FileOf`, ended by the digest of the file's bytes), so every page of a result - its first in
the call's own answer and each `read_result` gives - is laid with them by the one path a result's pages are laid by
(`KeptResults.ResultLaidAsync`), and a page that begins inside a block gives its head again; a file viewed is never laid
with blocks, whatever is beside it. `read_result` reads too a message a compaction gave by reference
(`StoredStream.MessageText`, by the id `StoredStream.MessageId` gives it) and the continuation
record (`KeptResults.ContinuationId`), and a call's result file is named by `PageKey.OfCall` of its
whole id.

The loop the API clients share is `Agents\Loop\ToolLoop`, driven in its own tests by a fake provider: one request
after another over an `IChatProvider` - the provider's own wire, its form of a conversation's messages and tools, what
each of its failures is (`ChatFailure`), what a request has used so far (`ChatPart.Used`, counted where it ends
without its turn - and a request the run left once it was sent, by its pause, the person's interrupt, its time or the
handoff's bound, with nothing of it said yet leaves the run's cost unknown, saying so in `AgentCost.MissingPrice`,
never naught), what is heard of an answer that is none of its parts (`ChatPart.Heard`, which keeps the stall bound
from a stream that is alive) - each turn's calls run by the run's
`AgentToolRuntime` (`AgentToolHost.Open`) through `AgentToolRuntime.RunTurnAsync`, which an `AgentTurnCut` cuts when
the run pauses, the person interrupts its turn or the step runs past its time, every call it cut still answered
(`AgentToolRuntime.Interrupted`, `AgentToolRuntime.NotRun`). The person's interrupt (`AgentRun.Interrupt`, an
`AgentTurnInterrupt`) leaves the request under way as the pause does - its partial answer thrown away, so the
conversation is stored whole to its last whole turn - and ends the run `Cancelled` (`AgentTurnInterrupt.Cut`) with
what it used, at the top of the loop or wherever it waits: a gate, a retry's wait, a request, the calls; a host that cannot serve the tools a run is offered says why before it starts
(`AgentToolHost.Unserved`). The loop owns the bounds - `maxTurns` but the handoff turn's, the budget checked before every
request against the cost `AgentPrices` counts (a start without the prices it needs refused by the runner, below),
the duration, the stall - the run's order of entries of its provider and client (the serving model's
keys in the credential's order - the runner hands the run its model's keys from the entry it starts on,
`AgentRunner.CredentialFor` - then each later model of the same provider and client with each of its keys,
up to the first entry of another, `ToolLoop.JoinLaterEntries`; the serving entry `Now`, the walk planned
(`PlannedFor`, by `AgentFallback.Next`) and taken (`TakeAsync`, the new entry asked with tries of its own)
only where a request will follow it), a key refused never asked again of any model, each request through the
gate's lane of its provider and key (`AgentRun.Gates`, `ClientGates.LaneOf`: its input counted as it enters, a
429 setting the cool-down its failure covers, `ClientGate.Met`, a cool-down past the longest wait that limit met at
once), the retries
(`ToolLoop.Backoff`,
`ToolLoopTerms`), the handoff turn (`AgentHandoffSignal`, whose question and answer the claude-code client reads the
same way), a message to an
agent at work (`AgentMessages.TryTake`), the output check (`StructuredOutputGate`), the model each turn names
(`AgentModelIds`, which the claude-code client holds its messages to too), a level a move changed
told in the conversation where the provider takes a message for it and else carried by every request,
the model's own default named by none (`IChatProvider.EffortMessage`, `ChatRequest.FirstEffort`) and the
conversation: `StoredConversation`
under the agent's `sessions/<id>/` - the id itself where it is no longer than a SHA-256 digest,
else its digest (`OrchestratorLayout.SessionDirectoryName`), so an id of any length names a
directory every file system takes - (`AgentRun.SessionsDirectory`, `OrchestratorLayout.SessionDirectoryIn`), each line a
JSON array of the provider's messages written at a point where the history is whole, each message kept and sent back
byte for byte, every request the conversation whole and carrying the context of the model it asks
(`ChatRequest.ContextTokens`), for a provider that keeps its own count of the conversation to send
none past it, so each sends what the last did. The engine's fallback has two owners, one rule each: the loop moves
the run inside the one conversation (`AgentFallback` the rules - what a limit covers, which entry a
cause moves to, which decline moves nowhere), and the runner (`AgentRunner.OrderedAsync`, over the
step's `Order` of `AgentRunEntry`s) walks the rest of the order across clients, a new run for each
entry it takes, watching the events of each client it works for where it got to (`Watching`) and
merging what every entry did into the step's one result (`WalkTotals`, its usage folded by the one fold of usage and
cost, `AgentUsageReport.Sum` over `AgentCost.Sum`: a count is known only where every part with usage has one, and a
part with usage and no cost is unknown, never nothing). A step budgeted in dollars is never started on an entry
without a price of each kind its client is billed by (`IAgentClient.BilledBy`, which reads the one fact of the client's
kind given its entry, `AgentClientKind.BilledBy` through `AgentProviders.BilledBy`: input, cache read and output on
every client, the claude-api client's cache write of its cache lifetime and both of the claude-code client's), nor
on a provider that prices in another currency: the runner refuses it, on every client, before any is taken
(`AgentRunner.Priceless`, in the words of `AgentPrices.BudgetRefusal`) - the step's own first entry ending the step
`NotStarted`, a later one passed over and handed to the serving client as an entry it may not take. The workflow's
check asks the same fact first (`WorkflowValidator`'s budget prices), each model of the order against the client it
is reached through (`AgentResolution.ClientOf`, the one rule the run resolves each entry's client by), so a model the
run would refuse is refused before the run, naming the model, the client and the missing price. The first request asks for a quarter of the model's `maxOutputTokens` (`ToolLoop.FirstMaxTokens`), a turn
cut off while it called a tool, before it wrote anything, or while its request held it to a schema (`ToolLoop.WhileHeld`: the
answer to a nudge would be a whole object of its own), doubling it. A turn the provider paused
is sent again with nothing added for as long as the provider pauses it, through the one owner of
retrying as a cause that passes by nature (`Retrying`, each pause a `RetryTry.Passing`), each
pause told as a notice of `ToolLoop.PausedTurn` with how long the turn has waited; no count of
pauses ends it, only the step's own bounds - its time, its budget, a handoff or an interrupt.
Every message the engine sends the agent - the step's
prompt, a nudge, a repair, the handoff's question, a message to an agent at work - is masked as the system prompt is,
before it is sent or stored. Every client ends a run in the same words, whatever its wire: a step that
never began, a model nobody asked for, an answer outside its schema, a declined request and an account at its limit are
each said by `AgentEndings`, and what a run used, by model, is counted by `AgentUsageTally`.

The requests of one provider and one key go through one lane of the gate (`Agents\ClientGate.cs`, held by its own
tests over a clock and a wait that move only when told): at most `agentClients.<client>.maxParallel` under way at once
(`ClientGateSettings.BuiltIn`, 3 for claude-code, 4 for claude-api and 2 for glm where the entry says none; a client
that signs in with a login one lane by its client, two keys of one provider two lanes keyed by a hash of the key -
`ClientGates.LaneOf`, made once and shared), the API clients' optional buckets pacing a lane's minute
(`requestsPerMinute`, `inputTokensPerMinute` counted as a request enters - one larger than the bucket let in alone once
it is empty - and `outputTokensPerMinute` charged by `ClientSlot.Answered` once the answer is had, each waited out until
the oldest of the minute is a minute old) and a 429's cool-down holding what its failure covers - a model's rate limit
that model's requests on the lane, an account's limit every request of it (`ClientGate.Met`, the one reader of a 429's
wait; `RateLimited`, never shortened by a sooner one; `CoolDownOf`, the longer of the two a model is held by) - all
counted on the clock's timestamps so a wall clock stepped holds no lane. Each client enters the lane at its own seam
(`AgentClientCapabilities.PacesRequests`): the loop the API clients share before each request, its input estimated
(`EstimatedTokens`) - the provider's own search among them, which the loop asks for the tool runtime as the run stands
(`AgentNativeAsk`, the loop's `NativeSearchAsync` over the wire `IAgentNativeSearch`, `ClaudeApiNativeSearch` on the
Claude API: the entry serving the run then, its key's lane by the same turn every request takes, `LaneTurnAsync`, and
what it used counted at once to that entry's part); the runner around each Claude Code launch
(`AgentRunner.InLaneAsync`), whose requests it cannot see one by one.
A cool-down past the client's longest wait (`ToolLoopTerms.LongestWaitOf`) is waited by neither: the loop meets it as
the limit it is, and the runner ends the launch at that limit before it begins, the walk moving on to an entry the
cool-down does not hold. A wait is said as `WaitingToRetry` and ended by the run's pause - a launch paused at the gate
never began, and hands off nothing (`AgentRunner.PausedAtTheGate`) - beside the orchestrator's `maxReasoningAgents`.

The `claude-api` client is `Agents\ClaudeApi\ClaudeApiClient`: the loop over `ClaudeApiProvider`, built for each run
from the run's entries (`AgentEntries`: the provider's, the model's and the client's own where the configuration
declares one, which the runner copies from the step's request) and refusing a start without the provider's and the
model's. `ClaudeApiRequest` is the one owner of a request - its body, its
headers, the version, the betas, what the tool sends itself or never sends (`ClaudeApiRequest.Owned`, which a client's
`requestExtras` may not set, `ExtrasProblems` refusing it when the configuration is read - the sampling parameters the
version refuses on every model among it, `ClaudeApiRequest.SamplingRefused`) and the cache's lifetimes; the provider
streams each answer through `Agents\Http\ApiConnection` - one `HttpClient` for the process, given
no time of its own to connect in (the operating system's own retries end a connection that never
comes), its events read by `System.Net.ServerSentEvents`, a refusal, a network that failed and a
stream cut each an `ApiEvent` of its own, never an exception; a refusal's body read to its end,
each piece heard as it comes (`ApiEvent.Refusing`, told every `Waits.SaidEvery` while it still
comes) and kept whole as it streams in the step's `api-refusals/` (`ApiRecords`, `ApiRefusedBody`),
a body that could not be read to its end a stream cut naming the bytes kept - puts each block back
together from its deltas, and keeps the answer's message as the API wrote it;
`ClaudeApiFailures` is the one table of what each status and error type is to the loop. Its tests replay the answers
under `tests/dss-harness-test/fixtures/claude-api/` through `ApiEndpoint`, a handler that stands in for the network
and keeps every request as it was sent.

The `glm` client is `Agents\ZaiApi\ZaiApiClient`: the same loop over `ZaiApiProvider`, built the same way from the
run's entries (`ToolLoopTerms.Of`, `ToolLoopTerms.Unstartable`, which both API clients start by). What the two API
clients' wires share has one owner each under `Agents\Http`: `ApiBody` writes a request's body - the tool's own members,
the stored tools and messages written raw, a client's `requestExtras` merged and refused where they set an
`OwnedMember` - and `ApiAnswers` reads a posted request's events into the loop's parts (`ApiAnswers.Parts`), says
a refusal, a network that failed, a stream cut, an answer that never began, an ending it does not know and a call it
cannot put back together in the same words for both, settles a turn whose end its calls disagree with
(`ApiAnswers.Settled`: one done that holds calls is a turn of calls, one of calls that holds none failed part way), and
reads JSON's members. `ZaiApiRequest` is the one owner of
a Z.AI request - its body, its header, what the tool sends itself (`ZaiApiRequest.Owned`), every
message as the conversation stored it - and `ZaiApiProvider` reads each chunk into the loop's
parts and puts the message back together - its text, its reasoning and each call's arguments by
the call's index - rewriting nothing of what is sent: once what the model last read and wrote, by
Z.AI's own count, reaches the context of the model the request asks (`ChatRequest.ContextTokens`),
the next request is not sent and the context is full (`ZaiApiProvider.ContextFull`), for the
step's compaction to carry the work on. `ZaiApiFailures` is the one table of Z.AI's codes
(`ZaiApiFailures.Codes`) and of its statuses where it names none (`ZaiApiFailures.Statuses`), which the help says row by
row. Its tests replay the
answers under `tests/dss-harness-test/fixtures/zai-api/`, recorded live by `ZaiApiProbeTests` and curated.

Where a step names an output, every client asks for the envelope `AgentEnvelope` builds round the step's schema -
`notes`, `output` (the step's schema whole, null beside it, its definitions at the envelope's root), `assumptions`
(`AgentAssumption`), and `questions` (`AgentQuestion`, the one shape of a question an agent asks or a step's output
writes) where `AgentOutput.AskRounds` leaves the step rounds to ask - and one `StructuredOutputGate` for each run reads
every answer of it on all three clients: the members by the subset's check, the output against the step's schema under
`$.output` (`JsonSchemaSubset.Problems` from a path, `JsonSchemaSubset.Respelled` for an enum's spelling), what no
schema says (the notes not empty, a null output only where the answer asks, and each assumption and question by its
record's own rule - `AgentAssumption.Problems`, `AgentQuestion.Problems`: every text written, options no two alike, a
recommendation among them - which `AgentRunResult.Problem` and the run's `questions.json` hold them to as well), an
output that reads against its schema held to the step's own rules where it has any (`AgentOutput.Holds`, each problem a
path under `$.output`, sent back as a schema's is and counted with its repairs - the route's rules of a review's
findings and the analyst's evidence alike, one hook), and the run's end - `Completed` or `Asked`, with `PersonAsked`, or
a repair sent back, then `InvalidOutput`. An output that reads and holds is held last to the checks the engine says
will read it next (`AgentOutput.Corrections`, from `FlowStepRun.AnswerCorrections`): each problem a check's own runner
finds of it (`IFlowAnswerCheckRunner`, the one judgement the check's run makes) goes back in the same conversation in
`StructuredOutputGate.Correction`'s words, an `OutputCorrection` event of the stream, no repair counted, for as long as
each answer is new - one that gives again an output it was sent back with is the agent's word that it cannot put what is
left right, and the run ends with it as given, for the check to record. Every JSON an agent reads or its call carries is written by one writer,
`AgentEnvelope.Written`, JSON's own escapes alone and at any depth, so an apostrophe, an angle bracket, an ampersand
or a letter past ASCII reads as it was written: the envelope, a value a problem quotes, a template's JSON value
(`FlowValue.AsTemplateText`, `{run.closure}` among them), the engine's account of the work a piece starts from
(`{piece.before}`), a red leg's digest in the continuation record, a handoff given as the whole answer
(`AgentHandoffSignal.AnswerOf`), each tool's input schema and a measure call's answer. The runner writes
the notes as `notes.md` (`OrchestratorLayout.StepNotesFileName`) before `result.json`, and removes an earlier attempt's
before an attempt begins, for the step's directory is every attempt's; it writes the first user message as sent, masked,
as `user.md` (`OrchestratorLayout.StepUserFileName`) before the client is taken - the parts the attempt was given, held
by the one owner of their order (`AgentPromptParts.FirstMessage`: the run context, the plan updates and the continuation
record, the record only where the conversation is a new one - every launch on a client that renders its conversations,
and any run handed none - the run's prompt as the task). The continuation record itself is built by
`Agents\AgentContinuation` from the step directories of the agent: what it is, the last iterations
word for word from the stored stream of the newest attempt, the newest first and every one of them
(`Iterations`, each
message the engine sent the agent in its place), the handoff, the continuation message after an
attempt that was cut off, the last red build or test, the steps so far, the newest first, with
each one's notes and output whole, and every file changed - nothing of it cut.
`AgentContinuation.RenderAsync` keeps it whole as the step's `continuation-record` result
(`AgentCallRecords.ResultFile` of `KeptResults.ContinuationId`), its pages laid as every kept
answer's are; the prompt holds what it is, how many pages it is, an index of the pages each part
is on and its first page, and `read_result` gives every page. What it reads is copied to the step's
own `handed/continuation/` (`OrchestratorLayout.HandedDirectory`,
`AgentContinuation.CopiesFolder`), which the tool alone writes, through no link, and the agent reads as a root of its own;
the bounds `agentContext.continuation` once held are retired, refused by `MisplacedKeys`. One owner says what an attempt's events are
(`Agents\AgentAttempt.cs`): every run that names the attempt, from the first of them on - an attempt that went on with
an answer is more than one run, each beginning at turn one - its turns numbered across them, and across a launch begun
again inside a run (`AgentAttempt.Items`), a later launch's first message read as its task alone - the inverse of
`AgentPromptParts.FirstMessage`, `AgentPromptParts.TaskOf` - never the run context or the continuation record it
carried, so no record holds another, read alike by the continuation record, the compaction, the engine's handoff and the reason step's compaction
(`AgentAttempt.Of`). The compaction beside it is `Agents\AgentCompaction` (`Reduce`, over the attempt's events, which
the caller windows): the engine's own reduction of a conversation that filled its model's context, made where the step's
limit is answered `compact` - the run context and the task whole as they were first sent, an earlier compaction record
standing for the items its events hold and never copied again, the last `AgentCompactionBounds.LastIterations` (3)
iterations word for word, every earlier message of the agent its text whole with its thinking left
out, every earlier call one line (the tool, its input cut at `callInputChars`, how it ended, the path where its input
names one), every earlier result left out, and every message the engine sent since the first whole - the bounds
`agentContext.compaction`'s (`AgentCompactionBounds`: reducedChars 200000, callInputChars 400, the
oldest messages given by reference where the reduced part is over, each whole in the stored stream
by the id `StoredStream.MessageId` gives it, read by `read_result`), what it kept and reduced held by
`AgentCompacted`. It begins a new conversation, on every client (`AgentRun.Compaction` - the record is the first
message of one, the old kept whole; the loop and the claude-code client ask it before any parts), the step's stream
saying it as a `Compacted` event - why, the session left and the one begun, what was kept and reduced, the sizes - and
its result counting it (`AgentRunResult.Compactions`), once, the event and the count one fact: the runner's one
`CompactionToSay` hands each launch a sink of its own (`LaunchSink`, in `InLaneAsync`) and says it as the first launch
given the compacted conversation begins it - its client telling the sink so (`IAgentEventSink.ConversationBegunAsync`,
told once where the client's own rule of a run never started stops holding: the loop as the provider begins its first
answer with the model asked - `ChatPart.Began`, else the first answer had - claude-code as a call of it runs or a turn
of it ends), or the launch ending any way but `NotStarted` having told none - naming the session the launch began. A run
that ends not started - by the runner, by its client (no model, program, policy or key, a refusal, the web unserved) or
by the provider before any answer began (a model the plan does not serve, Z.AI's 1311; met once one began, it fails the
run) - or held at the gate compacted nothing, and a retry or a move given the same record counts no other. A side-task
whose run given the compaction never started is left outgrown (`SideTaskWorking.Outgrown` reads a run ended
`NotStarted` as one that never worked), so its next message is given the compaction again and says it then. A
compaction carried before a task of its own (`AgentCompacted.BeforeItsTask`, a side-task's, whose why is
`AgentCompaction.OutgrewItsContext`) is the run's continuation in place of the request's (`AgentRunner.ContinuationOf`),
said and counted the same way. What each client is sent: `--json-schema` the
envelope as built; the loop's `ChatRequest.Schema`, which the Claude API sends as `output_config.format` in the copy
`ClaudeApiRequest.Sent` makes - every array bound structured outputs do not take moved into its description, over
`JsonSchemaSubset.SchemasIn` - and which, once the API refuses it as more than it compiles
(`ClaudeApiFailures.RefusesTheFormat`: its grammar too large, more optional or union-typed properties than it takes, or a
schema too complex, each way the API says it held in the one list `ClaudeApiFailures.MoreThanItCompiles` and matched
whatever its case, failed as `ChatFailureKind.SchemaRefused` - a conversation's first request's too, never read as a
model the account is not given), the loop sends the run's later requests none of, the envelope said in words in a message
it appends to the conversation (`AgentMessageKind.EnvelopeInWords`) - never in the system prompt, which every stored
turn's thinking was made under. The refusal is remembered for the client's life - by the `ToolLoop` the client keeps, one
for the process, as the registrations keep each client - by the provider's API address, the model and the envelope
exactly as sent, safe under runs in parallel: every later run of that envelope on that model, in the same session, sends
none from its first request and is told the envelope in words in a message of its own after its first, a notice saying it
was refused earlier in this session with what the API said then, masked (`ToolLoop.SchemaRefusedEarlier`), and so is a
run that moves to that model, or finds another run's refusal of it meanwhile, before its next request; the same envelope
on another model, and another envelope, still send their format. A provider whose wire holds no answer to a schema (`IChatProvider.SendsSchema` false, Z.AI) is told the envelope in words
in a message of the same kind after the step's first, in every conversation the run begins (`AgentEnvelope.InWords`),
so the first message is exactly what `AgentPromptParts.FirstMessage` wrote and `AgentPromptParts.TaskOf` takes apart,
and the attempt's items hold the envelope once (`AgentAttempt.Items`); an answer that read as no JSON asked again in JSON
alone (`ChatRequest.JsonAlone`: no tool offered, `response_format` a JSON object).

The harness's own web search is built under `Web\Search`: each kind of source an implementation of `IWebSearchKind` -
pure, asking and reading only what it is handed - found by the one scan of the core (`CoreImplementations<T>`, which
the codebase graph's languages are found by too) into the registry `WebSearchKinds`, which refuses two kinds of one
name and holds a source to its kind's keys and every source's own (`WebSearchSource.OwnProblems`, the `credential`'s
shape by `WebSearchCredential`). `json-api` reads an answer by RFC 9535 JSONPath (`Core.Json.JsonPath`, the tool's
own, held to the standard's compliance suite, its `match` and `search` by `IRegexp`) through `JsonSearchItems`, its
templates read by the configuration's one brace grammar (`FlowTemplate.Pieces`); `feed` and `opensearch` read feeds
by `FeedItems` over `WebXml`, the one reader of XML from the web; a field is markup only where its source says so
(`JsonSearchItems`' `markup`) or its format does (RSS, an Atom text by its type), reduced by `WebPageText.OfMarkup`, and
any other is text as it stands (`OfText`), never guessed; every status and rate limit is read by
`WebRateLimit` (a pause as given, a year as a year; one no answer sizes the asker's own pace,
doubled by `Retrying.Doubled`), an endpoint's answer to a query by `WebSearchStatus` over it, a
failure told in the source's own words whole; what a site answers is read whole - robots.txt,
every field (`WebPageText`), every item of an answer's page, its titles and snippets as written,
XML however deep it nests (`WebXml`, on the reader's own stack), a JSON answer walked by
`JsonWalk` - held only to its protocols' own facts: a sitemap's 50,000 entries and 50 MiB, those
past them counted and said, and a `<loc>` under 2,048 characters, a longer one refused by name
(`SitemapDocument`, `WebAddresses.SitemapLocLength`); each rule decided in one pass. An I-Regexp
of any length, its groups nested to any depth, is read on a stack of its own and compiled once to
the linear matcher, kept for the process's life; a query is read and evaluated on stacks of its
own (`Frame`), so a filter nested however deep evaluates. One past the automaton .NET's linear
matcher builds is refused in its words (at parse time where written in the query, at the filter
where read from the document), never matched as nothing (RFC 9535; RFC 9485 section 8). And `sitemap` is answered by the harness's own index of a site
(`Web\Index`): `WebIndex`, BM25 over `pages.jsonl` - each page whole, its title, every heading and
all its text, every term however long, a hit's snippet cut from the text when it is asked for
(`WebIndex.SnippetLength`), its hits a page at a time with how many answer in all
(`WebIndexFound`) - under `.orchestrators/.web-index/<source>/`
(`OrchestratorLayout.WebIndexDirectory`) - lines that only grow, a page that could not be read among them, written anew
under a new generation once the lines replaced outnumber those kept and `SitemapFill.MostStaleLines`, never emptied
(`AppendLog.Lines`) - filled in the background by `SitemapFill`
(`RobotsTxt`, `SitemapDocument`, the fetch asked by `WebFetchAsk` for markup, a page's parts, a gzip, or text whatever
type its server says; a fill that leaves nothing a search may find stops short, and why one stopped short is kept until
one ends whole; every sitemap reached by `Walks\Walk`, each once however many name it; a page
that could not be read recorded and the fill going on, however many fail in a row; a fill that
stopped short begun again by the next search;
every page and redirect, and every sitemap of the site robots.txt does not name, held to robots.txt; each request at the
site's crawl delay and in the source's turn the run's gate gives) through `WebIndexes`, one fill of an index at a time
on the machine, filled again whenever the source's settings change.
The configuration's sources are `agentWebSearch`, laid over the built-in ones key by key (`WebSearchSources`, the one
owner of what the sources are, from the embedded `Templates/web-search-sources.json`, which `init` writes): each held to
its kind's keys and every source's own where the configuration is read (V56), a reason step's `search` held to them
where the workflow is (V55). `web_search` is a tool of the runtime (`AgentTools`), offered to a step that has a source,
its schema naming them; it asks `HarnessWebSearch`, which owns every rule that is no kind's: the query held to the mask,
each source in its own part (`WebSearchPart`), what its lookups found read once a run and each answered query kept in
the run's `web/searches.jsonl` as any step may be told it - masked as below, a result whose link holds a secret left out
and counted - with each address it was asked at and whether its key was sent (`WebSearchRun`) - a later step of the run
given it under its own rules, each of those addresses decided again, and why a lookup found nothing never kept, nor a
pause asked for but by what the source answered - each address a source asks for the step decided by the mask - a secret
behind its escapes too, as `web_fetch` decides (`LineMasks.HoldsUnescaped`, and recorded and told by `RedactUnescaped`) -
then by the policy's `WebSource` - the `Web(...)` rules, never `webDomains` - and recorded before it is asked, a
sitemap source's site decided so before its index is searched and the pages its fill reads by the policy's `WebFill`,
the configuration's `Web(...)` rules alone, since the index outlives the step, each result held to `Web` and left out
and counted where refused, each request made - a later page of a source's results among them,
asked by `web_search`'s `page` - counted against `maxPerStep`, each source's `perMinute` and
`perDay` held machine-wide by one record beside admission's, a source that names no `perMinute`
asked one request at a time by a lease in that record that the process asking holds
(`WebSearchPace.TurnAsync`, `Waits.WhileHeldAsync`), and a pause it asks for kept there
(`WebSearchPace`), a key read by
`WebSearchKeys` from the slot or `gh auth token --hostname` for the source's host - the gh login's token held by its one
owner (`GhLogins`), in memory alone, never in a record: read once per engine session (`EngineSession`) and kept for its
every step, read again before the expiry the host tells of it passes - `gh` says none, and GitHub's API names it on each
answer to a request a token that expires signed (`github-authentication-token-expiration`), read again a minute ahead
(`GhLogins.Ahead`), once for that expiry - and read again once where the host refuses a request it signed as unsigned
(401), the request then sent once more with the token read where it is another and never a third time, a second
refusal answered as the first would have been (`WebSearchRenewal`); a reading that gives no token - gh signed out, or not
answering in time - is held nowhere, so the next step reads gh again, never takes the place of a token held, and leaves a
step that began without one to be sent the token the session comes to hold, read by another of its steps; each token a
step comes to send held by its mask before it is sent (`GrowingMask`) - a slot's key sent to the scheme, host
and port the source's own address writes alone (`IWebSearchKind.KeyOrigin`, a source whose address takes its host from
what discover finds refused one where the configuration is read), a gh login to that host or its API alone
(`WebFetchKey.Origins`), never a host a document the source read names - and added by the fetch to what it sends the
scheme, host and port each of the source's search requests first asks alone, where it is one of those - its lookups are
sent none - as a header or a query parameter, over https alone, never to an address a record or an answer holds - a
query parameter of its name is dropped from every address, a redirect's
that echoes it back among them, and a first address naming one refused (`WebFetchAsk.Key`) - each address it may not go
to refused by the key's own rule (`HarnessFetch.KeyRule`) before the step's rules decide it, nothing sent, and recorded
as theirs are - the step's mask holding each form it is sent or echoed in (`WebSearchCredential.Forms`) masking each
answer as written before its kind reads it, its form kept - one that still holds a secret behind its escapes not read,
so no reader's cut parts one - and each text the kind read of it as the step is told it - behind its percent-escapes and
HTML's character references too - read as a page's reader reads them, every name HTML holds and a number with no `;` -
however many readings deep (`LineMasks.RedactUnescaped`: no count of readings ends it, each escape
undone shortening the reading, so the readings end of themselves), a text its reader cut short, its cut marked, cut again before
what could be a secret's start in any reading of it, an escape the cut left unfinished dropped (`LineMasks.RedactHead`) -
so no half of a secret is told - and each part given in a `<web-search>` block by `WebBlocks`, the one owner of how
text from the web reaches a model, a page's `<web-page>` among them.

This build checks workflow definitions and starts and drives a run of one (see "Running a workflow" below). Each
step is given to the runner of its type
(`FlowStepRunners`, over every `IFlowStepTypeRunner` the root registers - `FlowStepRunners.Served` lists them, and a test
holds the two to each other); a step of a type none serves yet fails, saying no runner serves its type. Those served
are machine steps, each a thin adapter over the owner of its rule: `OrientRunner` reads the main checkout by
`FlowCheckout` - the one probe the run's start reads too, over `IGitClient` and `GitRemotes`, the remote's forge
among what it reads - and each fact by its owner
(`LegSelection`, `TestInvocationResolver`, `AnchorCitationService.RootsOf`, `CiSettings.Unset`, `MutationService.Declares`,
`OrchestrationRules.OpenAgents`, `TreeHolders`); `GraphifyCodebaseRunner` checks the graph's longest path against the
run's directory and syncs the run's one codebase graph through `ICodebaseGraphService` (`Core.Codebase`, below);
`PlanCheckRunner` holds the items its `items` yields to `PlanValidator`, whose path budget is
`FlowRunPaths`'s with the deepest file an item owns, which reads each path an item owns and must not touch from the
repository's root (`GlobPattern.FromRoot`, below), and which also holds each item to its classes (P-C1 to P-C8)
and its tests (P-C9: the units its change affects in `tests`, none blank, or why it affects none in `noTests`, exactly
one of the two):
an item declares the classes of the decisions it changes or says in `noClass` why it decides none; a class id names
one class in a plan; each home and each site is a path inside the tree, held to the rule a path an item reuses is
(`OrchestrationRules.PathsProblem`), and one that is not is said and matched and looked for no further, so a `..`, a
doubled separator or a rooted path is the plan's problem, never the check's failure; the home is among the item's own
paths and there in the tree where it exists; a site is the home exactly where its path, compared as the machine
compares paths, and its symbol are the home's, and only that site is marked `home`; every other site changes -
`reads-home` or `deleted` - and is the item's too, for patching some of a class's sites is never done; more than one
site means consolidate, as one site that is not the home does; a class is searched by data its queries name again,
and its universe (P-C7, read by the one reading of a planned universe, `ClassClosureReading.PlannedAxes` and
`CellsOf`, each axis a `UniverseAxis`) answers each axis in one of the two ways an axis is answered - applying exactly
where it names values, with where the repository declares them and no why; not applying where it names none, with
why and nothing declared - and counts the cells its axes that apply make - the product of the counts of their values,
1 where none applies: the size of the decision as the plan states it, which its audits, its builder and its closing
review are each given with the class, and no other rule reads - while that it answers every axis the closure text
lists, by a member of its own (`kinds`, `targets`, `configurations`, `formats`, `entryPoints`, `tiers`, `forms`,
`directions`, and `further` for the further axes the text's heading "This repository" names, never its references or
its optimised forms), each in the one shape of an axis (`plan.schema.json`'s `axis`: `values`, `declaredIn` and `why`,
all three required, no union), is `plan.schema.json`'s to hold, so the structured-output check sends an omission
back within the plan step, as the check's own rules send back an answer that is neither way, and neither costs an
audit or another planning iteration; and one home belongs to one item - two classes of one item
may share one, a place that decides more than one thing, which that item changes alone. What the check finds reaches
the agent that gave the items within its own step: the engine holds the answer of every reason step whose output the
`items` of a check of its scope reads - the plan and a plan update through `plan.latest`, a round's self-audit through
`previous`, the diagnosis and its redirect through `diagnose.latest` - to that check at the answer
(`FlowCoordinator.AnswerChecksOf`, over the types that judge an answer, `WorkflowStepTypes.StepType.JudgesAnswer`: each
key read as the check's start reads it, `StartReadsOf` and `ReadExpressions`, with a plan check's own, `CheckReads`, and
the judged one from the answer, `FlowAnswerCheck.ReadOf`), judged by `PlanCheckRunner.AnswerProblemsAsync`, the one
`Checked` its run makes, so a problem the planner can put right costs no audit and no planning iteration; a check of
another scope, and one whose other reads or texts cannot be read yet, holds the answer at its own moment alone, and the
check runs after it as before, the record and the gate. The builder closes
the class (part 01's B and C): the implementer's definition and the implement and remedy prompts hold the
class-closure paragraph, every prompt that goes on with an item - mend, rework, reconcile, anchors, unblock, redo and
undo - reads the item's classes and the record so far (`{input.item.classes}`, `{implement.latest.closure}`) under
"The class you are closing", and the implement step's answer schema requires the record of each class (`closure`:
class, invariant, home, sites before and after, searches citing the tool calls that made them, the universe covered,
the pin, the arm, each neighbour and its measurement, the closing claim), each class's arm in its own entry; where the
repository declares legs, each reason step whose agent runs commands is given the `measure` tool (`AgentMeasureSupport`
on the step's request and run, standing alone in its turn), by one rule - `AgentMeasureSupport.OfferedOn`, the ground's
tools given `run` - that the engine gives it by, the tool runtime offers it by and the Claude Code client serves it by,
so no launch is told to take a tool its server does not list; its every call - a leg, its variant, a filter, the cell
measured - runs through `ITestLegs` as a leg step's legs are (`FlowStepLegs`, the one owner of a step's legs: the
isolation decided first, the process scope over the step's directory, the ledger kept), in the agent's worktree where
it has one - an agent that only reads measures its own tree, at the main checkout's HEAD or the commit its step names,
which no fold moves and the
start of its next step takes back - and in a local copy of the main tree where it does not
(`ReasonStepRunner.MeasuredAsync`), read by
`FlowLegVerdicts.ClassOf` - a red leg failed, a leg that passed passed, every other verdict unmeasured with the leg's
words as why - and answered with the verdict as the ledger spells it, the run's directory and the call's own records,
`measures/<call id>/` of the step's directory (`AgentMeasureSupport.RecordsOf`: the ledger, a red leg's log in an
agent's worktree, and what the call answered, `measure.json` at `AgentMeasureSupport.RecordFileOf` - the one owner of
where it is, which the tool runtime writes it at and `AgentMeasureSupport.RecordOf` reads it back from, a record with

(`FlowUpdateGates.ChecksTheItemsARoundOpensWith`, over `FlowUpdateGates.RoundsOpenedWith`, the groups whose rounds

any round, holds every item to the tree.
A start tree that cannot be read is never silent: the session
warns once why (`TreeDirectories.UnreadWarning`, through the records' warner), and every refusal its reading causes

directory it matches covers what is beneath it. Two entries
meet (`GlobPattern.Overlaps`) only where some path a tree can hold matches both: a path naming no directory holds
