and macOS, by its file id on Windows (`IHeldNative.OpenAbove`), one moved or replaced meanwhile
refused - and each listed by its handle, never by a path (on macOS by a descriptor of its own,
since a deep directory's path outgrows MAXPATHLEN), a link among them removed as the
link, and a directory a volume is mounted on never gone into but refused (`HeldDirectory.IsMountedOn`,
`JunctionRemovalException`) - on Windows a mount point, on Linux a mount's root by `statx`, a bind mount among them,
and on macOS another device (every recursive removal the tool makes, `IFileSystem.DeleteDirectory` among them). A pull alone follows a link
along the path it names, as it is spelt, and refuses one that leads into a place the isolation hides from every
command, decided by where what it opened stands (`ISyncTransport.PullFileAsync`, `ListFilesAsync` given the hidden
places of `IAgentIsolation.Hidden`, the one list the profiles hide, `IsolationHidden`); a host over ssh decides it
against its own (`SyncServe.Pull`, `SyncServe.List`). The step answers `isolation`
(`AgentIsolationRecord.ToOutput`, in `WorkflowStepTypes`' output of each leg step). The tool's own git runs none of
the repository's hooks (`GitHooks`: every command `GitClient` runs is given `core.hooksPath` at the null device,
`/dev/null`, `\\.\NUL` on Windows, through `GitOwnSettings.Apply` with the tool's other settings, but the subcommands
that only read, `GitHooks.Questions`, which answer where the hooks are as git runs them) but a commit's and a push's
(`IGitClient.RunWithHooksAsync`), which `GitPublisher` runs inside the isolation `CommitStepRunner` and
`PushStepRunner` ask of the main checkout's ground (`ExecutionGrounds.OfHooks`) before anything is staged or pushed; a
push inside one, to a remote over http or https, is handed the credential git's helpers give for its address, asked
outside (`IGitClient.CredentialAsync`, `git credential fill`), as values its environment holds and the one helper its
command line names reads (`GitCredentialValues`). Both answer `isolation` beside what they answered.
A step's records are kept where the one owner of a step instance's
directory spells it (`OrchestratorLayout.InstanceDirectory`, a work item's brackets as `FlowInstanceId.DirectoryOf`
writes them), named on the request (`AgentStepRequest.RecordDirectory`) for the runner, the advisor and the handoff's
read alike. A safe pause - and a plan update that ends a step in order - hands a reason step off by one path
(`FlowCoordinator.HandoffTurnAsync`): the agent is asked in its own conversation (`FlowTelling.Ask`, the attempt's
`AgentHandoffSignal`, which the client answers by ending the attempt after the handoff turn), its runner is waited for
within `handoffSeconds` - all the steps at once - and ended where it outlives them or a stop comes, then waited for
within `PointOfNoReturn.SafePauseDrain`; only then is the answer read of the step's own record
(`IFlowHandoffRunner.HandoffAsync`, `AgentRunner.ResultFileName`), the engine writing the handoff where it holds none.
What the step claimed is held through the turn and let go of after it by one rule for both
(`FlowCoordinator.AfterTheHandoffTurn`): a runner that has not ended keeps it held until it answers
(`FlowInstance.Lingering`), so neither an always step of the pause's always phase nor the visit an update makes again
in its place starts beside a runner still writing; else it is given back.
The coordinator deletes the read-only agent once no step can go on with its work (`FlowCoordinator.ReadOnlyAgentsOver`,
over the declarations that resume its maker and the instances drawn of them, each agent once - `_deletedAgents` - through
the `deleteAgent` the service wires to `IAgentService.DeleteAsync`, which removes its tree and folds nothing, writes a
refusal and a throw alike in the agent's log and takes an agent with no record as deleted already).
The key a step starts on is chosen with the order (`balanceKeyUsage`): the resolution's entries built by
`AgentStepOrder.Of` keep the list's order, or - where the configuration balances the keys - each model's keys run by
least spent in the last seven days (a tie in the list's order, for `OrderBy` keeps it), the week read by
`Agents\AgentKeySpend.cs` from `.orchestrators/key-spend.jsonl` - the repository's records across runs, one line for
each entry that ran (the time, the provider, the key's name never its value, the model, the cost - what the client
reported where it does, else what the engine counted), written and read under `OrchestrationStore.AcrossRuns`, its
lines older than the week dropped when it is next written - and each entry's run recorded through the request's
`IAgentSpendSink` (`AgentRunner.SpentAsync`: each part of the run's usage under the key its requests were signed with -
a client that moved keys while it worked reports each key's part apart, `AgentModelUsage.Key` and `Cost`, counted by
`AgentUsageTally` - a part with no cost known or signed with a login recording nothing, and a record that cannot be
written said as a notice, never ending the step).
Each request an API client sends, and each Claude Code launch, goes through the gate of its provider and key
(`ClientGate`): the API clients' loop enters
the lane for each request and `AgentRunner.InLaneAsync` holds each Claude Code launch - the key's own value is the
account; a login one lane by its client - the answer's tokens charged to the output bucket and every 429 the account
met setting the cool-down its failure covers from when the provider said the limit lifts, beside the orchestrator's
`maxReasoningAgents`.
The asking is the runner's too: a failed agent is tried again on its model - the step's `retries`, absent
the workflow's `maxRetries`, waiting its `backoffSeconds`, absent the workflow's, twice as long before each later try
(`AgentRunner.OrderedAsync`, `AgentStepRequest.Retries`/`BackoffSeconds`, the waits said as `WaitingToRetry`), from the
entry that served it last and never on a key refused or limited (`AgentRunner.RetryPlace`) - and
then moved to the next model as a decline moves, past the model's other keys. A run that ended on a key the provider
refused is no failed agent: it moves to the next key of its provider and client at once, waiting no backoff. The
run's pause ends a retry's wait and begins no launch after one ended - the step ends handed off with no handoff, saying
so (`AgentRunner.PausedWhileItWaited`, `PausedBeforeItsNextLaunch`, beside `PausedAtTheGate`). The provider's service failing past the
client's own tries (`AgentRunResult.ServiceFailed`, set where the loop says so) is neither retried nor moved past, nor
is a run that ended `RateLimited` with no entry left ended a failure: each is answered `FlowStepResult.SafelyPausing`,
and the coordinator ends the step stopped and asks the run for a safe pause of the cause `limits`
(`FlowPauseRequest.Causes`), which resumes that very step - merged with a pause a person asked that the loop has not
taken yet (`FlowCoordinator.RequestPause`: the first asker's cause, `all` where either said it). What a reason step
spends is charged to the run's budget as its agent works (`AgentRunSpend`, the request's event sink: each turn's
`UsageReported`, every token of every kind - `AgentUsage.AllTokens` - and its cost at the configuration's prices for the
model serving it, handed on by `IFlowRunEvents.Used`), and each launch is held to what is left of the run's dollars
before its reserve where that is less than its agent's own `maxBudgetUsd`, or where it names none
(`FlowStepRun.BudgetLeftUsd`, `FlowRunBudget.Bound`); a launch that bound ended is the run's reserve reached and not the
step's own budget (`FlowStepResult.AtTheRunsReserve`, `PauseCause` `budget`) - of the grant its share was reckoned under
(`FlowInstance.ShareGrant`, taken as its runner is asked): where that grant still stands the workflow's answers may allow
more, the step running again at once given its handoff, else the run pauses for its budget; a share reckoned before more
was granted reaches no reserve of the grant that stands, and the step runs again at once given its handoff. Dollars
are folded by one owner (`FlowDollars`: the counted sum, and the first reason a part could not be counted) for an agent
run's turns (`AgentRunSpend.Dollars`), an advice (`FlowAdvice.Dollars`), the reporter's answer (`FlowReported.Dollars`)
and the run's reasoning (`FlowBudgetSpent.Charge`): a turn whose cost cannot be counted - its model has no price of a
kind it used - is handed on with no cost and why (`IFlowRunEvents.Used`'s `uncounted`), never as nothing, and leaves the
run's dollars known only as at least the counted sum - `flow.json`'s `spent.uncounted` (`FlowBudgetRecord.Uncounted`,
absent where every part was counted, a record without it read as counted whole), said by status, the report and every
`--json` (`FlowDollars.Said`, `spent.uncounted`, an ask's `cost.uncounted`). In a run budgeted in dollars such a part
reaches the reserve for the grant that stands as a launch its share ended does (`FlowCoordinator.Charge`), so the run
asks, and a grant of more goes on with each launch held to what is left as far as the dollars were counted. Either mark
is kept with what was spent, never in the engine's memory alone (`FlowBudgetSpent.ReserveMetAt`, `flow.json`'s
`spent.reserveMetAt`, absent where nothing met the reserve past its count and refused at a grant the run was never
given): the uncounted part's with its charge, the share's set before the write that records the launch's end, so a
resume after a crash at any write from there asks once, before anything starts again - never by running the step past
the reserve to meet it a second time - and a grant of more recorded since goes on.

Every step instance's work is measured as it runs, on its own record (`FlowStepMeasure`, `step.json`'s and
`flow.json`'s `measure`, one owner in `Orchestration\Flow\FlowStepMeasure.cs`), null until the run draws it: when it was
ready (`readyAt`, the moment the pass of the engine's decisions that left nothing holding it but room began - its last
dependency's end, its making, its group's opening, a hold let go: `FlowCoordinator.DrawFreed`, every step one pass
frees ready at the one moment and drawn in the one place of the run's own order, the step record's `drawnIn`, so a
group's member, made a round of the pass after its group, never ranks after a step the same pass freed beside it; what
held it
before, the steps it depends on or the run's own holds, is theirs and never its wait; a group, which runs nothing of
its own, holds none), how long it waited and on what (`waited[]`, by the words a record's `waitsOn` holds - the
reasoning limit, a claim, a person's answer, the machine its legs run on holding every one of them still to run in its
queue, for its memory or for its room - folded where the causes change at every write and every walk, each period as
exact as the clock gave it), how long it ran (`ran`, the sum of its attempts' runs) and how long it stood stopped for
the run's own pause or a crash (`paused`). The open wait is kept in the record with its time (`waitingOn`,
`waitingSince`), so a wait that spans two sessions is one wait, whole; at a resume every open wait but a person's is
closed where the session before wrote its last record (`FlowResumeState.LastRecordAt`), and the time from there is its
pause. One entry per attempt (`attempts[]`), opened as the attempt starts, holds its own times and outcome, each run of
it (`runs[]`: an asking closes one and its answer's continuation opens the next, as the machine holding its legs and
letting one start does), what served it - the provider, the model, the effort, where a fallback moved it from and
why - its tokens by kind and dollars, each part of them by the model that served it at the price copied as its cost was
counted (`parts[]`: a price changed in the configuration later never changes what a past turn cost), the uncounted
reason where a part could not be counted, how many usage reports it was charged (`reports`), the turns (the model's
answers, one response each, on every client: each run's own count as its end says it, `RunFinished.Turns`, and for a
run a crash cut before its end the answers its ended turns held, `TurnFinished.AnswersHeld` -
`AgentRunSpend.TurnsTaken`), the tool calls by name with their failures and denials (a denied call is a call and a denial, never a failure), the compactions, what
it asked of the codebase graph in pages past the first (`graphPages`: how many, and the deepest page one answer
reached, with the operation that asked it and how many pages were asked of that answer - an answer its operation and
its inputs less the page, keyed as a kept result is - whichever client called the tool, by the one reading of a
stream's tool names (`AgentStreamCalls.ToolOf`); a page refused counts nothing, for it read nothing, and an ask is
counted as its call ends well, so a resume replays the same count from the stream), and
for a machine step what each leg did (`legs[]`: its verdict, its time, how long its machine held it before it let it
start, each phase's time and its digest's counts), the first error its digests read as it ended and the question raised
of the step while it was its own - kept after the question is answered, so each attempt says its own and never the
step's newest; the failed attempt the engine runs again carries its backoff
(`retryAfter`). What an attempt spends is counted once, at the one place a token is counted
(`FlowCoordinator.TakeMessage`'s usage branch, `Charge`): every turn charges the run's budget and the attempt's entry
with the same numbers, so the run's `spent` is the sum of its instances' - and is summed from them again at a resume,
for a step's record is written before the run's, with what a build that kept no measures recorded before them
(`flow.json`'s `spent.unmeasured`). A turn of an attempt that is over - a handoff turn answered as a pause hands the
step off, one its runner reported as the attempt ended - is written to the step's own record as it is charged (a
`step` change saying so), for a resume gives back from a stream only what an attempt still running spent. What the
advisor spent answering a step's own questions is kept beside them (`measure.advice`, never in an attempt, for the
advisor's turns are its own records'), on the step's own record as each advice is taken (an `advised` change about
the step, which writes its record: `FlowRunRecords`). An attempt a crash cut off - its
record still `Running` - is completed at the resume from its own stored stream (`IFlowHandoffRunner.AttemptOf`: the
events of the attempt the record says it was on, replayed through the engine's own count of a run's spending, each turn
priced as it was reported): only the turns past what its entry was charged (`reports`) are charged now, its run ends
where its stream did, and a stream that does not read whole, or cannot be priced, says so as the part's uncounted
reason. A machine step keeps no stream: its cut attempt is completed from the ledger its legs' run keeps in its step
directory as it goes (`FlowStepLegs`: written as the run claims its directory of records, naming the run and that
directory, again as each leg ends with every line so far, and whole at the run's end - `ILegRunWatch.Began` and
`ILegRunWatch.Ended`, which carries the leg's line; each write as the legs work is a record of their progress, never a
reason to lose their run, so one the file system refuses - a full disk, access refused, where another program's hold on
the file is waited out by the atomic write itself - is said once, as a warning, and the legs work on, the write at
the run's end being the one that must succeed), read by the ledger's own reader (`LegStepRunner.CutAccountOf`, read
through the same account every cut step is completed by) - each line a leg of the attempt that ended, as its measure keeps
it (`FlowStepLeg.Of`, the live ending's own reading, its phases with their times and its digest's counts among it), and
the attempt closed where its legs' work stopped: the latest the ledger and any record of the run it names were written,
each phase's log as it streams among them, so a build cut off two hours into its legs closes two hours in, with the legs
that had ended; a directory that holds no ledger, one that does not read - a line's digest of no digest's shape among it -
or one an attempt before left there - written before this attempt's run began, and so not this attempt's - leaves the
attempt with no legs and its run closed at the run's last record, as a step that kept no record of its own. The machine a step's legs run on tells its holds as each wait of a leg's admission begins and ends
(`AdmissionRequest.Told`, `ILegRunWatch.Admitting`; an ssh host's by a note its dispatcher reads) - a wait for a slot in
the dispatch queue's fair order, for the memory and for the room, then taken as the queue grants the leg its slot and
ended as the slot is given back or the leg is refused or stopped as it waits, so the measure sees every wait the queue
makes - and the step is held - its run stopped, its wait on those causes open - while every leg it placed that has not
ended waits there and none holds a slot (`LegStepRunner.StepHold`).

The report of a run is built from its records alone by their one owner (`FlowRunReport`, from `flow.json`,
`questions.json`, `updates.json`, `events.jsonl`, the item agents' closure ledgers and the frozen definition, read for
every report of the run in one place, `FlowService.SourceOf`, with what the run's engine is doing): the same records,
the engine doing the same, give the same bytes in every form -
text for a terminal, `--json` as one document, `--markdown` for a pull request or the clipboard - with the steps in the
run's order (the instance order of `flow.json`), every row of a list with an id of its own (an error
`<instance>@<attempt>`, a signal `<kind>#<n>`, a convergence row its list, the item, step or agent that said it and
what it is of), every number in one fixed form (durations to one decimal, dollars to four with the currency, times as the records keep them) and never a word
of now: a run still going is said so at the time of its last record, marked partial. What the records cannot give is
said in its `notes` - an events file not read whole, in its reader's own words (`FlowEventLog.Read`): a torn last line,
or the lines from the first that holds a NUL on, what a power loss left of a pass (the report is as of the event before
it) - a definition that is not there, or one that does not read with why it does not (`OrchestrationStore.ReadDefinitionOrWhy`; no
critical path is named). Its sections are the run (its sessions, its wall time, its active
time - the union of every attempt's runs, two steps at once counted once - its pauses between sessions, each from a
session's end - its last record, or where a crash ended it and left none, its last event - to the next session's own
first event, whatever its kind, by the session each event names (`FlowRunReport.PausedSecondsOf`, `FlowEvent.Session`: a
resume writes what its start took up before it records that it began, its held writes stamped as the hold is made, and
what is written after a session's end and before the next's - an answer its last poll takes - is the ended session's and
ends no pause; an older build's events, which name no session, are read as that build's were - from a session's last
record to the next event, and after a crash to the next session's record of its beginning), its waits for a
person, each question's to its first answer or, still open, to the last record, and its budget), the totals (tokens by
kind, the cache's share of input, the dollars grouped - `dollarsBy`, by the model that served each part of each attempt
and each advice by its advisor's (by step, the run's own question's under `run`), or by provider, step, agent or type - the retries and the fallbacks), one row
per step (its state, attempts, waits by cause - a wait on the machine's dispatch queue naming the class of it and each
tenant waited behind, joined over the whole wait, so a reader can tell its own run's units from another repository's -
run time, model, tokens, dollars, exit, error, handler and why it did
not run), the critical path (the longest road through the run's instances, each read as its declaration through
`FlowInstanceId` and linked from the latest visit of each instance its declaration names in its own scope, a group as
every instance inside it, the first in a scope from what its group came after, the first of an iteration from the
iteration before it, a visit after the first from what sent it back, a handler from what raised it - walked once in
the order of its links, each weighed by its runs and its waits for room, never a person's wait or a pause - what a
faster run must shorten), the failed attempts (each with its cause, the exception it threw with its stack and causes,
its digest's first error and the question its ending raised - each the attempt's own, read from its measure entry,
never the last attempt's), the questions people answered with their waits and recommendations, the convergence
(classes closed, each item's counts, classes reopened, hotspots, the issues carried to a later round, fixed there or
left, what loops left) and the signals a reader starts from - the slowest and most
expensive steps, the most retried, every fallback, the longest wait for a person, queue waits past a share of a step's
own time, a cache share under its bound on an attempt whose input reaches past it, a step that read past the depth of
one graph answer (`graphPageDepth`, which says a query was too wide), output a digest held that no
parser read, a review at its bound, a class reopened twice (by agent and class), a hotspot, spend that could not be
counted - each naming its steps and its numbers, their thresholds keys of `defaults.report` read by one owner
(`FlowReportThresholds.Of`) for every report of the run. The session's end writes this same report
(`FlowReports.Write` keeps its place; `report.json` is the document with the session's own members - its line, its
code, its end and its handoffs - beside it, `report.md` its sections with the session's own words at its head and its
questions, updates, handoffs and what is left for a person said in full - each open question with its recommendation
and its next step, by the one rule of it over what the run's engine is doing (`FlowAnswerRules.NextStepOf`, worded once
by `FlowAnswerRules.NextStepSaid` for the report, the status and every refusal of an answer alike):
`answer-orchestrator <run> <answer> --question <id>` where it owes nothing; where it still owes the recommendation it is
answered with (`FlowAnswerRules.OwesRecommendation`) - none sought yet, one sought, or one deferred - with no engine
running the run or a gone one, `resume-orchestrator <run>`, which seeks it first, for no advisor seeks one between
sessions and the answer command refuses any answer but `abort` until then; with a live engine whose advisor seeks it now
(`sought`), a running one, which seeks it as it raises the question, or a starting one (`FlowEngineState.Starting`),
which seeks every recommendation the run owes whatever the session before left the question saying, the answer, taken
at once - one handed over as the start begins, once the start has sought it - and ending the asking - never the resume,
which a live owner refuses, nor a stop, which would end the advice for the next resume to pay for again;
with a live engine pausing or recording what its complete pause left running - or running, the recommendation deferred,
which only a pause asked does - the pause's advice, the answer given then; and with a live engine that is stopping
(`FlowEngineState.Stopping`) the resume once the engine has gone, for a stop starts no advice - `abort` taken now
wherever one is owed. The report a session's end writes reads no engine (its source's `Engine` none), for that session
is leaving the run; `read-orchestrator-report` and `analyze-orchestrator-report` read it as they read the records
(`OrchestratorService.EngineOf`, in `FlowService.SourceOf`), so the same records give the same bytes while the engine
does the same), and `read-orchestrator-report <run>`
answers it any time - reads only, its `--json` the code, the line and the report on every exit (the report null where
the read stopped early), with `--steps` keeping the rows to named instances (one the run does not hold refused,
named), `--by` regrouping the dollars in every form and `--top` bounding the signal lists.

`analyze-orchestrator-report <run>` has one agent read that report and bring its pain points, only where a person
calls for it. The analyst (`report-analyst`, its agent, prompt and schema the build's own) and the reporter are one
runner (`RecordsAgentRunner`), given each its agent, its prompt, its schema, its record directory and what its answer
is held to beyond the schema: a reason step that only reads, narrowed to the run's directory, tried again where its
agent fails as the run's reasoning steps are (`WorkflowDefinition.RetriesOf`, the workflow's `backoffSeconds`), its
cost the person's. The analyst's answer is held to the report by the structured-output gate itself
(`AgentOutput.Holds`, `FlowAnalysisEvidence.Problems`), asked only of an answer the schema holds and sent back in the
analyst's own conversation under the schema's one count of repairs - never a run asked anew: each citation names a
section of the report (the schema's enum), the row by its `id`, the member by its path and the value the report holds
there, read by its JSON kind - a number for its value, a text and a truth word for word - each step a point names is a
row of the report's steps, and no member of the analysis but its recommendation states a number of its own: the
figures of its summary, titles, causes, impacts and what it noted are its citations, the report's own, and its
impacts', written by the tool. An impact - the time and dollars it cost - is a template: every figure it
states is a placeholder naming one of its pain point's citations by its place in the evidence, `{1}` the first, and
once the gate holds the answer the tool writes each as the cited value with the unit the report holds that member in,
as the report itself writes it (`FlowAnalysisEvidence.Rendered`, `FlowRunReport.SaidIn`, which says a value by the
report's own forms: `412.3 s`, `90.0 minutes`, `0.0200 USD`, `28.0%`, `180000 tokens`), so no figure is ever written
bare for a word beside it to claim: any other count with what it counts (`2 tries`, `1 session`), a number that is no
amount after its label (`exit 20`, `attempt 2`), and a failed attempt's exception and first error each number after its
own path (`firstError line 3`). One owner holds the unit of every number the cited sections hold, beside the builder
that writes them: `FlowRunReport.Units`, keyed by the member's path (`theRun.wallSeconds`, `theRun.budget.minutes`,
`steps[].usd`, `steps[].tries`, `totals.graph.calls`; an entry of an object covering every number inside it but where
one of its own says otherwise, an entry of a text the unit of the one number it holds whole, as a step's `ran` in
seconds), its every count's noun and every label pinned, and held to every number the builder writes by
`FlowRunReportTests`. A placeholder names a citation that holds a number the report measures - a number, or a text
that is one number whole, of a member the table gives a unit - so one past its evidence (`{3}` beside two citations),
`{0}`, and one that names a text of words are refused; and it stands apart: a letter, a number, a currency's sign, `%`
or another placeholder - whose figure would run into its own - touching it on either side, or a sign before it
(`${1}`, `{1}h`, `{1}k`, `{1}%`, `{1}{2}`, `-{1}`), is refused, only what touches it read. A digit anywhere else is a
number of its own and refused, once for each word it stands in, whatever wraps it or joins it (`60`, `3600s`,
`q1:3600s`, `(20)`, `$0.02`, `½`, `{1}0`), in the impact and as much in the summary, each pain point's title and
cause, and each thing noted and why, which hold no placeholder - but inside an id. The ids are built once for each
check, by one owner (`FlowAnalysisEvidence`'s `Names`), and are the words that start with a letter and hold a digit
among: a row's id, a name the id is made of as the row's own members hold it (a hotspot's item and path), a section's
or a member's name; every word of the report's texts (`WordsIn`) - each run of a text between white space, whole
(`Sizes/ParserTest.ReadsItsForm/1`, `src/3rdparty/zlib/inflate.c`, `C++20`), and each piece of such a run between the
characters no id is written with, all but a letter, a digit, a mark, `_`, `-`, `.`, `@`, `#`, `[` and `]` (a quote, a
parenthesis, a colon, a slash, a backslash, a plus, a comma), each read from its first letter or digit to its last, or
to a `]` closing a `[` it holds (`Inner`), so a failed attempt's `src/Parser2.cs(12,5): error CS0246` holds
`Parser2.cs` and `CS0246`, a signal's `leg 'win-arm64'` and `[win-arm64]` hold `win-arm64` and a fallback's
`moved from glm-4.6.` holds `glm-4.6`; and the paths the citations write (`c@1.exit`): any citation's in the summary
and the noted, which belong to no pain point, and the pain point's own in its title, cause and impact. A word of the
analysis - its run between white space - is read whole first, its ends read off the same way, and is an id where one
is it whole, written as the report wrote it (`_C++20_`, `**C++20**`); else it is read through, a name in it an id
where it stands whole - no letter, digit, mark or underscore joining it, nor a hyphen, a point or a comma with a
letter or a digit beyond - so `c@1`, `slowestStep#2` and a step named `build2` or `windows-2022` are written as the
report names them while `c@2`, `build3` or `build2-fast` the report holds nowhere are refused, and a word that starts
with a digit - a time, a date, a version, whatever text of the report holds it - is never one. The recommendation is
not read: it states the values it proposes - a configuration key's or a workflow key's exact text - and is never a
measurement. No word of the analysis is read for a unit or a currency: the figure and its unit are the tool's, so its
checked members cannot invent a measurement by how they write one. `analysis.json` keeps each impact as the tool wrote
it and, beside it, its template (`impactTemplate`); `analysis.md`, the text and `--json` say the written one, and an
answer the report does not hold is no analysis - the run's spend still said and kept.
Every rule a text must keep is the schema's (a pattern for every text, an enum for every closed list), and a run with
nothing to change is analysed as one, no pain point named. What a run of the analyst leaves is kept under
`analysis/<stamp>/` whatever it answered -

read of the steps in the order the run made them - which joins it, `FlowUpdateGates.PendingRound`, and once that check

a definition whose `amend` names no such change. The command records nothing for a change it refuses; the engine
records an amendment handed over through the inbox, or a queued change it can no longer take at its turn, `refused`
with why, under its own id. The report lists every update, and `list-orchestrator` says where each stands.
The planning of a plan update: where the run has begun the scope its plan updates are planned in
(the group its `amend.step` is directly in), a taken change is not refused but planned - the step the block names is
raised by the update alone as a handler is raised by an ending (`FlowCoordinator.RaisePlanner`: a new visit of it in
the newest instance of that scope, `FlowInstance.RaisedByUpdate` in its record, a group around it that had ended in
progress again, and every `repeat` around it counting its own bound from the iteration the update is planned in -
`FlowLoopCount`, in the loop's own record: the iterations from that one, and those granted past the bound since - an
iteration an update added before the count began, and a later update took back, left out no more,
`FlowLoopCount.AddedBy` - `FlowLoopCount.Made` and `Given` the one count the engine, the run's facts and the gates read, so the planning of a
late update in a long run is held to the loop's own bound from where it begins, never refused by the iterations the
plan spent before it, the bound's question saying what it counted since that update), never drawn by the ordinary
schedule (`FlowCoordinator.Instantiate`), and admitted ahead of
everything else (`AdmissionWalk`, which walks every other waiting step in the order it first became ready - the pass
that drew it, `FlowInstance.DrawnIn` in the run's own order, never a clock - the fixed order breaking ties among what
one pass freed: a step blocked on a claim reserves it, so a fold or an
agent's making waiting behind readers is never overtaken by a reader that became ready after it - a busy run's
pre-existing triages once starved a recovery's remedy that way) - while the run is held (`FlowCoordinator.HoldOf`: nothing starts outside that
scope, a held step reserving no claim, what is in flight untouched, no next iteration of a loop outside it, no
redirect made outside it), `flow.json` saying `hold {update, at}` (`FlowHoldRecord`). The step's `amend.then` is
followed when it is done - the redirect's machinery inside that scope (`FlowCoordinator.SettleUpdates` ->
`DecideRedirectOf`), a question open on a step it resets withdrawn - and once that scope has come to rest (the step
ended, what `then` set going ended - never a step of it left of the run, one a pause or a stop stopped among them, which
runs again at the resume (`FlowInstance.IsLeft`) - and a `repeat` it is in has ended its iteration) the updated plan
stands: the update is `done`, the hold ends, and the steps that start from here on resolve every name anew. A failed planning
step is decided by its own handlers and `onFailure` as any step: `stop` ends the run, `pause` asks, `continue` gives
the update up - `failed`, nothing placed, nobody told, the hold ended, the run going on with the plan as it was, the
entry saying the request or the answer is recorded and no plan holds it. A plan the check `then` names refuses stands
only once a later iteration of the loop around the planning passes one (`FlowCoordinator.TheThenRefuses`); where
nothing around the planning plans it again - the loop accepted at its bound as it stood, or no loop there is - the
update is given up alike, its entry saying why (`FlowCoordinator.PlansNoMore`), and the run is never held for ever
on a plan that cannot stand. The prompts of the planning step and of its
scope read the update (`{update.cause}`, `{update.since}` and `{update.work}`, `FlowCoordinator.UpdateValues`) -
outside an update each is a sentence that says none is under way. Updates are taken one at a time: one that arrives
while another is under way is `queued` behind it and taken when that one is done, in the order given
(`FlowCoordinator.TakeQueuedUpdates`, the one owner of taking what is queued, which settles each queued entry it meets -
taken, or `refused` with why), and a changed answer queued behind an update is applied when its turn comes. A planning
step declared in the same iteration of a `repeat` as the work-item group it plans is no circular wait: the group the
hold keeps open is no work that iteration waits on to come to rest (`FlowCoordinator.HeldOpenForTheUpdate`). The
whole of it is across a crash and a safe pause: the hold and the raised visit are read back from the run's records at
the resume, which goes on with the update first.
The pieces of an update are placed once its plan stands: the pieces the `amend.scope` expression reads -
each `{kind, item, for, changed, keep, undo, instead}`, of the kind `added`, `changed`, `removed` or `told` - are placed
by `FlowCoordinator.PlaceThePieces` and kept in the update's entry (`FlowUpdatePiece`: the kind, the work item, where it
was placed, the visit that carries it). An `added` piece makes one more work item of the work-item group (the `forEach`
group `amend.whenAddScope` names a step of), at once where the round is in progress and owed to the check that opens the
round where it has not begun - which checks its own items and the owed ones as one list (`PlanCheckRunner`), its output
`items` that list, so nothing joins a round unchecked. An update done that changes the work updates owe a round whose
opening check has already joined it - that check started, and the work-item group it opens not expanded yet, a step
between them such as a pause over an audit still to end - draws that check again (`FlowCoordinator.CheckAgainWhatWasJoined`,
the redirect machinery from the update's planning step: every step of the check's scope that depends on it drawn
again, a question one of them asks withdrawn), so the round opens with what the updates owe it now - a withdrawn item
never built, a changed one built as its newest piece says, never as the piece it replaced. The entry names the check
(`FlowUpdateEntry.CheckedAgain`, absent from an older entry, which reads as before), a session's start draws it again
from there where a crash came before the drawing was written, and the report says it (`FlowReports.CheckedAgainSaidOf`). A `changed` or a `removed` piece finds the newest instance of the
group whose item has its name: where it waits it is given the piece's item in the place of its own, or - `removed` -
withdrawn before it began; where it has begun - a step of it started, at any depth - it is brought to rest (nothing
more started or drawn in it, what it owed dropped, what is drawn or raised in it since skipped, each reason step in
flight given the handoff turn of a safe pause and stopped, `FlowCoordinator.SettlePiecesEndingAsync`, a runner that
outlives its stop keeping what it claimed until it answers, and a step of it that ends otherwise than done - failed
with a retry left or none, asking, past its time limit, or stopped by a pause or a stop - stopped for the update and
never given a new attempt, `FlowCoordinator.StopForTheUpdate`; each of these reaches every step of a group nested in
the instance, at any depth, by one walk down it, `FlowCoordinator.StepsWithin`, and its counterpart up from a step,
`BeingEndedAround`, and each nested group ends stopped for the update once the instance has come to rest, never done
over work the update takes back) and then visited again, in its place and with its agent - a new
scope of the piece's kind in which the live agent a `create-agent` step made is taken and not made again, made and named
in the piece's entry before the instance brought to rest ends, so a crash between finds it and never makes a second;
where it has ended, one more work item of the group, with new agents. A `removed` piece whose work item no instance
carries needs no step, and withdraws the work an earlier update owes a round that has not opened under that name: each
such piece ends in its own update's entry as withdrawn by this one before it was built
(`FlowCoordinator.WithdrawWhatIsOwed`), so no round builds what the plan took back. One naming an item of the list the
check that opens a round was opening it with (`FlowCoordinator.OpeningUnderWay`), which no instance carries, takes it
out of that list: the piece is owed to that round as a withdrawal (`FlowUpdatePiece.Withdrawal`, absent from an older
piece, which reads as before; `IsWithdrawing`), the check that opens the round, drawn again once the update is done, is
handed its name (`withdrawn`) and drops the item from its own, the group's visit never expands it
(`FlowCoordinator.OpenGroup`, which ends the withdrawal once the round opens without it), and no list an update's pieces
join holds it (`PlanValidator.CheckPieces`: a removed piece's item joins the round only where an instance carries it). What an update did to an instance is in
the instance's own records - ended for the update (`FlowStepRecord.EndedFor`), the piece it carries (`PieceOf`) and the
instance it was visited again in place of (`AgainOf`) - so no session after runs an instance an update ended, a resume
goes on bringing one to rest, and the pieces are placed once from the update's entry however often a crash makes the
engine meet its plan standing, an instance an earlier update visited again among them. A visit an update ended waits on
nothing and is counted ended by the engine and the status alike, by the engine's own rule of what is left
(`FlowInstance.IsLeft`, over `FlowInstance.IsStoppedForAnUpdate`; read by `Unended` and by `FlowStatus.IsLeft`), where one
a pause or a stop stopped is left, to run again at the resume. Every instance of the group is of one kind, and the step
its kind names runs in the place of the one `whenAddScope` names - under its name, with its dependencies and its `when` (`FlowCoordinator.DrawWorkItemPlace`) - the
other two alternatives skipped in its instance, saying why; a read of the add step (`{add.latest}`) or a resume of it
follows whichever ran (`FlowCoordinator.EndedDoneLastOf`, which `<step>.latest` reads for every step that goes on with
another's work: the newest answer among the step and every visit whose `resume`, resolved in its own scope or one
around it as its conversation is, reaches it, directly or through another step that does - wherever that step is
declared, so a builder's rework inside a review loop is among the steps that go on with its implement step). The steps of the group read `{piece.kind}`, `{piece.changed}`, `{piece.keep}`, `{piece.undo}`,
`{piece.instead}` and `{piece.before}` (`FlowCoordinator.PieceValues`, `BeforeOf` - the engine's account, from its own
records, of the instance that carried the item before); in an instance no update made, the kind is `added` and the texts
are empty. `PlanValidator.CheckPieces` checks the pieces with the items where a `validate-plan` step's `scope` names
them - each of the four kinds and its texts, an `added` or `changed` item an item of the plan's list by name and member
for member, no two pieces one work item, a `changed` or `removed` piece naming a work item the plan had, an `added`
one naming none an instance of the work-item group carries - and the items an update places are checked with those of
the round they join as one list. Where the check that opens a round raised the update, that round has not opened and no
instance carries its items - from the second round on a list the self-audit wrote, which no planner did - so the round
the pieces join is the list that check was opening it with, its output's `items` (`FlowCoordinator.OpeningUnderWay`):
the update's checks are handed it under `round`, a piece may change or withdraw any item of it (`known`), and the
planner is shown its items among the run's work (`{update.work}`, `FlowCoordinator.WorkOf`), each as not begun. A
problem two rules find - one pair of items meeting in the plan's list and in that round - is said once. A work item is known by its name across
the run - `ItemInstanceNamed`, its tests' key in `affected-tests.json`, its updates - so the check that opens a round
is handed the names every instance of the group carries (`carried`, read where it starts) and refuses a round's own
item under one of them (`PlanValidator.Check`'s `carried`), an owed item excepted: a changed or a removed piece names
the item it does again or takes back. The rule holds the items the round builds: a round added to a group with no loop
around it carries the owed work alone (`owedAlone`, read where its check starts), and its own items, which the check
reads again from the plan, are those the round before built under those very names, so none of them is refused; a
loop's later round is a visit of its own and builds every item it opens with.
The pieces are told as they are placed: every `told` piece's message is sent through the attempt's own
telling (`FlowTelling`, made where a reason attempt starts and handed to the runner - `ReasonStepRunner` wires its
messages channel and its handoff signal into the agent run) - a reason step in flight that a piece names, by its own
instance or a scope around it, in one message into the conversation it is in, which lands when its calls have
finished and never cuts its turn; a step that waits on a question of its own with the answer; a step that starts or
goes on later in named work in the `<plan-updates>` part of its own prompt (`FlowCoordinator.PlanToldOf`). A reason
step in flight that no piece names is listed as not concerned and a piece naming nothing under way as not delivered
with why (`FlowUpdateEntry.Told`/`NotConcerned`/`NotDelivered`, each telling also in the step's own record,
`FlowStepTold`); a reason step ended in order is told its piece first, as the lead of the handoff question
(`FlowCoordinator.EndedInOrderLead`, the engine waiting for the client's own turn where the telling is live). Where
the round a piece joins has ended, the work is owed to the loop's next iteration (`FlowInstance.OwedIterationBy`,
rebuilt at the resume, by each piece's own state, `FlowUpdatePiece.IsOwed`), which runs whatever its `until` says - a
loop that ended done runs again for it; only where that loop is at its own bound is one iteration
added for the update, and none while the loop's newest iteration is under way with its round still to open, which the
work joins at the check that opens it (`FlowCoordinator.RoundToOpenIn`). With no loop around the work-item group, the piece is owed to a round added to the group
(`FlowCoordinator.AddARoundOwed`): the group is drawn once more as its next visit (`build.items+2`), with the check that
opens its rounds and every step on the dependency path from that check to the group - a pause asked about the check's
problems among them - where each was drawn before the round ended, and every group around it that had ended done in
progress again (`FlowCoordinator.OpenTheRoundAgain`, called again from the entry by a resume that finds the round
not yet drawn); the check is handed the owed work with its own items as one list, and the visit carries the owed work
alone (`FlowCoordinator.OpenGroup`), never the items the round before built. An iteration or a round is added once per
update, at most `amend.maxAddedIterations` over the run, published as an `iterationAdded` event and kept in the entry
(`FlowUpdateEntry.AddedIteration`, said by `FlowReports.IterationSaidOf` as round n of the loop or of the group). One
whose owed work is all withdrawn before it opens is taken back by the update whose placement left it owing nothing
(`FlowCoordinator.TakeBackWhatOwesNothing`), unless another update's work still owes the same loop or round: its entry
says so (`FlowUpdateEntry.AddedWithdrawnBy`, absent from an older entry, which reads as before), and from there it
counts against no bound - `FlowUpdateEntry.StandingIteration` is the one read of what an entry added that stands, taken
by the run's count of iterations given, the gates (`NoRoundMore`, `RoundNotOpened`, `PendingRound`), the grants
(`FlowGrants.AddedTo`) and the status. A loop's added iteration not yet made is given no more (`ExtraIterations`
lowered), so its bound reads as it did and asks its question again where work is owed past it; a round added to a group
with no loop around it is closed again (`FlowCoordinator.CloseTheRoundAgain`): the check drawn for it and every step
between that check and the group end skipped saying why - each drawn visit that had not ended, a question it asked
withdrawn, and each not drawn yet - the group's slot holds its round before, the groups around it made in progress
again end as their members have, and a later update's round drawn again reads that reason to draw them anew; a session's
start takes back and closes from the entries where a crash cut either off. The report and `list-orchestrator` say the
taking back (`FlowReports.TakenBackSaidOf`). A
loop at its bound where the run has been given every iteration allowed asks its bound for the owed work - it reaches
that question whatever its `until` or its `blocking` says, for owed work ends no loop - and each owing entry says so
once the question is asked, or is found standing at a session's start (`FlowCoordinator.LeaveToTheBound`,
`FlowUpdateEntry.AskedAtBound`); the answer decides whether the loop runs on to carry it. What
an update done owes is carried from its entry at every session's start too, so a crash between the update's end and
its carry loses nothing, and an entry that says its carry was made - the iteration or round added, or its loop's bound
asked - is carried no second time, so a loop the bound's answer ended is never run again for it
(`FlowCoordinator.ReopensFor`). Where the group runs no round more - the run has none left to add, or a group around it
ended otherwise than done and draws nothing more (`FlowUpdateGates.NoRoundMore`, the gates' rule) - an update whose
work only an added round would carry is given up with why before anything is placed, its pieces never carried out
(`FlowCoordinator.NoRoundForTheWork`). The report and
`list-orchestrator` say every piece, where it was carried out and how that ended, the iteration or round added, a loop's
bound asked for the work (`FlowReports.AskedAtBoundSaidOf`), and who
was told what, who was not concerned and what was not delivered.
Each step is handed the run it belongs to (`FlowRunPlace`) and what the engine read for it
where it starts (`FlowStepRun.Read`: a plan check's `items` and `scope`, the pull request's base `FlowTemplate` fills for
orient, an anchor check's `rows` or `paths` expression, a fold family step's lists of names - read by `FlowStepKeys.NamesOf` -
a `ci-wait`'s commit where it names none - the one the run last pushed - a commit's `folds`, the instances of the
steps that fold upstream of it) - and a reason step's `prompt` and `resumePrompt` filled around their skills, as
pieces (`FlowStepRun.Prompts`) - the agent it works in (`FlowStepRun.WorksIn`)
or, of `others`, the target whose turn it is (`FlowStepRun.Target`), and its keys' templates filled (`FlowStepTemplates`, the one

`run`, `check-mutations` - share `LegStepRunner`: the use case of each command (`IBuildLegs`, `ITestLegs`,
`IRunnerLegs` - a run that writes the tree in place, by `HarnessConfig.WritingRunners`, the answer the step's claim of
write reads through `ConfiguredRunnerFacts` - and `IMutationLegs`) run in the agent's worktree or the main checkout, its

the tree; each copy made, said where the leg takes its tree after the sync; each leg ended, said by `LegLedger` as its

leg's failing phase log are kept in the step's directory, by the one owner of a step's legs (`FlowStepLegs`), which a
reason step's measure call runs its leg through too. A leg run something other than its legs ended - refused, or
stopped (`FlowStepLegs.EndedOutsideItsLegs`) - ends the step with its own code. The checks that run no legs answer `FlowStepResult.Red` where they found red,
which the coordinator reads by `failOn` as it reads a red leg: `AnchorBalanceStepRunner` and `AnchorCitationsStepRunner`
over the anchor services, held to a step's rows or paths by `AnchorBalanceReport.HeldTo` (each `AnchorFinding` carries
the id of its row, none for a registry as a whole) and `AnchorCitationReport.HeldTo`, their findings the lines the
checks print (`AnchorReports.BalanceFindings`, `AnchorCitationReports.Line`); `CiReadStepRunner` over
`ICiLegsService.CheckAsync`; and `CiWaitStepRunner` over `ICiChecksService`, which reads a commit's check runs and
statuses through `ICiJobSource` until one is red - classified by `ICiLegsService.ClassifyRunAsync`, its job's log read
whole - every one has ended, none appeared, or its time is spent, with `CiConclusions` the one
place that says what a conclusion came to. A failed read of a commit's checks is read again
through `Retrying` for as long as its failure can change - a network failure or a 5xx keeps
waiting, told every five minutes, and a 401 or a 404 ends it at once (`CiChecksService`). A
branch's open pull request is asked of `gh pr list --head <branch>`, its `--limit` doubled until
gh answers fewer than asked, so one among any number is found (`GitPublisher`). Every call of `gh` goes through `GhProcess`: the repository it answers for, never asking
(`UnattendedCommands`, which every git command is started with too), ended at its limit (21) - its caller's, a step's
`timeoutMinutes` (`WorkflowStepTypes.CommandLimitOf`, handed on as `CiLegsRequest.ReadTimeLimit`,
`CiChecksRequest.ReadTimeLimit` and `ICiJobSource.Within`), else `GhProcess.Limit`. The fold family - `FoldStepRunner`, `DeleteAgentStepRunner`, `RefreshStepRunner` and `RebaseStepRunner`, over
`FoldFamilyStepRunner` - calls the verbs' typed use cases and reads their `AgentVerbFacts`, never an exit code:
`FoldStandings.Read` says whether a dry run ends the step, asks or applies; `FlowQuestions.FoldQuestionOf` is the one rule
of the question it raises - `foldConflicts` for conflicting merges alone, `foldOutside` for paths `FoldWithin` finds
outside a fold's `within`, read from the main tree's root, then each consent it lacks, a person's first - with what
it is about (`FlowDryRun.Of`, over `AgentPlanned`), which the runner keeps in the step's `fold.json` (`FlowFoldRecord`) with where its answer will stand; a
consent is given by name only where the dry run made again names exactly that, and one that no longer does is never
passed. A fold's apply, and a deletion's, is held to what its dry run named (`FoldAgentRequest.Expected`,
`DeleteAgentRequest.Expected`, measured again under its hold and compared by `AgentPlanned.DifferenceFrom`) - a
refresh's and a rebase's request carry none - and which steps fold is one rule, `WorkflowStepTypes.Folds`, the
definition's check and the runner alike. `FoldLedger` writes a fold's intent to `folds.json` before the verb is called
and, by the verb under its hold of the tree (`FoldIntent`), `writing` as its write begins and `written` with what it
left once the write is done or has thrown (`FlowFoldLedgerFile`); then, once the verb answered, applied, stopped or

`FoldLedger.Settle` reads nothing of the tree, which a side-task that waited on the apply's hold may have written since.
An apply stopped - which writes nothing once its measure is done, every write after it uncancelled - is settled stopped

step's `fold.json` takes what the apply answered before the ledger's settle, and an apply that threw goes on with its own

(`FoldLedger.Owed`, over the instances the coordinator read where it started - `FlowInstanceId.Precedes`, then

no path to stage the index marks assume-unchanged or skip-worktree checked before anything is
staged; the staged set written to the ledger (`FlowCommitEntry`) before `IGitPublisher` stages it by explicit path and

(`IGitClient.ParentsOfAsync`, `git cat-file commit`, which no graft or shallow boundary stands in for), that commit
alone - a hook could move the branch to a commit of its own, standing on one that carries anything - and what it
changes against that commit the set alone; one that stands elsewhere, took more, or left a path of the set out, is

(`FoldLedger.IgnoredOf`); and a set an attempt before left staged settled first, committed only where the tree holds

checked - `{run.ran}`, `{run.notRun}`, `{run.red}`, and `{carried.*}` of one commit - are `FlowChecks`', over the
step records the coordinator hands it; a check is a type `WorkflowStepTypes.StepType.Checks` marks or an independent
reason step. A red result stands until a later visit or iteration of the same step of the same work item ends green
checking the same (`FlowCheck.Work`): within the recovery, a visit for the same failure or issue, so another issue's
green never hides it from the visit that is to put it right. A deletion run
again whose agent its record says deleted - its ending cut off by a stop's drain, a time limit or a crash - is done
(`FoldFamilyStepRunner.DoneAlreadyAsync`), its output what `fold.json` kept of the apply. A
refresh or a rebase of `others` is one turn for each target (`FlowInstance.Targets`, `FlowTargetRecord`), in

each refused where it is not on the run's branch (`FlowRunPlace.OffItsBranch`):
the push sends the commit the run's commit steps recorded last in its ledger (`OrchestrationStore.ReadFolds`, the last

HEAD names by then, which a hook or a build working in the main checkout's git directory, written whole, could have
moved - to the main checkout's branch on the step's remote, else `FlowCheckout.Remote` - one, which the definition's check
holds every push step that names a remote to - through `IGitPublisher.PushAsync` -
`<sha>:refs/heads/<branch>` with `--porcelain`, never forced, its line read for whether the branch moved; the pull

or opened through `GhProcess` on the repository `GitRemotes.ForgeAddress` reads from the remote's

to the step's directory; `FlowReports.LeftForAPerson` names each pull request the run opened or found, and each path
its folds changed that git ignores, as its commits answered them. Every command a
publishing step runs is one of `PublisherCommands.All`, over `IGitClient.RunWithinAsync` and `GhProcess` - the commit
and the push over `IGitClient.RunWithHooksAsync`, the repository's hooks run inside the isolation their step asked -
given the step's `timeoutMinutes` else the command's own limit. The other step runners - the agents, the rest of the steps over the services the tool already has - are
the next thing the tool grows.

A definition is held to the `config.json` it is checked under as well: a `run` step whose runner -
or a runner its run checks name - says `writesTree` names with `in` the create-agent step whose
worktree it works in, since the run reads its definition in the main tree and folds into it; the
agents a run makes, named `a` and a number that grows to the workflow's `maxInstances`, fit
`worktrees.maxNameLength` where the repository sets one, and the path budget of their worktrees in
every case; and a commit step gives a value for every variable `commit.template`
requires and none for one it does not declare - or, with no template, a `message` and no
`variables`. Within the definition, the `amend` block takes an amended request into a text
`input`, a changed answer (`changedAnswerMinutes`) or both; its `step` is one step, outside every
`forEach` and `always` group, raised by an update alone and going on with the work of a step beside
it; `whenAddScope` names a step declared directly in a `forEach` group - the work-item group - and
`whenChangeScope` and `whenRemoveScope` that step or alternatives of its type beside it, which say
no wiring of their own and which no other step names; and the work-item group expands from the
`items` of a `validate-plan` step it waits for. A step that names a create-agent step with `in` or
`of` waits for it - through its own `dependsOn`, a group's around it, a handler's source or the step
it is an alternative to, a step inside an alternative group among them (`FlowGraph.Waits`) - since it starts once the
agent is made; where that step ended otherwise than done - skipped, passed over, failed under `always` or handled - the
coordinator does not run it (`FlowNotRunCause.AgentNotMade`), saying the agent it works in was never made, and the agent
it works on is kept on its instance (`FlowInstance.WorksIn`) from its start, so a deletion's record names the agent it
deleted after its create-agent made another. A template is
read by the configuration's one brace grammar (`FlowTemplate.Pieces`): `{{` and `}}` are braces,
`${...}` is left as written, and a placeholder that names nothing is refused. `piece` is read only in the work-item group, and what only a
prompt reads - `recommendations`, `question`, `status`, `update`, a skill - by no step's own key.
What only a prompt reads stands where its agent is asked it: `{recommendations}` in a reason step's
prompt and the advisor's - the bar the repository wrote, read live each time it is given - `{question.*}` in the advisor's alone, `{status.*}` in the reporter's two -
`{status.question}` in its `askPrompt` alone - `{update.*}` in the prompts of the step that plans an
update and of the steps of its scope, and `{piece.*}` in a step of the work-item group; the
advisor's and the reporter's prompts are read too, and read no step by name, and a pull request's
`body`, which the engine fills and no agent reads, reads what a template key reads and no skill.
A question gives only the texts the engine names (`step`, `kind`, `problem`, `answers`, `record`),
and so do the status (`facts`, `question`, `records`), a plan update (`cause`, `since`, `work`) and
a piece (`kind`, `changed`, `keep`, `undo`, `instead`, `cause`, `before`) - each list kept once, in
`WorkflowExpressions` beside the run's own texts, and read by the typing; the bar is one text, and so
is each run fact (`WorkflowExpressions.RunFacts`), which a template reads and an expression does not.
A `pushCheckpoints` with no push step that is a checkpoint, two handlers one ending raises that
both name a `then`, a fallback that is its agent's own model or is named twice, a gathered name
given twice, named for an engine's fact or for a member, `times` or `then` beside a `pause`
answer, and a workflow that names no advisor (V43) are each refused.

`export-workflow <workflow> --to <dir>` is a use case of Core (`WorkflowExportService`): it copies
a workflow - its yml and every file it names, the one list `validate-workflow` and `init` read
(`WorkflowFiles`), and no other - into `<dir>/<workflow>/`, a folder of its own that must not be
there (13 where it is). A declared workflow is exported once its check holds (12 where it does
not), from the definition and the directory that check found, so what is copied is what was
checked, each file byte for byte and proved where it lands (`VerifiedFileCopy`); with `--shipped`
it is the implementation workflow as this build ships it, held to `WorkflowValidator`'s rules as for a
configuration with no `commit.template`, written as
`init` writes it. The yml is written last, and a file that cannot be written takes back what was
written before it, with every folder the export made, so a folder with part of a workflow in it is never
left behind - or the refusal says why it could not be taken back. A used workflow's files are placed
where it sits under the workflow's folder (`WorkflowFiles.PlaceOf`, the one placing init and the
build's own set read too), never by how a use spelt it, so a hidden folder keeps its dot; a use of a
workflow outside the folder, or of a remote one, is refused (13) with nothing written, for the
folder alone would name a workflow it has not got - the refusal names each, a remote one with the
`--from` that vendors it.

### Running a workflow

A run is an orchestrator the engine drives (`FlowService`, a use case of Core; the CLI only wires
it). `run-orchestrator <workflow>` checks the definition as `validate-workflow` does (12 where it
does not hold) - read from the definition tree, the main checkout, whichever tree the command was
typed in, as every later session of the run reads it - reads `--input` - `name=@<file>` through `IFileSystem`, relative to `--directory`,
a missing file a usage error - and checks the inputs against the definition before anything is
made, by the one owner of what an input takes (`FlowInputs.Resolve`, which the engine holds its run
to as well); then, inside the repository's one section (`FlowSessions.AcrossRuns`), it refuses another
unfinished run with work in the tree - a run whose agent's record cannot be read counts as one,
said - chooses the name (`r<N>`, one more than the highest there; a name `--run` gives is held to
`worktrees.maxNameLength` where the repository sets one and refused where a record or anything else is there), holds the start
to the path budget of its agents' worktrees - what each worktree's own check counts below it
(`WorktreeRoom`), with the copies and workers its leg steps keep inside them (`FlowRunPaths`) - opens the file each of
the run's own inputs of the kind `file` names where its value, given or its default, is not empty - a path from the
main checkout's root or an absolute one inside it, read from the main checkout as it stands, committed or not, and
decided as an agent's read of it is, since every agent of the run reads the copy - on the ground the one builder of an
agent's ground builds for it (`AgentStepGround.OfFileInputs`: an agent's read of the main checkout under the
configuration the run starts under, never a ground built by hand beside it): held to the main checkout by where it
leads, every link on its way followed - the file's own and a directory's above it (`ConfinedPaths`) - kept from every
place no agent's read reaches - every credential slot of the tool, every Claude Code directory and every place the user
keeps credentials in, `agentPolicy.hiddenPlaces` among them - and from every read `agentPolicy.restrictions` refuse
(`AgentPolicy`), and read through the file as it
was opened, where it stands decided again before a byte passes (`AgentFiles.OpenDecided`), so a link put on its way
since reaches nothing; anything else refused (13), naming the input and the path, no run started
(`FlowInputs.OpenFiles`) - makes the run's directory and copies each file into it, `inputs/<input>/<the file's name>`
(`OrchestratorLayout.InputCopy`), before it makes the run's record, its status and its owner
(`.orchestrators/<run>.owner.json`), and leaves the section. The file's bytes are first read there: a place of the
run or a copy that cannot be made - a file on a share gone, a locked range, a full disk - takes back what the start had
made of the run, or says what it could not, and refuses the start (13), naming the input and why and that no run was
started (`FlowInputFiles.Keep`, `FlowSessions.CreateAsync`), so no directory is left holding no run's record, which a
start of that name would be refused over. What a step reads for such an input - `{input.<name>}`
in every prompt and every expression, and a pull request's base - is the copy's full path (`FlowInputs.AsRead`, the
one owner of what a step reads for an input, which every session hands the engine), so every step of every session,
a resume's included, reads the file the run was started with, whatever the person did to it since; the run's records
keep the value as it was given. That the run keeps its copies is a fact of its own, recorded as it is made
(`FlowRunContext.InputCopies`, `flow.json`'s `inputCopies`) and read back by every session: a run an older build made
kept none and its `flow.json` says nothing of them, so its steps read each file input as it was given, as that build
handed it to them, never the path of a copy that was never made. Every agent of the run reads the run's `inputs/` as a root of its own
(`AgentStepGround`): an untracked or uncommitted file is in no agent's tree - a write agent's worktree is cut from the
run's start commit, and an agent that only reads has its tree brought to the main checkout's HEAD - and reaches both
alike. A used workflow's file input is no such thing: it names a file of that workflow's own directory, which the
definition's check reads. A session of a run already made -
`resume-orchestrator`, or `answer-orchestrator` where no engine runs the run - first sweeps what a
killed engine's steps left running (`ChildSessions`), refuses a definition the repository's entry
in the main checkout no longer says - a definition is changed only by what it says, so what each says is compared,
both as this build reads them and digested by this build's one serializer (`FlowResume.RefuseAChangedDefinition`
over `FlowRunContext.DigestOf`): the entry the definition's check makes now, and the run's `definition.json` as this
build reads a frozen one (`FrozenDefinition`), whichever build froze it - each member that may be null and that an
earlier release left out, as it left out every null and had none of the members added since, read as null, and each
member a new definition is refused for naming, which an earlier release's may hold (`FrozenDefinition.Retired`: the
advisor's `kinds`, the codebase graph's `maxFileBytes`), read in its shape and ignored, and each member written in a
shape this build changed (`FrozenDefinition.Reshaped`: a sweep's `arms`, a test step's `filter`) held to the shape that
release wrote it in and read as what this build's parser makes of the same words - a sweep's list of arm ids, written
empty on every step that named none, read as no arms, every arm swept, and the ids it listed as the list they are; a
filter written as one text read as the expression that scalar is - so it says what the unchanged entry does, and
written again is in this build's shape alone. Never against the digest
`flow.json` holds (`definitionDigest`, written as the run began and kept as the record of what it began with), which
the build that began it made of the same words written its own way; never by where the file was read from; and never
by a use's fingerprint, the digest that build made of the called file, which no frozen definition holds to make
again - what the use brings the run, its steps and every part of it carried, is in the definition and compared there
(`FlowResume.Said`). So a checkout that moved, a command typed in another tree, or a run an earlier release began is no
change - and claims the run inside the same section: refused by
name where the run was deleted since, refused while a live engine owns it, a dead owner reclaimed
and said, a request no engine took removed - one that cannot be read refuses the session, and the
claim just made is let go first, so no owner is left behind by a session that never began. Two starts,
or two sessions of one run, can never both
pass; and `delete-orchestrator` decides and removes inside that section too, taken before the
orchestrator's own, so no claim comes between its look at the owner and its removal of the run.

The run's records are written in one order at every change - a step's own files (its `handoff.md`
where it handed off, its `output.json`, then the `step.json` that names them - a refresh's or a rebase's of `others`
with each target and where it stands; a reason step's `policy.json`, written as the step starts: the
agents' configuration is read when each step starts, as its prompts are, so an edit of `config.json` -
a side-task's among them - reaches the steps that start after it and never one under way, and each
keeps the policy it started under - the ground as resolved, the web search it asks, what it runs on
with the key's name alone; and, where its `writes` narrow its worktree, its `untracked-at-start.jsonl`,
written once, as it first starts, and read by every later start: its head, then each path the worktree
held untracked, one to a line), then `flow.json` (the
truth a resume reads), `workflow.json`, `pre-existing-issues.json` where the change listed one, and last the event
in `events.jsonl` - each naming the run's session it belongs to (`session`, from 1, one more for each session the run's
engines drive: what a session's start writes, held or before the session is driven, is that session's, and what is
written after a session's end and before the next's the ended one's; the log's opening reads the sessions it tells of,
the highest any event names and no fewer than the beginnings it records, `FlowEventLog.Sessions`; an older build's events
name none) - each line handed to the system whole and in order as it is written and put on the disk once per
pass of the engine's loop - as the pass ends, before the loop waits on anything, and as the session ends, in order or by
its cancellation token (`IFlowRecords.Flush`) - so an end of the engine's process loses no line, and a power loss what the last pass had not
put on the disk, never a line before it: writes never put on the disk reach it in any order, so the log can come back
with the pass's later lines and its size and NULs where an earlier page of the pass never landed, and as no line holds a
NUL - each is JSON - the log's opening takes back from its first NUL to its end (`AppendLog.Open`, `batched`) and its
reader sets aside the first line that holds one with every line after it, said. That holds where the file system shows a
byte it never wrote as NUL, as ext4's ordered and journalled modes, XFS, Btrfs, APFS and NTFS do; one that can show a
block's old bytes instead (ext4's writeback mode) can leave a line of the last pass's that reads as no event, refused by
its number. The log's close never throws a flush's failure over the failure a session leaves by: the records say it as a
warning (`FlowRunRecords.Dispose`), and a session that ends in order heard it at its last pass's flush. Each record is
read back strictly: a value the engine does not name, a nested record that
does not hold, a time in any but the one form (`yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss`, UTC; one not yet come is
written `null`), a log line out of sequence or corrupt is refused by its number, and only a torn last
line, or the lines from the first that holds a NUL, are set aside, said - by the report's notes, and as a warning by the
session that opens the log for append and takes them back (`FlowEventLog.SetAside`). A resume reconciles `flow.json` against every step's own record, taking the
step's own whole wherever there is one - so what changes a step's measure that no stream gives back, an advice taken and
a turn of an attempt that is over, is written to the step's own record as it is charged - keeping the index's order and adopting what only a step's
directory holds at the end. The graph is rebuilt in that order, never sorted again - `build+10` after
`build+2`, `rounds#10` after `rounds#2`, a loop's later visit (`rounds+2`) and its items as their own,
a block's members whatever the block ended, the agents the run holds open (each a create-agent step
made, held by its newest visit, that no deletion deleted) - and a record whose scope never comes, or
whose state the engine does not name, is refused rather than taken for one that runs again. It takes back a handoff a
crash left beside its record - the engine's where its first line says so and why, as the engine
writes every handoff of its own (`FlowHandoff.ByEngine`, read back by `FlowHandoffRecord.Of`), the
agent's otherwise - reads each handoff back as it was handed, and refuses - naming the file - a record
that names a handoff that is gone, and a missing `questions.json`, `pre-existing-issues.json` or
`affected-tests.json`, never made again empty. A handoff an attempt still held when it was cut off - an agent's account no
prompt holds yet, stopped or running - is given to the next attempt; neither a later pause whose turn
gives none nor the resume writes the engine's over it.

The session then goes on from those records alone, where the run stood, whatever ended the last one
and whichever engine wrote them. Every question in `questions.json` comes back with every answer it
was given - the next id after the highest of any state, and what a configuration's counted answers
spent and every `more` a bound was granted counted again from the answers - and a step waits on each
one still open. What was running or stopped runs again as a new attempt, and so does a failure that
ended the run (its record's `failure` is `endedRun`) save one an answer `fail` ended, which stands and
keeps the run stopped; what that stop left NotRun (`notRunCause` `RunEnded`, or `DependencyFailed`
where the failure no longer blocks it) is drawn again under the same id, and a group stands open
over such a member, never ended done over it. What the run owed is made before anything runs: a
failure recorded `owed` - one that ended while a pause recorded what it left running, or before what
decides it was written - an ending whose handlers its record holds `owed`, issues a step's record
holds owed their triage (`issuesOwed`), an issue a triage answered fix for whose recovery was never
raised, and every redirect in `flow.json`'s `redirects`, each in its turn - a pause and a hard stop
alike leave a redirect owed, never making it, for the resume makes it once what they stopped stands
to be withdrawn. A triage's answer is
listed and counted before its end is recorded, so the end's one write carries the run's file of
issues (`FlowSnapshot.Issues`) in the one order; a crash before that file leaves the end written, and
the resume lists the issue from the triage's answer - once, for one the list already holds the same in
all but its id and time is not listed again. A change's snapshot holds the run by value - what was spent
(`FlowBudgetSpent.Recorded`) and the pause (`FlowPauseState.Recorded`) taken as they stood, never the engine's own
objects - so a write a session's start holds, made once the session goes on, says the run as it stood when the change
was taken, never paired with a grant or a mark that came since. Each record is written before what follows from it - a question before the record of the
step that waits on it, an answer before what it changes, a visit with what raised it, a handler's raise in its source's
record before the handler's visit, so no record holds a raise owed beside the visit it made (`FlowInstance.RaisesOwed`:
a crash between the two leaves the raise said and no visit of it, which the next session makes, and a record an older
build left holding a raise owed beside its visit is read raised, its visit that raise), a failure
owed until it is decided, every visit a redirect leaves marked `leftBy` before the redirect leaves
the run's records, and a handler a redirect leaves before it ended marked `left` in its source's
record, for it took nothing: the ending it was raised for is abandoned, settled by none of its handlers
and never rebuilt by a resume - so a crash between any two writes leaves records the next session completes: an
answer written is carried out once, a configured answer never written is given, a handler is never
raised twice, and an ending whose handlers all ended is settled. An ending the records leave waiting is rebuilt as its
raise made it, from its source's record: the visit of each handler that record holds `raised`, in the order the
workflow declares them (`FlowCoordinator.EndingOf`) - never a triage of an issue the source reported nor a visit of the
recovery, which name the source as what raised them too - so what depends on the source waits for its handlers alone,
as it does within a session, and the source's record names only them as the ending settles. A session is never said done over a
step that never ended, nor one its scope never drew, and a run is never said done - by a session, or by the engine that
takes it up before its session - over a step a pause or a stop stopped, which runs again at the resume, nor over a
failure or a handler's raise owed to the next session. What the session's start writes is held, in the
order made and each with the run as it stood, until it is known the session goes on: a resume beside
an open question is refused only where nothing can run until a question is answered, and then it has
written nothing - no event, no attempt, no state; a session an answer began, one whose budget
question is open, and one beside a question still owing its recommendation - deferred by a stop or by a
pause a stop cut short, left sought by a crash, or never sought in a questions file an earlier build wrote
(`FlowCoordinator.OwesAdvice`), which `SeekOwedAdvice` seeks - are never refused, and end paused on the
question left. A stop asked between
sessions - `abort` answered with no engine running the run - ends the session it begins where the run
stands, stopped, as a stop in a session ends it: nothing it found stopped runs again or is given the
