engine's handoff in place of its own, nothing owed is made and nothing starts; the session after it
goes on with all of it.

Each session ends however it ends with the run's report (`report.md`, `report.json`), its owner
released in a `finally`, its line in the run's log, and every record it wrote named in text and in
`--json` (`FlowRunResult`, `FlowReports.Document`): `0` done, `20` failed - `21` where every failure
that ended it was incomplete after its retries (`FlowRetry.RunsAgain`, read from each step's record:
its code, and the `cause` it keeps where the code cannot say it, `LockHeld` for a refusal whose only
obstacle was a held lock) - `1` paused on a question,
the budget's among them, and `130` at a safe pause or a stop. A refusal met inside a session is
answered as a refusal, naming the records as they stand. Another terminal reaches the engine
through two files its poller reads at once and every 2 s: `stop.json` (`pause-orchestrator`, which
waits until the pause is complete; `stop-orchestrator`, which waits while the engine runs, told
every 5 minutes, its own Ctrl+C ending the wait with the stop left asked) and `inbox.json`
(`answer-orchestrator` to a running engine, each answer under an id of its own). The poller never
waits on what it hands the engine; what it cannot read is said once and read again, anything else
asks the run to pause; a last poll at the session's end takes what came late - a pause or a stop
handed to the engine as every poll hands one (`FlowService.HandOnWhatIsAsked`), never only removed,
so where an answer that poll takes drives the run on, that drive's start takes it as it begins, and
where none does it ends with the session - and the next session takes what is left. The engine takes an answer offered before a session begins at its start, before
anything is admitted - so a resume is never refused over the question it settles - and hands one left
unread as its session ends back cancelled, never refused, so it stays in the inbox for whoever takes it
next; what a step spent that came late is counted. Every answer handed over is weighed by one owner
(`FlowCoordinator.AnswerHandedOver`), whether a session's loop or the inbox taken between two drives
meets it, and what became of it is written into `questions.json` under its inbox entry's id before
anything else is said of it: an answer taken carries the id in who gave it (`by.inbox`), and one the
run does not take - its question no longer open, its question still owing its recommendation with no advisor
seeking it (`FlowAnswerRules.Unrecommended`), or it changes an answer already given - is kept in
the file's `refused` list, then recorded as an `answer` event naming why. An answer a session weighed
leaves the inbox only once what became of it is written: one weighed at a session's start, whose writes
are held until it is known the session goes on, is settled when they are made, and handed back - left in
the inbox, and said - where they never are, a refused resume writing nothing; so nothing empties from
the inbox an answer the run's records do not hold. One that reaches a start that goes on - the command's own entry, one
a past engine left in the inbox, one handed over before the first admit - answering a question owing the recommendation
the start seeks, is weighed once that advice is under way (`FlowCoordinator.WeighHandedOver`), so it is taken and ends
the asking; only a start that seeks none for it - a stop asked as it began, after which it seeks none, or a pause, which
defers it - refuses it, naming the resume once the engine has gone or the pause once it is complete. Whether the start
takes such an answer is one rule (`FlowCoordinator.StartTakesAnswers`), which also decides whether the start's writes
say `starting` - each as it is made, so a write the start held from before a stop or a pause was asked of it says it is
not once the hold is made (`FlowCoordinator.AsWritten`) - and a stop or a pause asked of a start under way, or while the
run's state may still say `starting`, writes what the start stands on over `flow.json` at once, outside the hold - the
stop applied or the pause asked, the questions the past session left sought deferred - (`FlowStartsStanding`,
`FlowCoordinator.TakeTheStartsStanding`, `IFlowRecords.Stand`, through `OrchestrationStore.Rewrite` and
`OrchestrationStore.RewriteFlowQuestions`, the one read and write of a part of each, which the release's taking back of
the mark uses too), inside the one section every write of the run's records is made in, so it never meets one half
made: the run's state never says `starting` once the start no longer takes such an answer, and says the step its
refusal names, though the start writes nothing else until its hold is made. What became of a waiting answer is
kept with what it is settled with, its why among it (`FlowWeighed`),
and said once the start has weighed it: `answer-orchestrator`'s own answer so refused is the command's refusal (13) with
the run's why, read from `questions.json` under its entry's id - whatever the session it began went on to do, its own
end, line and code, said after it and kept beside the command's in `--json`'s `session` (`FlowRunResult.Session`) - by
the one rule an answer the command handed over is answered by whichever session weighed it (`FlowService.OwnRefused`),
and an inbox entry's line says it was taken once its recommendation was sought, or why not. What became of what was
handed to a session is said by one owner on every exit of it, its end in order and a refusal met inside it alike
(`FlowService.SayWhatWasHandedOver`), the command's own answer read from what the run's records hold under its entry's
id and otherwise from what the session settled it with, which it keeps past the entry's leaving the inbox
(`Offered.Weighed`) - never from what it still offers, which forgets an entry as the inbox lets it go: refused, the
command's refusal as above; taken, said so; never weighed or handed back, said to stay in the inbox.
Once settled it is counted, and leaves the inbox
once the file lets it go: a removal that fails is tried again at the next poll or drive's end, and one
the inbox still holds as the session ends - the removal failed to the last, or a crash came between the
take and the removal - is settled by the run's records, so a later session that meets the entry only
empties it from the inbox: no answer is weighed, offered or taken twice. `answer-orchestrator`, having
handed an answer to a running engine, waits on the service's clock - for as long as that engine
lives, told every 5 minutes - for
what `questions.json` records under its entry's id: taken, it says so; refused, it answers the run's
refusal (13) with the engine's why. An engine writes what it made of the entry before it lets its owner
go, so where the command sees the owner gone it reads `questions.json` once more, and that read answers.
Where the engine's session ends without weighing it, the command's own session is the next, and weighs
that very entry under its id - so the run records one outcome of the person's answer. An entry a session
weighed between the engine's going and the command's claim of the run is read once the command holds
the run, before any session, and answered as the wait answers one - taken, or refused (13) with the
run's why, the questions and the inbox named either way, one owner of both - then emptied from the inbox
as settled, and no session is driven over it. Where a session that claimed the run first still holds it,
the command's claim is refused, and not its answer: the entry weighed, it is answered as above; not yet,
the command waits on that same entry as one handed to the live session, never handing it over twice.
The inbox is named on every exit after the write, a cancelled
wait and a session refused before it weighed the entry among them. Where the engine leaves before it takes a request, the command answers from the
run's state and takes the request back. `stop-orchestrator --now` ends the engine's process tree -
only on this machine, and only the process whose start matches the one its owner recorded - and
removes the owner once the engine's process has gone, the rest of its tree not waited for. Whether a run's engine is live is asked of one owner
(`FlowRunOwner`) by every command: `delete-orchestrator` refuses a run a live engine owns (13,
naming `pause-orchestrator` and `stop-orchestrator`) and removes a gone engine's owner with the run,
and `list-orchestrator` says what the engine is doing - none, starting, a session's claim taking the run up
(`flow.json`'s `starting`), running, pausing, recording what a complete pause left running, stopping, a stop it applied
ending its session (`flow.json`'s `stoppingSince`), or gone.

Two commands answer a person's question about a run (`FlowService.AskStatusAsync`,
`FlowService.AskAsync`): `ask-orchestrator-status` the tool's own - what is happening now, what is
done, what is left, what it waits for, and when it may finish - and `ask-orchestrator` a person's,
over the same facts. The facts are the engine's (`FlowStatus`, pure, over the records the same store
methods `list-orchestrator` reads: `flow.json`, `questions.json`, `updates.json`, the frozen
`definition.json` and the run's owner), computed and never guessed, stamped with the moment they
were read: how the run stands and for how long, its engine and its pause; each step instance in
progress; what it waits for - each open question with its next step, by the one rule the report names it by
(`FlowAnswerRules.NextStepOf`, over what the engine is doing): its answer; its answer taken now, ending the asking, where a
live engine's advisor seeks the recommendation or a live engine is starting, which seeks every one the run owes; or, where the question still owes its recommendation
(`FlowAnswerRules.OwesRecommendation`), the pause's advice where a live engine's pause defers it, the resume, which seeks
it first, where no engine runs the run, and the resume once the engine has gone where it is stopping, `abort` alone taken
now - a plan update
under way or queued, an instance waiting on another, on a claim or room, or on the fix of an issue that holds a file its
work item owns or that the item needs, a `ci-wait` reading the
checks of the commit the run last pushed; what is done and what was spent of the budget; what is
left at least and at most, with the bound that gave the most - at least what keeps the run from done,
by the engine's own rule of it (`FlowInstance.IsUnended`, `FlowInstance.RaisesOwed`, which the
engine's `Unended` and the resume read too): each instance that has not ended and what an ending owes the session
that goes on, a failure owed and each raise an ending still owes, named - a raise by the visit the resume raises, and
never one whose visit the records hold, which is counted once, as itself; at most besides each
member of a scope still open not
drawn yet, a loop's iterations to its bound, a handler's visits to its `maxVisits` with the steps its
`then` sends the run back over, the recovery's visits to its `maxVisits` for each failure it can take
with the steps it sends the run back over, and what no numeric bound holds named - and when it may
finish, as a range that rests on this run alone: of each step of
the definition that works the shortest and the longest time an instance of it took to end `Done` - a
group's own span is its members' time, never counted beside it - (the lower end laying what is left
along what depends on what as the engine orders two instances, `FlowInstanceId.Precedes` then
`FlowGraph.Waits`, so work that runs side by side is counted once; the upper end summing every
instance that is left - a handler owed its raise among them, as the instance the resume raises, timed
by its step - and everything the run may still make, one after another), a step no
instance of which has ended `Done` in this run counted and named and in neither end, as a failure
owed is, which its handlers, its policy or the recovery decide, the time a
person takes to answer and a wait for room - a claim, the run to be quiet, a counter of its limits,
each a word the admission writes from `FlowWaits` and the facts class by it - left out and said to
be, and no estimate at all where nothing has ended, where nothing is left - nothing keeps the run from
done, so a run paused with only an owed failure or raise is never said to have nothing left - or where
the run has ended (done or failed: a stopped
run goes on at its resume, and its stopped instances are among what is left), the facts saying
which. The most is everything the run may still make by the engine's own bounds and rules
(`FlowComing`), so it is a bound: in each scope still open - the top level while the run goes on, and
each group, iteration, item and recovery visit not ended - each member the schedule has not drawn yet;
`FlowRepeat.Bound` for each repeat instance not ended, past the iterations it made;
`WorkflowStep.VisitsAllowed` for a handler, in each scope its source can still end in, as the engine
counts its visits, with the steps its `then` sends the run back over at each visit - where that `then` sends the
run back over a group around it, in the scope it goes back to, past the visits made of it anywhere in that scope's
instance; and
`FlowRecover.VisitsAllowed` for each step whose failure the recovery can take (the policy that decides
for it, `FlowScope.OnFailureOf`, is `recover`), each visit of the recovery with the steps it sends the
run back over - what a redirect resets read by the engine's one rule of it, `FlowResets.Of`, and a step
it resets counted as able to end again - each bound widened by what was granted past it (`FlowGrants`,
the one owner the engine applies an answer by and counts the answers back by at a resume: each `more`
a repeat's, a handler's or the recovery's bound was answered in `questions.json`, and each iteration a
plan update added to a loop), a handler's granted visit the run has not carried out yet counted in the
scope it was granted in, and each piece of a plan update not carried out one item of the work-item
group. What such a visit makes is counted whole - a group with all that is in it, its loops to their
bounds and its own handlers and recovery. What no numeric bound holds - a `forEach` not yet expanded, a
repeat with no numeric bound, a step whose pre-existing issues each raise a triage, a plan update
still to be planned - is named, the run's own
bound of instances the only one that holds it; and a question open at a bound is named as what can
grant more past it. Where the
workflow's `reporter` names an agent, its words follow the facts, run by the one runner of the
agents that read a run's records (`RecordsAgentRunner`, the analyst's too), its reads narrowed to the run's directory alone
(`AgentPolicyGround.ReporterRoot`: no command, no write, no web - the three tools that read and no
other), its answer masked, its cost the person's and never the run's. Both commands only read: no
state file, no step, no agent, no budget, no lock an engine needs, not even the sweep every other
command over an orchestrator makes first - what a call leaves behind is its own record under the
run's `asks/<stamp>/` (the facts as given, the files of its reporter's attempt, the conversations
its client stores under `sessions/` - never under an agent's of the run - and `ask.json`), a
directory the engine never reads. Where no model words them the status still prints the facts, says
`no model worded this` and why, and exits 0 - 130 where an interrupt stopped its reporter, as an interrupt ends every
command - the facts are the answer, and the words were a service; the person's question is refused, naming why (12 where the workflow names no reporter or
the reporter's own files do not read - whatever keeps the reporter from wording the facts is why no
model did, read by `KnownCauses.Meaning`, and never an error of the command - 13
where the key is not there, 14 where npm or Claude Code is missing or too old, 20 where the model
failed, 21 where it could not be reached or its account is at its limit - `AgentRunResult.ToOutcome`
the one mapping - and 130 where an interrupt stopped the reporter),
and what a run that was begun spent is said however it ended - a client that throws after paid turns, or an interrupt
that stops it, is why no model worded them, its spend and the model its spend's own account says served held past the
throw (`RecordsAgentRunner`'s begun run) and still said and kept in the call's own `ask.json`, the `--json` answer in
the command's shape with its record named - and neither command installs Claude Code or brings one up to date. An orchestrator
made by hand, which no flow runs, has no reporter and fewer facts: its status prints what
`list-orchestrator` has of it and says so, and the person's question is refused (12).

A side-task is an agent outside every workflow (`SideTaskService`, `run-side-task` and
`list-side-tasks`): a conversation between a person and one agent over the repository's main
tree, asked directly - a chat in the terminal by default (the agent's text streamed, each
action one line as it is decided, a denial with its rule, Ctrl+C interrupting a turn and a
second ending the chat, a line ending in a backslash going on to the next, `/exit`, `/model`,
`/effort` with a level, `<code>=<level>` or `default`, `/records`, `/help`), or one message
with `--prompt`, answered once (`--json` its one document, a usage error without a prompt).
No second loop: each turn is an `AgentStepRequest` handed to `IAgentRunner` as the engine
hands a step's - the model resolved as a step's (`--model`, `--tier`,
`defaults.agentTier`, `--client`, `--effort <level>` or `--effort <code>=<level>` with
`all=<level>` for the rest, each checked against what the model takes by the one check of a
step's, `AgentEffortRules`), the order built with each entry's credential, what it spends counted
against its key - so the clients, the tool runtime, the stored stream, compaction and the fallback
are the ones every step uses; one builder sets all of it up (`SideTaskService.SetUpAsync`), at the
start and again for the chat's `/model` and `/effort` - a new model keeping only the levels that name
it and the one for the rest - and what a reason step is launched with beyond its model it takes from
that step's own builder (`ReasonLaunch`): its order, the Claude Code directories its ground keeps it
from, the mask its records and answers are held to - every secret the configuration appoints that the
slot answers, each provider's keys and each client's token, beside every form of each search key -
and the Claude Code it starts, made ready as a step's is and refused on the finder's own code and
words (12 the configuration, 13 an update refused, 14 the program missing, 21 the install of
Claude Code could not reach the registry, an install waited for to its end) where the entry that would serve first is on that client - one
`ReasonLaunch.ProgramAsync` decides for every asker, a step, the advisor and the reporter alike, a later entry on it
passed over when its turn comes with the finder's words as why - and refused, 14, where `agentPolicy.isolation` is
`required` and the machine cannot isolate its commands (`AgentIsolation`, below). What differs is what it is given: its
ground (`SideTaskPolicy`) - no restriction list, no allow list of pages, all four capabilities, the
main checkout the writable root, the worktree rules and the protected paths off, this tool's own
verbs open to it as the person's own session's are, but those that read a credential slot or write
its state (`AgentPolicy.SlotOrStateVerbs`) - with the built-in refusals kept (root
actions, every credential slot of the main checkout, every Claude Code directory its clients
use and every place the user keeps credentials in (`AgentPolicyGround.CredentialPlaces`), to its file tools and to every path a word of its commands names (`CommandAnalysis.PathsNamed`),
a directory that holds one given whole to a program that may read it among them but the main tree
it works in and those above it - a command over that tree whole, `.` or no path, is not told from
one over its sources and reaches the slots' files: the policy decides what a command names, it is
not a sandbox - `Write(.git/**)` and a command's write into `.git`, a removal or a move of a
directory that holds the main tree's `.git`, the state, a slot, a Claude Code directory or a place
the user keeps credentials in, the main tree itself among them
(`AgentPolicy.RemovalRefusal`), the tool's own state - each state path under the main tree,
`HarnessLayout.StatePathsUnder`, never the tree itself - the commands that print a credential, a
git or gh command called by a name none of its own commands is, and `run-side-task` itself,
refused to every agent where a word of a command or of a script the policy reads names it or a verb
the shell expands may, and refusing itself where the agent's mark, `AgentChildEnvironment.AgentMarker`,
is in its environment, a command that sets it, takes it away, may take it away or names it but as data refused
(`AgentPolicy.MarkerTouched`), or where a process of this tool's is among the ones that started it
(`AgentAncestry`, over the process table's seam: the tree walked parent by parent as the table names each, a process
that took a freed id never read as a parent (`SampledProcess.ParentId`, below), the tool - its own runtime, as the engine is -
told by the file the table gives a process: a runtime whose application - the first word past its own options, never
an argument of it - is the tool's assembly, the file this process runs as, or a host of the tool's package
(`ToolPackage.HostsPackage`: a file of the tool's command beside the tool's assembly, as a build puts it, or beside the
store a dotnet tool install keeps the package in); by its command's name (`ToolPackage.IsCommand`, the rule the tool's
update finds its running copies by) only where the table gives no file, so a launcher of that name - a script, whose
process runs its interpreter, or another program's shim - is none; one detached from the agent's tree - `at`, a
`tmux` server, a double fork - told by the mark alone, and a table read by names alone, or one without this
process, refused saying why, never read as a tree with no agent in it - the mark and the tree read together by
`AgentAncestry.UnderAnAgentAsync`, the one rule the fetch of a remote workflow reads the cache alone by too, each
refusal saying which made the command an agent's and that a person starts one from a shell of their own, in the one
wording the fetch's refusal gives too, `AgentAncestryAnswer.Why` and `AgentAncestryAnswer.APersonsShell`); code an interpreter runs and a process apart from the agent's tree
are where that reading of words ends); no limits, no output envelope; the web
search of every configured source turned on, with one more asked beside them: `native`, the
provider's own search - on the Claude API a request of the harness's own whose only tool is the
provider's web search (`ClaudeApiNativeSearch`, no server tool in any conversation), asked by the
loop with the model and key serving the run when the agent asks, through that key's lane, its
`max_tokens` the loop's own first room - a quarter of the model's `maxOutputTokens`
(`ToolLoop.FirstMaxTokens`), doubled up to the most where the answer was cut off before the
search returned anything - and naming no `max_uses`, so the model searches as often as the query
needs, its usage - each search among it -
counted then to that entry's part and priced at the provider's `pricePerThousandSearches`, a failure
of it - a hold past the longest wait among them, named - one failed part of the search saying why;
on Claude Code its own `WebSearch`, kept in a side-task's
`--tools` beside the engine's server; on Z.AI none. A chat goes on between the person's
messages the way its client goes on with any conversation: one launch held open where the
client renders its conversations (Claude Code), the person's later messages reaching the agent through
the channel a message to an agent at work uses, recorded as the person's (`ChatMessage`), the first
interrupt cutting the turn alone and leaving the launch open - reaching the launch after every line
the person wrote before it and before any written after, for the client hands those lines on as the
interrupt is raised, on the thread that raises it (`AgentTurnInterrupt.WhenAsked`) - a message the
interrupt dropped said to have been dropped, each turn of the launch written to `task.json` as it ends, and a launch that ends
by itself recorded and the lines it never answered sent again to a new one - counted by the client's
own count of the messages its turns answered (`AgentRunResult.MessagesAnswered`), never by what was
written, so a line taken by a turn that ended without answering is sent again. Such a launch is never
tried again nor moved by the runner: a try or a move begun inside the walk would begin again from its
first message and lose every line it had taken. Its retries are 0, so a failed turn ends it; and where
the walk would move on - a decline, a limit, a refused key, a failure - it ends the run on that ending,
says the move (`FallbackStarted`, `AgentFallback.ChatGoesOn`) and hands back the order it would have
gone on by with the move that brought it there (`AgentRunResult.GoesOnBy`, an `AgentGoingOn`: the
entry `AgentFallback.Next` finds, each after it as the walk would take it, and the `AgentMove`). The
chat goes on in a new launch from the conversation so far with the lines no turn answered - on the
entry handed back where there is one, as one request per line where that entry's client stores its
conversations - and its next request carries that move (`AgentStepRequest.Moved`, cleared once the
person sets the model or effort again), so the walk passes a first entry that cannot be started over
as one a move of its own reached and, the run being a chat's, hands back the entry after it with the
same move, never asking the one that cannot start again. Every side-task's request asks the
runner for no retry of a workflow's (`AgentStepRequest.Retries` 0): a one shot's turn, and each
message to a client that stores its conversations, whose agent failed on every model the walk
moved through is tried again whole by the side-task itself through the one owner of retrying
(`Retrying`, in `SideTaskWorking`) - after `SideTaskService.RetryFirstWait`, the wait doubled each
time up to `Waits.SaidEvery`, each wait said - for as long as it fails in a new way, by the digest
of its model, its ending and its error, and is ended, said, once a try fails as an earlier one did
(`SideTaskWorking.FailedTheSameWay`); a failure of the provider's service past its client's own
tries and a refused key are never tried again, and an interrupt ends a wait as it cuts a turn.
A run the person ended before a client
took it is never launched, by one owner of what ends a run before its launch begins
(`AgentRunner.Unbegun`): a chat's messages ending - the person left (`AgentMessages.Ended`) - and the
interrupt of a run that is no chat's, a one shot's turn (`AgentTurnInterrupt.Asked`). The runner
returns such a run before its turn of the lane and races the gate's wait and a retry's against it as
it races a handoff, ending it `Cancelled` with nothing launched (`AgentRunner.LeftBeforeItBegan`,
`AgentRunner.CutBeforeItBegan`). A chat's own interrupt there cuts nothing - no turn of it is under
way, and it is said so - and ends no wait; spent before a client was given the run, it is never handed
to the launch (`LaunchedAsync`), so it never cuts the turn the launch begins. The gate's wait is said
in the chat as it begins (`WaitingToRetry`). A chat's run is begun only on a client that renders its
conversations - the runner refuses it, never started, on any other - and Claude Code moves to no
other key inside it, so `MessagesAnswered` is always its one launch's own count; the run's end says
it (`RunFinished.MessagesAnswered`), and a line given to a launch that never answered it is read once
in the conversation that goes on and written once in `transcript.md`. Whether a turn of the launch is
under way is the client's own turns' (`TurnStarted`, `TurnFinished`), however many lines were written
to it meanwhile, and a line an interrupt drops is said (`MessagesDropped`). The launch's ending is its
last turn's only where the client says the run ended at that turn's own result
(`AgentRunResult.EndedWithItsLastTurn`: Claude Code's run ending at a turn's result, or idle with
nothing waiting as the person leaves), so a launch gone between turns, or in the middle of one, marks
no finished turn with its failure. The person leaving while a turn runs or a line waits never drops
that turn: Claude Code interrupts the turn under way with the waiting lines cancelled - unless the
person's own interrupt cut it already, answered or not, for a turn cut is never interrupted again -
reads on to the cut turn's result within `ClaudeCodeClient.InterruptBound`, counts it and ends there,
the lines it dropped never counted as answered, so what the turn used, cost and spent is kept and a
line it never took goes on with the chat. A turn begun once the person left - a line Claude Code took
before the interrupt reached it, or one typed after the person's own interrupt was answered - is cut
at once and settles nothing: its line is never counted as answered, and goes on with the chat too.
`/model` or `/effort` typed while the launch works ends it the same way and carries the lines it
never took, or took only once the person had left, to the new launch (`GoneOnAsync`), each turn
written on the entry of the launch that served it. One
request per message where the client stores them, each going on with the stored
one. A side-task whose last run that worked - one that began a session - ended `ContextExhausted`, a
chat's or a one shot's, has outgrown its context (`Working.Outgrown`, read from its stream): it keeps
no stored conversation to go on with, in `task.json` or in this process, for handed again it would
meet the same wall, and its next request - the chat's next message or launch, or a `--resume` in a
later process, by the one owner of how the next turn goes on (`Working.GoingOn`) - carries the
engine's compaction of the conversation as a step's is made - the whole conversation since the last
compaction, every launch of it read as one, the person's later messages as they said them - as the
request's `Compaction` before the person's message (`AgentCompacted.BeforeItsTask`), so the runner
says it in the side-task's stream as `Compacted` and counts it as it does a step's; the person is
told once, as the run given it begins, and the turn that outgrew it says only how it ended. The side-task's name is the person's (`--name`) or the date and
time it began - with the first words of its message in one shot; a chat is claimed, and named, before
its first message is typed, so by the time alone - the smallest suffix none holds freeing it where
others began in the same second, however many did, found from one listing of the side-tasks'
directory, and a name of any length taken where the machine's paths hold its records, refused (13)
by the machine's own limit on a path's length where they do not (`PathBudget`); its owner (`SideTaskOwner`, the owner file beside its records) is claimed before
anything is written, under one machine-wide lock for the side-tasks' directory, with `task.json`
written inside the claim, so two commands never take one name - a name another holds refused (13),
the records it holds named as that side-task's and never as the command's, a dead owner reclaimed
and said. `--resume` opens one again, refused (13) where it names no
side-task or another process holds it open, and `--name` beside it a usage error (10); it goes on
with its stored conversation, or, where the model it now runs on is reached by a client that is
handed none, from the conversation so far (`AgentContinuation`), on what the person last set it
to run on (`SideTaskRunsOn` in its record: the tier with the tier's later models, or the model
named outright) unless the command line names a model or a tier; an effort or a client the
command line names stands over the record's. Its records live in `.side-tasks/<task>/`, a root slot
of the layout in `StatePaths`, the tree's floor and the managed ignore block - refused (13) before
anything is written where git does not ignore it (`SlotIgnored`) - written by the tool alone and
kept until a person removes them: `task.json` (each turn with its client, provider, model and
effort, what it used and cost, and what the agent ran under), the stored stream `stream.jsonl`,
the transcript as a person reads it `transcript.md`, `denials.jsonl` and `web.jsonl` as a step's,
the stored conversation under `sessions/` where its client stores one - named on every exit,
in text and in `--json`, or said to be none where the command stopped before any were written.
Its exits are its turn's (`AgentRunResult.ToOutcome`, the one mapping) in one shot - 20 failed, 21
cut short, 130 interrupted: a one shot's interrupt cuts its turn by the turn's interrupt
(`AgentTurnInterrupt`) on every client, never by cancelling the run - Claude Code ending the launch
at the cut turn's result, the loop of the two APIs leaving its request where it stands and cutting
the calls running - each ending `Cancelled` (`AgentTurnInterrupt.Cut`) with what it used, cost and
spent kept, and a launch still waiting at the gate or to be tried again never begun - and, on any client, 12, 13, 14 or 21 where it could not start; a chat's are 0 however the
person leaves it once it has begun, 130 where two interrupts stop it while it is still being set up
or opened again. Its interrupts are its own
(`SideTaskTerminal` over `TerminalSignals`, the one registration of Ctrl+C, SIGTERM and a hang-up,
with `PointOfNoReturn.ChatsWithAPerson` turning the command line's own handling off for it): the
first cuts the agent's turn by the run's `AgentTurnInterrupt` on every client - a message to a client
that stores its conversations ending `Cancelled` with what its request used, the conversation kept to
its last whole turn (`Working.KeptWhole`, as the chat says it) - the second ends the chat as `/exit` does - a launch held open runs under
the command's own stop, never the side-task's, so the second cuts its turn, ends its messages and
waits for its result, what it used, cost and spent kept - each said by whether a turn of the agent's
was under way to take it (`SideTaskPress.Turning`: for a launch held open, its own turns tell it, so a
press while it is idle between turns says no turn was cut); and the side-task's own stop, linked to the
command's, is bound to them (`SideTaskInterrupts.StopsOn`) for wherever no turn runs - being set up
or opened again, its Claude Code or another model made ready: a one shot's first interrupt
stops it there, a chat's second, and an interrupt taken before the stop was bound is applied once it
is. No host serves either verb: a chat is the person's, on this machine (`HostAgentProtocol.NotForwardable`).

A session's interrupts are its own (`FlowTerminal`, `FlowInterrupts`): Ctrl+C, and off Windows
SIGTERM and a hang-up, are taken by `PosixSignalRegistration` and never end the process, and the
command line's own termination handling is off for every command (`CommandInterrupts`, the one
choice of how a command takes its interrupts, which `Program.cs` makes by): the three session
verbs and a side-task count their own, and every other command's first interrupt cancels it -
said, and it ends once its work has stopped, however long that takes - and its second is the
system's hard stop (`TerminalSignals.StopAtTheFirst`). They are counted once, for the whole session - every drive of it, the one an answer taken as
it ended begins among them - and the terminal's bound begins at the second of that one count,
whoever pressed the first; only the session's end clears it. The first asks the engine for the safe
pause, which starts no clock; the second asks it to stop where it stands: applying the stop is recorded at once, before
any step it stops is touched (a `stopApplied` event, as a later `--all` of a pause under way is), so the run's state says
Stopped from then on whatever a runner its drain waits for still does; the engine records a step whose runner does not end within 90 s of applying
the stop as stopped all the same (`PointOfNoReturn.SafePauseDrain`), and the command ends within 120 s
of the interrupt whatever is left (`PointOfNoReturn.HardStopBound`, the drain and 30 s to write the
end, so the terminal never cuts off a session the engine is still ending in order) - what a crash
leaves, which a resume goes on from. A command given `--output-logs` then writes its zip before it
ends, after the bound and with no bound of its own (no cap is put on it), for as long as packing the
run's directory takes, the run in it as the engine left it then; the second interrupt's warning says
so (`FlowTerminal`, told what the command writes at its end through `IEndWrites`, which `FlowOutputLogs` answers). A session cut off answers as every command over its run does:
the run and `resume-orchestrator <run>` named, every record listed in text and `--json`, and its line
in the run's log. A hang-up keeps the process to pause the run but leaves nobody to read the
terminal: from it on the terminal says nothing, and a line said while the session runs - an
interrupt's, the poller's (`FlowTerminal.Warn`) - is dropped where the terminal can no longer be
written to, never an exception that ends the process part way; the run's records hold what happened. The engine's loop alone applies either,
and a cancellation of the session's token is the second, never a cut-off. A step of a type no
runner serves yet is given to `NoStepRunner`, `FlowStepRunners`' fallback: it fails, saying no
runner serves its type (its code 14).

A session's output logs are one Core service, `FlowOutputLogs`, which any front end asks for through
the session it begins (`SessionOptions.OutputLogs`, an `OutputLogsRequest`: the path and the command line
as typed) - the command line by `--output-logs <file>` on `run-orchestrator`, `resume-orchestrator` and
`answer-orchestrator` alone, with no configuration key and no default: no flag, no zip. The lifecycle
every command shares (`CommandSession`) holds the path before anything is weighed - whole, read from
the directory the process stands in; a directory, a path inside `.orchestrators/` (where every run
keeps its own records, and a start names its run only as it starts), one inside the repository's main
checkout or one of its agents' trees where that tree does not ignore it - the tree found by git from the
nearest directory on its way that is there, and held to be the run's where it shares the command's main
checkout's git common directory - that checkout and every worktree git keeps of it - or is an agent's
repository whose mark names that checkout (`AgentRepositoryMark`), asked of git directly and never of
the locator of a tree's repository, which refuses a tree it runs nothing from, such as a worktree of a
bare repository, where the question is only whose tree it is; `check-ignore` read
against the index (`IGitClient.IsIgnoredAsync`), so a path the tree tracks is never ignored: such a zip
is one of the tree's uncommitted files, which every agent a run of it makes is handed with its seed, and
the next zip would hold it once for each; any other work tree, another project's checkout, a worktree
of a bare repository or a repository of dotfiles at the home, is none a run hands or folds from, and takes the zip - or one whose directory cannot be
made is refused with 13, nothing started - and at every end - the body's answer, a directory refused,
a failure it caught - writes the zip before it says how the command ended, the operation's own end and
the ends handed to it run first, with `--json` or without, so the manifest holds the lines they say and
the code a defect they met gives (70), and every wait any end makes - replacing a zip another program
holds among them - is said as the body's waits are, the operation's teller (`Waits.TellingTo`) set for
its whole life: the events it ends with are
kept as they will be written, so the zip holds its output as it ends, and then published, the zip named
as every record of a run is, the last line naming them (`outputLogs: <file>`) and
`records.outputLogs` in every document (`IDocumentFacts`). The zip is written whole through
`IFileSystem.WriteAtomic` - a file beside the target, then renamed over it - so a resumed run's zip
holds the whole run and a crash never leaves half a zip; one that cannot be written is said in its
place and named nowhere, the code standing as a run's log stands where it could not take a line, a
defect of the tool's ending the command with 70 as at its end. Which run the command reached is told
by `FlowService` as soon as the run's record is there (`FlowRunReached`), so a start without `--run`
that ended by a defect still has its run in the zip. The command's output is kept beside its console
by `CapturedHarnessOutput`, which hands every member to the console and to `OutputCapture`, the
console's own renderer writing into memory, under one lock: the lines in the order the terminal got
them, the `--json` document apart. The run's directory is walked from it held (`IFileSystem.Hold`,
`HeldDirectory`), one directory held for each level, so no link or junction is ever followed; links,
key stores and dotenv files at any depth (the tool's slots' names, `.env.*` and `*.env`) and the shared
copy of one a seed names, the run's `temp/`, the graph's caches (`FlowOutputLogs.GraphCaches`) and each
agent's worktree are left out, each listed in `manifest.json` with why. Every byte is held to the mask
the command's sessions kept the run's records through, never built again at the end: each session
begins its masks (`SessionMasks`, an owner of the engine's session) with the secrets its configuration
appoints that the key slot answers, and holds every mask the one builder of a launch's mask makes while
it runs (`ReasonLaunch.Mask`) - a step's web-search keys in every form they are sent in among them - and
every mask that comes to hold the gh login read again (`GrowingMask`), read as it holds its tokens at
the end; the sessions are told to `FlowRunReached`, whose `Masks` the zip reads. So a configuration
edited or a slot changed since a session began masks nothing its records were not masked of. Those are
this command's sessions alone: a resumed run's zip holds the records of earlier sessions too, which were
masked as they were written, but a file an earlier session kept as it came may hold a secret this
command's sessions no longer hold - a key since rotated out of the slot, a provider taken out of the
configuration - for nothing derived from a secret (a digest, a length) is kept from one session to the
next. The mask
is read byte for byte - Latin-1, which keeps every byte - by `ActionValues.ReadByteForByte`, which masks
each secret's bytes in UTF-8 and in UTF-16 of either byte order read so beside the secret itself, a
piece at a time cut where no secret parts (`ILineMask.Cut`); the manifest's strings are masked as text.
Where no session built the mask - the command began none, as an answer handed to an engine running
elsewhere (`FlowService.AnswerAsync` waiting on its inbox entry) and a refused resume begin none, or
none could build the configuration's (its providers do not resolve, the slot could not be read) - every
place the run's layout marks as one whose writer keeps bytes as they came, which no record's mask was
applied to, is left out whole, each named with why: never an unmasked copy. The layout that spells every
place is the one owner of the mark (`OrchestratorLayout.IsKeptAsItCame`), read by the zip and by the
help that lists it: the run's own (`OrchestratorLayout.RunPlacesKeptAsTheyCame` - each agent's
transcripts under `logs/`, `work/`, `plans/`, `inputs/`, `artifacts/`, `remote-workflows/`, and each
agent's `shared/`, `rows/`, `evidence/` (`AgentEvidence`'s copies of its worktree's evidence roots) and
`sessions/` (the provider's messages as they came)), and in each attempt's directory
(`OrchestratorLayout.AttemptDirectories`: every step's, each advice's, ask's and analysis's), what
`OrchestratorLayout.AttemptPlacesKeptAsTheyCame` names - the red legs' and red CI jobs' `logs/`, which
the runner's values alone masked, a measure call's `logs/`, `handed/`, a side agent's `work/` and
`sessions/`, and the continuation record, which quotes red legs' lines as they came. A command line the
parser refuses writes none: no command began.

### The codebase graph

A run's `graphify-codebase` step keeps a map of the repository under the run's `graph/` (`Core.Codebase`): every file the
tree lists is a node, every declaration an implementation reads is one, and the directed edges between them each say how
sure they are (`exact`, `unique`, `candidates`). Nothing of it names a language. Everything that reads a file's contents
is an implementation of one contract, `ICodeGraphExtractor` - its `Language`, its `Version`, its `Claims`, whether it
`Outlines` its files rather than reading a language's declarations, a pure `Extract` and its `Help` - which answers a
language-neutral `FileExtract`: nodes - a value's type (`ValueType`), the type an extension extends (`Extends`), the
scope whose declarations alone see it (`SeenIn`), the element selectors a component is named by (`Selectors`), the
files that are its templates (`Templates`) and whether its members are reached from their own code by a receiver alone and
never by a name written alone (`MembersByReceiver`: a name such members' code writes by itself is looked for past the scope
they are declared in and its bases - said by a type of its own members, and by a member a file adds to a type from outside
its body of the members of the scope it is declared in) among what they say - the scopes they are put in (open to
other files or closed: what a closed one declares, and the type or scope it is the scope of, its file's alone), imports by scope, relative path, address, path ending, directory (a scope every file under a directory imports) or a path under a root of the layout (`Rooted`), with their prefixes and filters, an import that stands in for the one before it (`Fallback`), an export (`Export`), an import of a file whose imports this one shares (`Shares`), one whose names are the file's importers' too (`Reexports`), one that takes the names a file publishes alone (`Published`), one that names a place a bare name is looked for (`Layout`), one whose prefix stands for the one name it shows (`Binds`), one of two places a name may stand at that the file cannot tell apart (`Either`) and one that serves one qualifier's references alone (`Serves`),
address roots, the names the file publishes (`Published`, with `PublishesTaken` where what its own such imports take is
among them), whether its names are bound within it (`BoundWithin`), whether it keeps its names' kinds apart (`KindsApart`:
a call reaches a member taking arguments alone, a use a value alone, neither a type), whether it writes its type names
whole (`WrittenWhole`: a qualifier's or a value's type is the type of that whole name alone), whether its directory is a
unit of its language's layout (`FolderUnit`) and the roots of the layout it declares (`LayoutRoots`), references by name
with their qualifiers -
one that asks whether a declaration is there, and is no external callee where none is (`Probe`), one made around the node
it is made from rather than in that node's body - a decorator, a parameter's annotation or default - looked for from where
the node is declared, its body's own closed scope passed over (`Around`), and one whose qualifier names a fixture, reached by
the nodes of the fixture sub-kind alone (`CodeQualifierKinds.Fixture`, `CodeSubKinds.Fixture`), among them - the string literals the file holds - every
one that holds a character, however short and however many, each value once in the file's own
table (`ExtractLiteral`) with every place it is written, its line and the node whose code holds it
(none where the file's own
does) - each its value as the language reads it: one collector
(`ExtractLiterals`) keeps them for every reader, the C# reader taking the compiler's value and the scanned readers the
value `ScanLiteral` decodes from what each lexer saw of the literal's form - a prefix, a raw string's delimiter, a
triple quote, a heredoc's label and closing indentation - by its language's escapes, a `String.raw` template's as
written, an HTML character reference by its grammar whatever its length; an interpolated or template string's
constant parts each a literal of its own, its holes read as code, a character constant, a regular
expression and JSX markup none, a JSX attribute's text one - and seven marks - a prototype, a test, a test by a type
another file declares (`TestByType`), a type tests are built on (`TestBase`), a part of a declaration other files hold parts
of too (`Part`), generated code with why, and each line it saw something it cannot bind or stopped reading at (`dynamic`),
with why - of which the linker reads the first five; every dynamic mark carries a
kind (`ExtractDynamic.Kind`), a constant of the reader that makes it, and what an implementation's help says it does not see
is a limit that names the signs telling a file it applies (`CodeGraphLimit.Signs`) - the kind of a mark, or what the linker
found of the file's references and imports, each sign one thing it knows and no language named (`CodeGraphLinked.Signs`): a
reference left candidates (`Candidates`), an import taken as several places and a reference left candidates through one -
what it found there one or several, as the place that found it says, never told by the files it lies in (`CandidateImports`),
and of a reference counted external why it named nothing - a name or a qualifier's head only imports
naming no file of the tree bind (`OutsideImport`), a name written alone nothing binds in a file that binds its names within
it (`Unbound`), a fixture no scope or serving import provides (`UnprovidedFixture`) - so that an answer says in full of a
file the limits it shows, and of none it does not. Every limit a reader marks names the kind of its mark, and every limit
that says a reference is bound by its name alone - a receiver whose type the file does not say, in every language: C's
`untyped-calls`, C++'s `overloads` and `auto-values`, C#'s `untyped-values` and `generic-extensions`, Dart's
`inferred-types` and `extension-members`, JavaScript's and PHP's `inferred-types`, TypeScript's `union-types` and
`any-values`, Python's `duck-typing` - names `Candidates`, what the linker gives such a reference left among several; the
contract's kit holds every mark of every fixture and of every cut of one to a kind a limit of its implementation's help names; an
implementation whose code another reads - an HTML page's scripts and styles, a Vue component's, a Razor file's C# - says
that reader's limits among its own (`JsHelp.Unseen`, `TypeScriptExtractor.TypesUnseen`, `CssExtractor.SheetUnseen`,
`CSharpExtractor.CodeUnseen`). Beside the calls, every
reader of C#, JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP, Dart, C, C++ and Python gives each member a member reads or writes without calling
it - a field, a property, a constant, an enum member, any name a `nameof` names, a `case`'s constant (Dart's pattern
constants among them), the first name of a receiver's chain - a member's or, in JavaScript and TypeScript, an
element's - where the reader takes it for a value (JavaScript and TypeScript by what the file says of the name: a
variable, a function, an import's binding but a namespace's and a type-only one's, whatever its case), a conditional's
branches - as a `uses` reference, qualified as its receiver is where the file says - a chain of
any length written as links, each name's use qualified by a link to the use of the name before it
(`ExtractQualifier.Link`, its names spelt back by `FileExtract.Written`), but Python's, whose names past the first member
are values by no name the file types (below) - one past a C# variable
of a declared type its first name's use qualified by that type, so it is read through each name's
type as one past a field is - and reads an enum
member's value as the member's code - C's, C++'s and
TypeScript's as C#'s, PHP's and Dart's. A type the code writes is no use but a `references` edge, in every reader - a
declaration's, a cast's, a `sizeof`'s, a template's or a call's type arguments (a C++ template's value argument read as
code), a parameter's of a lambda, a closure, an arrow or a function a body writes and its return type, a PHP anonymous
class's bases, traits and member types, an `as`'s or an `is`'s, a pattern's, a TypeScript assertion's (`<T>x`) - C and C++
taking a bare name in parentheses for a type's where the file knows it as no value, a C# `x is State.Done` both a
reference and a use of `Done`, which the syntax cannot tell apart; a declaration is no use either - each declarator of
`int a = 1, b`, a pattern's variables, a macro's parameter, a function pointer's own parameters, a structured binding, a
discard - nor is a type or a namespace a member is reached
through, nor a label a `goto`, a `break` or a `continue` names (`ScanCalls.NamesLabel`), and a member named as a word of
the language - PHP's `$node->parent`, `FieldType::String` - is its member's use. A use that names nothing the
repository declares is the common case and counts nowhere: a use is recall, never a doubt, so it makes neither a node
`unsure` nor a file's unsureness. A use is looked for as a
member of any arity or a type (the same steps as a call), and `query-codebase-graph`'s `node` answers a node's `users`
and `uses` groups beside its callers and callees.

The data a repository's code is configured by is read too, every data file's nodes made by one owner (`DataNodes`):
a key a member node of SubKind `key`, an element one of SubKind `element`, a container a section inside the section that
holds it - every one the file holds, however many and however deep, walked on a stack of the walk's own and never by
recursion - a summary and a signature put on one line and kept whole - a key's value its summary
whole, no sentence of it ending it (`ExtractText.Value`) - so no data file's extract is one the
core refuses. A
key's path is written, and read back, by one owner (`CodeKeyPaths`): each name joined by a dot, an item's place and a
name empty, of white space, holding a control character, or holding a dot or a bracket - the characters a path is parted
by - in brackets, quoted as `ReportText.Quoted` writes it and read back by `ReportText.Unquoted`, so a path is one line
and one sequence of places (`targets.x64.callingConvention`, `limits[1].value`, `packages[""].name`,
`messages["Sure?\nIt cannot be undone."]`, `Logging.LogLevel["Microsoft.AspNetCore"]`); a place in single quotes is read
as the same place (`['Microsoft.AspNetCore']`, its own mark and a backslash escaped as `Quoted` escapes a double quote -
one escape rule, `ReportText.QuotedBy`, with the mark its parameter) and never written; a key node is named by its own
name where it stands alone on a line (`Microsoft.AspNetCore`), every reader of data files - JSON, YAML, XML, MSBuild -
writing its keys' paths through the owner.
`json` (`.json`, `.jsonc`, `.json5`, the named manifests keeping their own extractors) and `yaml` (`.yml`, `.yaml`, but
`pubspec.yaml`) each make every scalar key anywhere in the file a key named by its path, its value as its summary, and
each member that holds others a section over its lines. JSON is read on a stack of the reader's own however deep it
nests (`JsonOutline`), stops where its reader does, nothing of the file read, and reads a `$schema` or `$ref` naming
another file by a relative path - its `#` pointer left out - as an import of it. YAML reads what it repeats by reference
once, where it is written (`YamlReading.Written` keeps an alias as the node its anchor names, never that node again): an
alias is a key whose value is the alias, with a reference to the node its anchor names (`CodeQualifierKinds.Own`, a
node of the file's own by its id, which the linker makes a `uses` edge of `exact`); a merge key is no key of its own,
its mapping a reference to each mapping it merges, in order - one or a list, a mapping merged twice in one merged once -
and a mapping written in the merge key's place is read there, at `<<`. So aliases that repeat one another, or one wide
anchor aliased a hundred thousand times, are as many nodes as the file writes, and a workflow's jobs and steps are read
once each however many aliases and merges reach them. YAML makes each document of a file of several a section by its
place (`[0]`), names a GitHub Actions workflow's steps by their `name:` (else `step` and its place), reads a step's
local `uses:` as an import of its `action.yml` and a job's as an import of the workflow file it names, each `uses:` once
on the line it is written on, and keeps what it read before the place it stops reading, marked. An empty JSON or YAML
file, or one of comments alone, is no stop. `xml` (`.xml`, `.config`, `.props`, `.targets`, `.resx`, `.xaml`, `.manifest`, `.nuspec`, but the MSBuild projects
and solutions `msbuild` keeps) reads every element however deep, makes its root a section, an element with an id-like
attribute (`name`, `key`, `id`, `x:Name`) an element named by its path and that attribute - the path told only where a
node is named by it, so elements that name nothing cost no more than their reading - and keys of a `.resx`'s
`data name=`, of a `.props` or `.targets`'s `PropertyGroup` children and of a `.config`'s `appSettings` `<add key>` and
`connectionStrings` `<add name>` (`appSettings.Timeout`, `connectionStrings.Main`,
`appSettings["Serilog.MinimumLevel"]`, the value or connection string the
summary), a `.props` or `.targets`'s `Import Project` an import of the file it names. A `.xaml` view's elements it names
by `x:Name` are fields of its `x:Class` type, of the element's type, as the build generates them, so the code-behind
reaches one by the field's name as it reaches a field of its own. An MSBuild project's own `PropertyGroup` properties
are keys of the project's alone, in a closed scope no other file sees, and a `$(Name)` its attribute or element text
writes - a comment never - is a `uses` of the property it reads (the `key` qualifier): the project's own of that name -
those declared before it, where it is read as properties are, in a `PropertyGroup` or an `Import`, every one where it
is read once all are - else the key of that name an XML file declares. A key, an element and every node a style sheet declares - a rule, a keyframes, a mixin, a
function, a font face, a variable, each of a kind within a kind `CodeSubKinds` owns and no code's kind is spelt as -
are reached only by a reference that says it names one - a `key` qualifier, a `selector` qualifier, a style sheet's
`style-variable`, `style-mixin`, `style-function`, `keyframes` or `font-face` qualifier (`CodeSubKinds.ReachedBy`), a
use through an import's prefix, a use an import makes visible by a name the file that declares the node exports it by
(`import { btn } from './x.module.css'`) - and by the keys' join, never by a name alone as code names code (`Takes`, the
one place that says what a reference may reach; from a file that keeps its names' kinds apart a call reaches what takes
arguments alone, a use a value alone and a new a type alone), so a PHP `$radius` reaches no SCSS `$radius` and a C#
`Button()` no mixin `Button`. The linker joins each key to the code
that names it: a string literal equal to the key's last segment, its whole path, the path as .NET's configuration spells
it (`Payments:TimeoutSeconds`, `Payments__TimeoutSeconds`, `Limits:1:Value`, `Logging:LogLevel:Microsoft.AspNetCore`
naming `Logging.LogLevel["Microsoft.AspNetCore"]`, read by `CodeKeyPaths.Dotted`) or a path
that runs through a YAML alias or merge to it - the longest part of the path its file holds deciding, a mapping's own
key shadowing a merged one's, each place looked for once and a path that comes round to itself through its references
ending there - and a literal writing a path in brackets, in either quote mark (lodash's `"a['b.c']"`), names the key of
the path the writer writes (`CodeKeyPaths.Canonical`), never the loose form of a key's path, its names' own dots as they
are, which code splits as .NET's configuration does; and each field or property whose name is the segment as a naming policy the repository declares
(`codebaseGraph.keyNaming`: `camelCase`, `snake_case`, `kebab-case` or `exact`, `camelCase` and `exact` the default)
writes it - each a `uses` edge of `candidates`, for nothing says the code reads that key; every key a literal or a name
names is joined, however many keys share it, and a key its file keeps to itself - an MSBuild project's own property -
is joined to none. The join is derived whole at every link, so a changed policy links again and reads no file again. A `.xaml` root's `x:Class` and a C# `partial` type say they
are parts of one declaration (`ExtractNode.Part`), and the linker derives `partOf` between the parts of one qualified
name - ids stay per language - which every walk that reads members - the `node` operation, a `related` walk, a type's
outline, the spans a body is served from - walks as one. A repository may map further file name endings to an
implementation of its own (`codebaseGraph.claims`), claimed after the exact names the registry holds and before the
extensions.

An implementation is registered by being written: the one scan of the core (`CoreImplementations<T>`, which
`CodeGraphExtractors.Implementations` reads) finds each, `AddDssHarness` registers each type of it
(`AddCoreImplementationsOf<T>`), and the registry built from them refuses two of one name, two claims of one exact name or extension of which either gives no
content test, no fallback or two, a fallback that claims a name or an extension, a claimed name no file can bear or
extension no file has, a version below 1, and a limit (`CodeGraphLimit`) with no short name - lower-case letters, digits and
dashes - or one whose name another limit of its implementation bears - so a clash is a red test, never an order. A file goes to the
claimants of its exact name, else of an ending `codebaseGraph.claims` maps, else of its extension, else to the fallback
(`listed`); their content tests decide among
several, and none or several saying yes lists it `ambiguous`. Everything else about the graph - `codebaseGraph.languages`,
V52's names and `help codebase-graph-languages`, which says each implementation and each of its limits under its short
name - is read from the registry. A test keeps the core from mentioning
anything under `Codebase\Languages\`. Every span counts lines as `CodeFileText.Lines` cuts them - CR LF, LF and CR
alone, as an editor and git count - and an implementation that reads a parser's positions turns each into a line by
`CodeFileText.LineIndex`, since a parser may also break lines at NEL and the Unicode separators.
An implementation reads its file's text by position (`CodeFileInput.Text`, a `CodeText`), never as
one string of it: over its file, the text is read through once by `EncodedText`'s rule for where
each block begins in its bytes and each line begins (`CodeLineIndex`), and then each block is
decoded again as it is read, a few held at once. A parser is given it by position too - the C#
compiler a `SourceText` over it (`CodeSourceText`), AngleSharp its UTF-8 as a stream,
`Utf8JsonReader` its UTF-8 a block at a time (`JsonOutline`), `XmlReader` and YamlDotNet's parser
a `TextReader` - and where a library keeps more, the implementation's help names it (`Holds`).
An extract is sound by `FileExtract.Problem` - every span inside the file, every
parent present, holding its child and no cycle, ids unique and of its implementation, text whole
UTF-16, every link to a reference before its own, each literal's value once with its places inside
the file - and every
node's digest is the core's to set (`WithDigests`), whatever the implementation set. The C#
reader parses on a thread whose stack the file's own measured nesting needs
(`DeepCalls.RunSized`), again on twice that where the parser's own guard still stops it, and
reads the tree on stacks of its own; a file whose depth no thread can be given is marked dynamic
at its deepest line, with why - no extract is empty without its reason. An `Extract` that throws or answers
no sound extract, or a content test that throws, lists its one file `unreadable` with why - a defect `failOn: incomplete`
fails on as it does on any file not read - never the end of a sync. Each implementation's tests derive
from one kit, `CodeGraphExtractorContractTests<T>`, whose checks (`CodeGraphContract`, each shown red on an
implementation that breaks it) hold it to fixtures for each claim, determinism whatever the line endings, answers alike
from many threads, a sound model, tolerance of any cut of a fixture, pure content tests that never both say yes with
another's, the same answer read over a file in blocks of three characters as from its string, the
extracts stored with the tests for its version (`fixtures/codebase-graph/<language>/v<version>/`,
written where missing with `DSSHARNESS_STORE_EXTRACTS=1`), and the edges its fixtures name through the linker. The saving
itself is measured (`CodebaseGraphServingTests`) over nine fixture repositories under `fixtures/codebase-graph/serving/` - C#,
C and Dart, and one each of HTML, CSS and TypeScript, of Vue, of Angular, of Razor and Blazor, of JSON, YAML and XML read by C#, of Python
- each with its `tasks.json`, the declarations a task's reference answer needs, and its `sites.json`, the data a site task
decides by and every place that decides it, each with how it decides: the bytes the pack and the bodies serve against the whole
files', the bytes each `sites` answer serves against the files its places stand in - the lines that end it among them, every
limit of each language whose files the graph read - each pinned, and every place checked to be in its answer as the card of the
node at its line saying the way the task says it decides, never any card that spans the line, so a change that drops a use, a
literal's place, a key's join or a selector's reach from an answer, or leaves a place the graph reads to the text search, goes red.

A language no parser this tool can carry reads goes through the structural scanner (`Codebase\Languages\Scanning\`),
whose core knows no language: a language's lexer cuts the text into tokens (`ScanToken`), its comments apart and each
conditional's directives marked as opening, alternative or closing - each lexer's run a `ScanLexing`, which holds what
every language's reads alike: the tokens and comments it collects, a name's characters, a line break, a punctuator read
alone, and the one reading of the language's comments (`CommentEnd`) its code and the code its literals hold are both
read by - and `ScannedText` matches the brackets - each branch
of a conditional read from where the conditional began, the brackets every branch leaves open at one depth joined into
one closed by the bracket after it (a brace the first branch leaves open kept though another leaves none, as
`extern "C" {` is), what the joined group holds being what every branch writes after its own opener, the head each other
branch repeats before its opener left out (`Inside`), every other bracket a branch leaves unbalanced stranded - matching nothing, holding
nothing, and ending its statement with the rest of its branch - and a stray parenthesis or square bracket stopped at a
brace so it never ends a body, a closer with nothing open it could close passed over at once, with no walk down what is
open; it gives a group's bounds and the bracket that closes one (`CloseOf`), a statement's end - past a `;`,
or the closer a language gives (`EndsStatement`) - the code between two indices, the comments above a declaration
(`CommentsAbove`) and a header on one line (`Spelled`, and as a node's signature `Signature`). `ScanCalls` reads a call alike for every such
language by the rules it gives (`ScanCallRules`: its keywords, and how it writes type arguments - the punctuators a
type holds and what may follow a list in an expression, which C++ gives a declaration's types more of than code's,
where `<` compares too) - a name, type arguments, `(` - its arity counted by the commas at its own depth; splits a list
of declarations at its top-level commas and finds the first of a token at its top (a parameter's default `=`), groups
and type arguments passed over alike;
`ScanComments` reads a declaration's summary from the comments above it and the mark of a generator
from every comment before a file's first code, however many lines a licence runs over;
`ScanStack` walks declarations, always moving on, a block nested in another a walk of its own read
in the order the text writes it, what a reader holds around a walk set again when the walk is read
(`ScanStack.Holding`), and `ScanFrame` says where a reader stands, never how deep it may go - so a
text nested any depth is read whole and none nests a reader past its stack; and `ScanExtract` gathers nodes by keys, giving their ids
once the file is read - a declaration with a body before one without, so a prototype never takes its definition's id -
with a namespace's parts in one file one node. `ScannedText.AngleEnd` and `ScanCalls.TypeArgumentsStart` find a list of
type arguments' end and its start from either bracket, alike for every language that writes them. A language's reader
(C and C++ share `CFamilyReading`; Dart's is `DartReading`, over `DartLexer`) says what a declaration, a scope and an
import are. Dart's lexer keeps a string whole with every interpolation it holds and says where each `${...}` holds
code - through `ScanLexing.LiteralStack`, the one stack of what a literal's reading is in, JavaScript's and PHP's lexers'
too, which passes over that code's comments by its language's rules and holds its braces alike for each
(`LiteralStack.Past`) - which the reader scans as a text of its own; its reader puts a library's declarations - its
file's and its parts' - in one open scope named by the library's path, keeps each private name to it (`SeenIn`), has a part share its
library's imports (`Shares`), and reads a test framework's `test`, `testWidgets` and `group` calls in a test file as test
