underscore - one the code computes or changes marked `dynamic` - and, where it names no literal `__all__`, what its own `*`
imports take (`PublishesTaken`), which the linker follows from file to file, each once; at the module's top such an import
is its importers' too, so a package that star-imports its modules gives their names. A Python file's extract says its names
are bound within it (`BoundWithin`), so a name a file neither declares nor imports is not looked for through the repository,
nor is a qualifier the type or scope of its whole qualified name or of its ending: a reference the file binds by no import
it makes is counted external, and why it bound nothing is the sign of the limit that says so - a name only an import naming
no file of the tree binds (`CodeGraphLimit.OutsideImport`) of the roots the tree does not show, a name nothing binds (`Unbound`) of the
names a file neither declares nor imports, and a fixture no scope and no serving import provides (`UnprovidedFixture`) of
the fixtures no `conftest.py` above the test declares - so a call into the standard library shows the first alone; a bare
import of two places, and a reference left candidates through it - one place or both declaring what it names - is the sign
(`CandidateImports`) of the limit that says which module such an import names. `self` and `cls` qualify a
`this` reference, `super()` a `base` one; a chain whose head an import binds is qualified by what the import reaches - the
`prefix` of the module the longest run of its names before the member reaches, else the `type` those names stand for inside
it - a module path however long and never a value, one rule for a call's, a use's, an annotation's and a base's chain - and
where every member of the chain is a use, each `type` past the first member is written as a link to the use of the member
before it (`ExtractQualifier.Link`), so a chain writes each of its names once and never the names before each again, and a
name the language keeps to itself on the way - a module's `__version__`, a class's `__init__` - is a probe of what the module
or the type declares (`ExtractReference.Probe`), the chain read on through it; a
name read alone and the head of a chain the file declares or imports - `CONFIG` of `CONFIG.get()` - is a `uses` of what it
names, whatever that is, an imported class or constant alike (a `references` where it names a class the file declares), and
each member a chain passes on its way to its last - `items` of `self.items.append(x)` - is a `uses`, those after the first
of a chain no import's head is values by no name the file types rather than links, since a `self` chain's head writes no name to link to and a function's body sees no
name of its class; a call of a name written with a capital first letter is an `instantiates`, as a method's `cls(...)` and
`type(self)(...)` are, of the class the method is of (an `own` qualifier); a type an annotation, a string
annotation, an `isinstance`, an `except` or a `case`'s class pattern names - dotted or not, through the import its head is -
is a `references`, every one read by the one reader of a type expression, which reads `Literal`'s values and `Annotated`'s
metadata as code; a `case`'s dotted value is a `uses` and its captures are bound. A decorator is read whole as code and kept
as a modifier by its dotted name: the name it calls with what it decorates is a call - of one argument where it is written
alone - a probe (`ExtractReference.Probe`) where an import of a package binds it, and one the language answers to names
nothing; no decorator is told by the name it is written with. A parameter a test or a fixture
requires is a reference with a `fixture` qualifier (`CodeQualifierKinds.Fixture`), reached by the fixtures alone - nodes of
sub-kind `fixture`, functions pytest's or pytest-asyncio's fixture decorator decorates, told by the import that binds the
decorator's head and named by its `name=` where one is given - as pytest finds one: what the test's scopes declare, its
class's and its module's, else what the nearest `conftest.py` that declares it holds of its directory and each above it - a
`conftest.py`'s module is a `directory` import that serves the fixture references of every file under its directory alone
(`ExtractImport.Serves`), which only such an import may do - and nowhere else; a fixture that requires its own name is given
the one a level out, which it overrides, and never itself; and a name a `parametrize` mark gives a test - the test's own, each
class's around it, its decorators' and its `pytestmark`'s, and the module's `pytestmark`'s, as pytest reads the marks of a test
and of each node it is collected under, one reader of them all - is no fixture of it, but one the mark's `indirect=` routes to
the fixture of that name, which the test still requires: every name where it is `True`, those of a list or a tuple of strings. A
class's own marks pytest applies to every class built on it too, so the class says the names they give in place of a fixture
(`ExtractNode.Parametrizes`), and the linker finds no fixture of such a name for a test of a class built on it, any number of
levels up along the bases it found, each type once: the reference is none, counted nowhere and signed nothing.
A test is what a runner collects: a pytest file - `test_*.py` or `*_test.py`, pytest's default `python_files` - holds tests in
its `test*` functions and its `Test*` classes, and no other file's names make one, so a `testing.py` or a `testclient.py`
holds none of them; a `TestCase` subclass - built on a class an import reaches by a name ending in `TestCase`, or on a class
of the file that is one - is a test class wherever it is declared, as unittest runs it by its type, and a type tests are built
on (`ExtractNode.TestBase`); and a test class's `test*` methods are tests. A class of a file a runner collects by its name -
pytest's, and unittest's and Django's `test*.py`, `tests.py` among them - built on a base another file declares, or on one a
`*` import may bind, says it may be a test class by that base (`ExtractNode.TestByType`), as does each `test*` method it
holds, and the link makes them tests where a type tests are built on is among its bases, any number of levels up; a base the
language answers to, or a class of the file that is no test class, makes none. A method is bound by its name alone, so each carries an `overrides`
reference of its own name with a `base` qualifier, an edge where a base of its type declares it along the chain; no word of
the language says a method overrides, so the reference is a probe
(`ExtractReference.Probe`) - it asks whether a declaration is there, and where none is it is no external callee.

The one linker (`CodeGraphLinker`) resolves every reference by the same steps for every language - the qualifier's
scope, a type and its bases among it; the enclosing scopes from the inside out; a scope import's prefix (an alias),
for what that import stands for; the file's imports in order, filters applied - a file imported making visible what it
declares at its top, what it declares exported by another name by that name, the open scopes it declares and what each
file it exports does, each export's filter applied and
each file once, an export making nothing visible to the file that makes it, and a file that shares another's imports
(`ExtractImport.Shares`, a Dart part's of its library) importing those after its own; the repository by name and arity, but
for a file whose names are bound within it (`FileExtract.BoundWithin`), whose name no import binds is bound by nothing (a
type's name written by a file that writes its type names whole, `FileExtract.WrittenWhole`, being the type or scope of that
whole qualified name alone and no other, and a call, a use and a `new` written in a file that keeps its names' kinds apart,
`FileExtract.KindsApart`, reaching a member taking arguments, a value and a type alone) - a
qualifier being read as such a prefix too where no type or scope has it as its whole qualified name, from the file
that makes the import or, made global, from every file of its language, and a name no value or type has that an import's
prefix is standing for that import, written as a value or before a type's name - and derives `dispatches`, `declares`,
`tests` and `partOf` from the `implements` edges and the marks - a declaration marked a test by its type a test where a
type tests are built on is among the bases its type is built on, along the `inherits` and `mixesIn` edges any number of
levels up and through types no file marks, each type walked once - and the keys' join from the literals and the fields
and properties that name a key. A type is looked in before its bases and its bases a level at a
time, each level nearest first, the first rank that holds the name deciding with all it holds: the mixins each type of
the level names, a rank each, the last first - each applied over what comes before it - then one rank of everything
the level's types inherit and implement, a mixin's own inherited bases (what a Dart mixin is declared `on`) not followed
where it is applied; a dispatch answers as sure as the surest way up to its answer. A type's
bases are found a round at a time - the first through no base, each next through the bases the
round before found - until a round finds what the one before did or comes back to bases an
earlier round found (`Fixpoint`): a base named through bases of bases any number of levels up is
found, and what a base is never hangs on the order the files come in. A declaration kept to a scope (`ExtractNode.SeenIn`) is seen only from the
declarations written in that scope or inside it, as the scopes they are written in climb. A closed scope at a file's top - one no scope holds and that is no type's or namespace's own, as a C
file's for its `static` names - is one every declaration of the file is written in, looked in after its own scopes, so
what it declares is found `exact` from anywhere in the file. A closed scope under a member's own qualified name is that
member's body - a Python function's, whose parent is the function or the module around it and never a class, and a
JavaScript wrapper's: a reference the member makes is looked for from that scope, then its parent, so a body never reaches
the names of a class around it but through what qualifies them; one made around the member (`ExtractReference.Around`) - its
decorators', its annotations', its defaults', the fixtures its parameters name - is looked for where the member is declared.
What a member's body declares is seen from that body and the scopes inside it alone (`CodeGraphLinker.Placed`, `Bodies`),
whatever its extract keeps it to: no other code of its file - a member's body is no closed scope at its file's top - no lookup
from outside the body, a qualifier's or a type's name among them, and no name the repository's step looks up reaches it. An import marked `Fallback` stands in for the one before it - a C `#include` in quotes, found by its
path's ending where the including file's folder lacks it - and is taken only where that one names no file; a
prototype found beside its body - the same language and qualified name - is that body; and a member defined outside
its type's body, as C++ writes `T::f`, is in the type its declaration's scope names. A qualified reference is looked for where its qualifier says alone. A `type` qualifier is a type or
scope found as a name is - nearest first in the scopes it is written in, then the container of its whole qualified
name, an alias, an import's, the repository's - else every container its name ends, or, where the file writes its type
names whole (`WrittenWhole`), the container of that whole qualified name alone and no other; a `named` one is that too,
unless a value a scope it is written in holds (a base's among them) is nearer; a `scope` one is the scope it names alone,
else the declarations in no scope - with no name those alone - each of its own language, `exact`, as PHP finds a function
or a constant in its namespace and then the global one. A `type` or `named` qualifier written as links is the chain its links write
(`ExtractQualifier.Link`), found as its names written out are: past an import's prefix it is or begins with - however many
names the prefix writes, Python's `pkg.mod` - its first name what the import makes visible by it, each next a member of what
the one before came to, each chain of a file answered once from the chain before its last name (`AliasedBy`), so a chain of
any length costs a step a link; and a reference whose chain found nothing, or left candidates, is bound - for the sign it
gives - where the chain's head is (`Head`). A value - and a `value` qualifier - is
followed through its member's `ValueType`, each name of a chain, from a value or from a type,
through the one before's
type, a chain written as links read a link at a time, each link stepped once for each
declaration, chain before it and name - so a chain of any length costs a step a link and one two
statements write alike is stepped once -
a chain whose head names a type - a qualifier's,
or a variable's declared type - looked for a link at a time through the declarations' qualified
names parted at their dots, the chain before each name carried as that one's and never written
out, a type the repository does not declare holding nothing it declares; a call on a value of no said type goes by
its name in the repository, never to a type and never to the caller's own scopes. A call a type does not hold goes,
`unique`, to a member that `Extends` that type or a base of it, as the extension's own file names the type - or a type
the repository lacks, by its written name - where the call's file reaches it: the scope of the extension's type, or
the one holding that, is one the call is written in, or is the top; or an import of the call's file makes it visible -
an import of that scope with no prefix (an alias names a scope and imports nothing), or of a file that declares the
extension, declares that scope open or exports one that does - each filter on the way letting the name of
what holds the extension, what a file imported exposes by a name walked once and
kept for every reference that asks it; one in a closed scope is reached from its own file alone, one kept to a scope from that scope alone,
and no override is an extension. Extracts keep names, not targets, so a name a changed file adds
binds callers in files that did not change. Each finding keeps every key it read - a chain's
links' keys kept once and read through whole
(`KeptReads`), a name's declarations, an id's parts,
a qualified name's containers, a name's run's end, a scope's parent, a type's bases, a file's imports and open scopes,
a language's global imports, the address roots, a path, a file name - each read through the one accessor of its index,
which says the key (`Named`, `ScopeNamed`, `ContainersOf`, `ParentOf`, `PartsOf`, `BasesOf`, `ImportsOf`, `IsFile` and
the rest); `CodeGraphLinker.Relink` takes the link it is made from (`CodeGraphLinked.Memory`, held in memory alone)
and finds again only the references of the files not given as the very object that link was given, and those whose
finding read a key whose part - what each changed file holds of it - is not what it was, the bases each round found moved
among them; every other reference keeps its finding, and `References` counts what was found. What findings ask again -
what a written name is from a file and a scope, what an extension extends, what a file imported makes visible by a name -
is found once, with what finding it read (`CodeGraphLinker.Cached`), every cache of the link - those, the chains' and the
aliases' memos, the links of chains stepped - sharing one set of makings (`MadeOnce`, `Makings`), the makings taken as the
graph they make and its strongly connected sets found as they close, on the making stack alone and with no recursion: a
key asked again while it is being made - directly or through any store that shares the makings - is a cycle; every key of a
strongly connected set of makings that holds a cycle answers its placeholder, nothing known, with whatever its store keeps beside
it of what the whole set read - here each member's made reads, joined once into the one `KeptReads` every member's kept answer
carries - and every read of such a key, while the set is made and after, is given that answer; every other key keeps the answer
its making made; each key is made once, each set is closed once as its outermost making ends, and nothing kept is ever made
again - so the link's work is linear in the makings and the reads, whatever key is asked first and however deep the cycles nest. No
making of the link reaches a cycle: what comes round in a language's imports, re-exports or bases is walked inside one
making, each file once, the union of what it reaches. A global import is read from the file that makes it, so a
relative one names the same file from every file of its language. An interface's member dispatches, for each type that implements it -
itself or through a base, the interface itself or one extending it - to the member with a body that answers it: the type's
own, else its nearest base's it inherits or mixes in, never an interface's own, which has none. A dispatch is as sure as
the least sure edge on its way up, each of several bases that answer alike is one of the candidates, however many, and
an edge found more than one way is listed once, as sure as its surest finding. Every declaration a reference may be is
an edge of its own - two or more of `candidates`, none picked and none dropped, however many - through the name index,
so no reference is counted as naming too many, and a link result counts only what references named outside the
repository - never a probe that found nothing, since nothing it depends on is missing.
A linker that answers otherwise raises `CodeGraphLinker.Revision`,
which every link result names: a graph linked by another revision is linked again, though no file changed and none is
read again.

The page and its styles are read too. Every markup file - an HTML page, a Vue component, a Razor file's markup - is
read by one reader (`MarkupText`): AngleSharp's HTML tokenizer, so a tag, an attribute, a comment and a raw-text
element (a script, a style) are read as a browser reads them and no tag a comment holds is an element, and one walk
over its tokens - a stack, no recursion, however deep the markup nests - that matches each element to its end tag: a
page's as HTML closes them where their end tags are left out (a `p` at the next block, an `li` at the next item), a
component's as written, `/>` closing any element, so no tag is dropped as a browser drops one it finds out of place,
and a component named as a raw-text element is - a `<Title>`, a `<Textarea>` - or as one no end tag closes - a
`<Link>`, an `<Input>` - holds the markup it is written around as any component does.
What one element says is one rule over a table each kind gives (`MarkupDialect`): each class a `uses` of the rule
`.name`, split at ASCII white space as HTML splits a class list - a tag of the markup's own expressions or of another
engine written into a name (Angular's `{{ }}`; on a page, `{{ }}`, `{% %}` and `{# #}`, `HtmlExtractor.EngineAny`) one
piece with it, whatever white space it holds, and no class (`MarkupDialect.Classes`) - and an id a `uses` of `#id`, looked for among rules
alone by a qualifier of its own (`selector`); which tag is a component's, an `instantiates`; and what each attribute's
value is (`MarkupRole`) - a handler's code, a bound expression, a loop, the names a slot declares, or nothing the graph
reads. What that code calls, uses and declares is never the dialect's to say but its language's reader's: each
markup's reader gives it the code as its framework compiles the value - an HTML `on*` the body of the function HTML
makes of it, a Vue handler that names a member a call of it with what the event gives - each piece the body of a
function of its own whose parameters are the names the markup declares where the piece stands that it names, found by
one walk that holds each name once over the stretch it is declared for (`DeclaredNames`), so no name one piece declares
is another's; the JavaScript reader or the C# reader reads them (`EmbeddedCode.Script`, `EmbeddedCode.CSharp`) and
each function is folded into the markup's node it stands for. Code a markup file holds is embedded one way
(`EmbeddedCode`): its language's own reader is given the host's text with only the code kept, so what it declares
carries the host's lines - or, where one piece stands inside another's, a text of its own each line of which is given
back as the host's line it stands for (`FileExtract.Relined`) - and every field of what it answers - nodes, scopes,
imports, references, dynamic marks, literals - is merged into the host's extract, every field that names a node
following it where its id is told apart or it is folded into one of the host's (`FileExtract.Renamed`). `html` (`.html`, `.htm`) makes each
landmark (`main`, `nav`, `header`, `footer`, `aside`, `article`, `section`) and each element with an `id` a `section`
from its start tag to its end tag, a `<template>`'s content among them, and the `body` one that holds what no other
does - named by its id where it has one, the node every reference made outside a section is made from; a custom
element (`<my-widget>`) an `instantiates` of a component of that name; a `script src`, `link href`, `img src` and
`a href` naming a local file by a relative path - one that climbs among them - an import of it (`HtmlExtractor.Local`,
the one reading of what a markup's `src` or `href` names); an `on*=` attribute the body of the function HTML makes of
it, given `event`, read by the JavaScript reader - `return validate(this)` a call of `validate`, `go` alone a use;
each inline `<script>` of JavaScript read by the JavaScript reader as a program of its own, from where its
start tag ends - a module where its type is `module`, and one of another type, a template a framework reads, no code -
and each `<style>` by the style sheet's reader in the syntax its `lang` or its `type` names (`text/less`,
`text/x-scss`; CSS where it names neither), one of a syntax no style sheet's reader reads read as none. The text runs
a page holds leave out a script's and a style's raw text (`MarkupText.Texts`, one flag of the walk), so neither is read
as a template's; a page whose text or attribute values write another template engine's tags - Jinja's, Django's or
Twig's `{% %}` and `{# #}`, Handlebars' `{{#`, `{{/`, `{{>` and `{{!--` - is read as a page and never as an Angular
template, each of the engine's tags marked dynamic of the kind `template-engine` (`HtmlExtractor.OtherEngine`), which
makes the file one the graph's sites search by text and is the sign of the limit that says so.

`css` (`.css`, `.scss`, `.sass`, `.less`) reads a sheet over the structural scanner's core, as the code readers do:
`CssLexer` cuts it into tokens - a string to its own quote not escaped, an unquoted `url(...)` one token, `/* */` a
comment and `//` one only in SCSS, Sass and Less, an interpolation (`#{...}`, Less's `@{...}`) one token whose code is
read in its turn, each one nested in it passed over to its close where the first scan found it (`CssLexer.Closes`), so
every character is scanned by its own interpolation's scan and the first alone - and `ScannedText` matches its braces,
so `CssReading` walks it block by block with a stack of the blocks it is in, each line a token's: a block, a
pseudo-class's selectors and an interpolation nested to any depth are read whole, never by a call into itself, and
nothing is cut at a depth. The indented syntax of `.sass` is first written in SCSS's braces line for line
(`CssLexer.Braced`), each line's end, trailing comma and brackets read by the same lexer, so one reader reads all four.
Each simple part of each selector - `.btn`, `#main`, `my-widget`, `%placeholder`; no pseudo-class, attribute or
`:not()`, but an `:is()`'s, a `:where()`'s, a `:global()`'s, a `:local()`'s and a `:deep()`'s selectors, and a nested
rule's `&__title` written onto its parent's name - is a member SubKind `rule` named as CSS reads it, escapes read
(`ScanEscapes.Css`, which a string's value is decoded by too), over its own rule's lines, inside an `@media`,
`@supports`, `@layer` or any other at-rule's block too. A suffix written onto a `&` that stands for several selectors -
`.a, .b { &-x {} }` - is one node named `&-x`, written onto each of their nodes (`ExtractNode.SuffixOf`) and never
written out name by name, so lists nested in lists are as many nodes as the sheet writes, not the product of every
list; the linker matches a name to the nodes that write it - the suffix its end, the rest a name a node it is written
onto stands for in turn - each node at each place of the name once, however many reach it. Each custom property,
`@property` and SCSS or Less variable is a `style-variable` - but a Sass or Less variable a block declares without
`!global`, a mixin's and a function's parameter and a loop's variable, which are the block's own: no node and no use,
known at once from one table of what the open blocks declare; each `@mixin` a `style-mixin`, `@function` a
`style-function`, `@keyframes` a `keyframes` and `@font-face` a `font-face` named by its family in lower case, each id
spelt with its at-rule's word (`#@mixin fade-in`) so two kinds of one name are two nodes; a selector, an import's path
or a name an interpolation writes is no node and no import, marked dynamic, what the interpolation uses read. A
`var(--x)`, a `$x` and a Less `@x` are uses of the variable (the `style-variable` qualifier), an `@include` a use of
the mixin (`style-mixin`), a call of a function a sheet may declare a use of it (`style-function`; CSS's own -
`calc()`, `var()`, `url()` - none), a name an `animation` or an `animation-name` gives - not one of the shorthand's
own words - a use of the keyframes (`keyframes`), a family a `font-family` or a `font` names a use of the font face
(`font-face`; a generic family none); a Less mixin call a use of the rule it names, an `@extend` and a Less `:extend`
an `inherits` of the rule it names - by the `selector` qualifier, as a document's classes are - and a Tailwind
`@apply` and a CSS module's `composes` uses of the rules of the classes they name. Each is made from the node that
holds it, what no node holds - a top-level `@include`, a rule of no parts - from the sheet's own top node, `(sheet)`
(`ScanExtract.Top`), and each string and `url(...)` is a literal of its node. Each is looked for nearest first, of its
kind alone: the sheet's own, exact; then what each file it imports makes visible, unique - one walk through them all, a
file reached once - a Sass member by an import of no namespace alone; then the repository's, unique. An `@import`,
`@use` and `@forward` naming a file of the tree is an import of it, each file it may be tried in the order its language
tries them - Sass's partials, extensions and index files a fallback each, Less's `.less` - none of a package, a URL or
one of Sass's own modules, and an `@import` Sass leaves to CSS (`url(...)`, one a media query follows) tried as
written; a `@use` is reached by its namespace, the import's prefix, a `@forward` is an export with its `show` and
`hide`, and a `composes: a from "./x.css"` an import of that file by its path, `a` the class it exports by that name.
A sheet named as a CSS module (`x.module.css`) keeps each class, id and keyframes to itself (`ExtractNode.SeenIn`) -
but one under `:global` - and exports each by its name and its camel-cased one (`ExtractNode.Exports`; a suffix
written onto several by the forms of its suffix, matched as its names are), so a script's
`import styles from './x.module.css'` and its `styles.btn`, or an `import { btn }`, bind to the rule `.btn` through the
import, by the linker's one rule for an exported name, and no other file's selector reaches it - nor a class markup
writes, which the module renames: what a module keeps to itself and exports is reached by its name from a node of a
style sheet alone, its own `composes` or `@extend` (`CodeGraphLinker.Takes`). A style block another reader hands the
style sheet's reader as a component's `<style scoped>` (`StyleScope.Scoped`) keeps the parts of each selector's last
compound - the element Vue's attribute marks - and its keyframes to its file, but those under `:deep`, `:slotted` or
`:global`; one handed as a `<style module>` is read as a CSS module is. `related` answers `styledBy` (the rules that style a node: its `uses`
edges to a rule, SubKind `rule`, alone) and `styles` (what a rule reaches: the nodes whose `uses` edges reach it, asked
of a rule - of any other node, nothing), so "who uses this class" and "what styles this element" are one call each.

Razor views (.cshtml) and Blazor components (.razor) are one implementation, `razor`: a component is a type named by
its file in the namespace a `@namespace` gives it - else the nearest `_Imports.razor`'s above it,
each directory past that one a name after it, as Razor compiles it (`FileExtract.FolderScope`,
which the linker reads the component in, its id the one its path gives), else its directory's
path, each part made a C# name as Razor makes
it (`my-app` is `my_app`), none at the tree's root - generic by its `@typeparam`s, named as the C# reader names a
generic type (``Grid`1``), and a view a section over its lines. The file is read as Razor's own parser reads it, in one
walk over its text with a stack of what is open (`RazorExtractor.Syntax`), so no nesting is too deep to read: its
comments; its `@code` and `@functions` blocks; the directives a line begins with; each statement it writes - a
`@{ }` block, an `@if`, `@foreach`, `@try` and their kin, with their `else`, `else if`, `catch`, `finally` and a
`do`'s `while`, written with no `@` as Razor writes them - its C# read token by token by the compiler's own lexer, so
a brace a string or a comment holds ends no block, and the markup Razor switches to inside it - an element where a
statement may begin, `<text>`, an `@:` line, an `@<tag>` template - held to the end tag that closes it; each
expression - `@x.y(z)`, `@await x`, `@( )` - in a text or an attribute's value, but a directive attribute's, whose
value is C# of its own, and an address's `@` and an `@@`, which are text. The class the file compiles to is read by
the C# reader as one class (`EmbeddedCode.CSharp`): on the first line its namespace and its `partial class`; the code
of each `@code` and `@functions` block; an `@inject` a property of the type it is given, `@model` its `Model`
property, `@inherits` and `@implements` a part of the class with that base, `@attribute` one with that attribute; and
each piece of C# the markup holds - each statement at the markup's top whole, the C# of the markup it switches to
among it, a `@{ }`'s braces none, for Razor compiles its code where it stands; each expression; each directive
attribute's value, a handler that names a method a call of it with whatever the event gives; `@layout`'s type and
`@page`'s route - code of the file's head, a field's function of its own, so it sees the class's members, a name it
reads by itself a member of the component (`this`) and no name one piece declares another's. Each piece is given the
names the markup's code declares where it stands that it names, by one walk in the order the file writes them:
each declared over the stretch C# declares it for as the C# parser reads each statement - an `@foreach`'s, a
`catch`'s, a pattern's variable, a local a statement's body declares - and a `@{ }` block's locals, and a pattern's
of a statement at the top, to the end of the stretch that holds them: the file's, else a component's content, which
Razor compiles into a template of its own and which declares `context` - or the name its `Context=` gives - else a
section's. Where that class is the component, it is the component's node, and says it is a part, which the linker
joins to its code-behind: the partial of its qualified name, and the partial of its name its `.razor.cs` file
declares beside it, whatever namespace the tree's path gives the component - one type in every
lookup, each finding the other's members as its own. Each `@using` is read by the C# reader
too, so a static one imports its type and an alias names its prefix. The markup - what is no markup taken out - is
read by the markup reader: a PascalCase or dotted element and a `<partial name=` are instantiates, as is an
`Html.Partial("x")` and its kin (`PartialAsync`, `RenderPartial`) the code calls. A `_ViewImports.cshtml` and an
`_Imports.razor` declare each `@using` they hold, and an `_Imports.razor` its `@namespace`, for the whole of their directory's subtree: an import of the
`directory` form, which the linker applies to every file of the language under it, and to no file of another
language or outside it.

A Vue single-file component (`.vue`) is one implementation, `vue`: the component a type named by its file in
PascalCase, as Vue names it, qualified by the file's path - the scope its script declares in, so the script's
declarations are its members - and exported `default`, so `import Foo from './Foo.vue'` binds to it (the JavaScript
reader binds a default import of a single-file component to what it exports by default, one of a CSS module or of data
to its prefix alone, so a member through it is what the file declares and exports, and one of any other style sheet
to nothing) and `Foo.x` to its member `x`. Its `<script>` and `<script setup>` - TypeScript where
their own start tag says `lang="ts"` - are read by the JavaScript reader as the one module Vue compiles them to, the
script's default export the component itself, each of its own declarations that export's options object names a
member the component shows whoever imports it. The options object - written alone, or given to a call such as
`defineComponent` - declares the component's members as Vue reads them: each prop and injection its `props` and
`inject` name (an array's strings or an object's keys), each key of its `methods` and its `computed`, each function
it holds (`data`, `setup`, a lifecycle hook) and each property `data()` and `setup()` return a member of the component
on its own lines, with the code it holds, so the template binds to them and a method's `this.save()` to the method;
each `watch` key is a use of the member it watches, and its handler's code the component's. The props a
`<script setup>`'s `defineProps` declares - an array's strings, an object's keys, the keys of the type it is given,
one written there or an interface or object type the script declares - are members of the component too. A
`<template>`, `<script>` or `<style>` that names its file by `src` is an import of it, as a page's `src` is. Its
`<template>` is read by the markup reader, nested templates among it: a component's tag - `<FooBar>` or `<foo-bar>`,
each naming `FooBar` - an instantiates, and each class and id a use of the rule that styles it; and its code is read
by the JavaScript reader as Vue's compiler compiles it - a `v-on` or `@` value that names a member path a call of it
with whatever the event gives, a function expression the handler itself, anything else statements the event runs,
`$event` its own; a `v-bind`, `:`, `v-model`, `v-if` and every other directive's expression, a dynamic argument, a
`v-for`'s list and `{{ }}` what their expressions read - each name it reads by itself a member of the component
(`this`), as the template compiles it, but a global Vue's compiler leaves to itself (`Math`) and a name a `v-for`'s
aliases or a `v-slot`'s pattern declares where it stands, the template's own and no member; a slot's pattern's
defaults code read once where it is written. Its `<style>` blocks are read by the style sheet's reader in the syntax
each block's `lang` names - CSS where it names none, `scss`, `sass` or `less`, one of another (`stylus`) read as none -
which the css implementation answers for another language's file as the C# reader does: a `<style scoped>` as the
component's own (`StyleScope.Scoped`), so its rules are reached from this component's template alone, a `<style
module>` as a CSS module (`StyleScope.Module`), and any other as the page's. A module block's classes, ids and keyframes
are kept to a scope of the name it binds them by - `$style` where it gives none - so a member that name reads, in the
template (`$style.red`) or the script (`this.$style.red`), is a use of what the block exports by that name
(`CodeQualifierKinds.Module`, naming that scope: `VueExtractor.Bound`), found as an import of a module finds it - a
suffix written onto others' by the names it writes - exact, and nothing else of that name; the template's
`class="red"` reaches none of it.

A sync (`ICodebaseGraphService.SyncAsync`) lists the main checkout by three calls of `IGitClient` that take no lock -
`ListIndexAsync` (`ls-files --stage -v -z`, the one reading of the index the whole tool shares), `ListWorkingFilesAsync`
(`status --porcelain=v2 -z --untracked-files=all --no-renames`) and `HashWorkingFilesAsync` (`hash-object`, its paths on
standard input 200 at a time, a batch git stopped in asked again without the files found gone, and a file at a time
only where that fails too, so a file gone while git hashed it answers null and is said gone, failing nothing else); a
listing of given paths names them as arguments, in batches no
command line outgrows (`CommandLineBatches`: 200 paths and 8,000 characters at most) - leaves out the credential slots
and the tool's state paths under the run's worktrees root before anything reads, says unreadable a name that is not
UTF-8 or that the records cannot hold (`OrchestrationRules.RelativePathProblem`: a drive, a leading slash or backslash, a
part empty, `.` or `..`, which a machine may allow in a file's name), never writing it into a record or asking git of
it by path, and holds every file to the core's rules
(`CodeFileText`: a NUL among the first 8,000 bytes - `BinaryContent.Holds`, git's reading rule and its window, which
the citation scan asks too, where the line-ending rewrite asks git's conversion rule, `BinaryContent.ForConversion`, of a
file declared `text=auto` alone, as git does -
or a Git LFS pointer is binary, UTF-8 or UTF-16 by its mark is read,
anything else is unreadable) before its implementation does. A path whose file git does not look at - marked
skip-worktree, as a sparse checkout marks it, or assume-unchanged - is hashed and read where its file is there and left
out where it is not, looked at no further than its directory where that is not there (asked once a directory, before
its file), since neither its file nor a link can be in it; a repository inside the tree that git lists whole as
untracked is not entered; a file about to be hashed - changed, untracked or not looked at by git - that is a link, or
that a link lies along (`LinkPaths.LeadsElsewhere`, a directory junction git walks into among them), is listed a link
and neither hashed nor read, by the one look every listing takes; and a tracked file git finds gone where a link lies
along its directory - git takes a file below a symbolic link to a directory for gone, where it walks into a junction -
is listed a link too, never gone (asked once a directory), as a check that finds a file not there asks of it, so a path
a link lies along is a link on every system, whether or not a file is where the link leads. Each file whose bytes decided its entry is listed
once more when the reads are done, as a sync lists it (`ListingOf`, nothing said or counted, no HEAD asked; by its
path, or - where the sync listed the tree whole and read more than `ListedWholePast` files, which by their paths take at
least three command lines, each having git read the whole index - by one listing of the tree, so a sync by paths or a
check never has git hash a file it was not given): one the listing no longer gives the blob it was read under, or that
went, is unreadable and keeps nothing. Every file whose bytes decided its entry is then held to how its read
saw it stand: one whose size or time moved while it was read, or by the time that listing is done - truncated and
written again whole, grown and put back, so git lists it clean again under the blob it was read under -
keeps nothing either; so an extract is never stored under a blob its bytes were not. The listing is asked
again, not a hash, because the blob a file is read under is the listing's - the index's where git finds the file
clean, which for one git would clean otherwise than the index holds it is no hash of what it holds - so a file that
needs renormalizing is never taken for one that changed, and no clean filter runs over a file git found clean, a
smudged Git LFS file among them. Every claimed file is decoded streamed, whatever its size
(`CodeFileText.DecodeAsync`, `CodeText.OpenAsync`): one under 1,024 bytes read whole, any other
read through once and then read by position, a block decoded again as its reader reads it, so
neither its bytes nor its text is held whole; a block that no longer decodes is a file that
changed while it was read; a view an earlier build left holding a file `tooLarge` reads it at its
next sync, which says once how many it read so. It reads a file again only
where its blob, its claimant, its claimant's version, or what `languages` decides of it changed, or
where its extract is gone, and tries a file it could not read again at every sync; a run with no graph starts from the
newest earlier run's manifest
that reads, its extracts copied as they are reused and a file whose extract that run lacks read again. Its records go
through `OrchestrationStore`, each strict with its `Problem()` and placed by `OrchestratorLayout`: `graph.json`, the
manifest with its digest; `symbols.jsonl`, the link result naming the manifest's digest and the linker's revision, made
again where either does not match - as lines, its head counting what follows and then each node, edge, count and node's
signs of what the graph does not see on one of its own - a node's id written against the id of the node that contains it
where that is shorter, an edge, a count and signs naming each node by its place - since it grows with the repository and a list read or written whole is held whole while it is
(`JsonLineWriter`, `JsonLineReader`); `extracts/<ab>/<blob>-<path>.<language>-<version>.json`, written once, before the manifest that names them - each node's names written against its parent's and each node a field names by its place (`StoredName`, `FileExtractJson`), so a file nested any depth is kept in bytes that grow with its depth and reads back to the very ids it was given;
`views/<agent>.json`, an agent's view (`CodeGraphView`); and `sync.jsonl`, one line for each sync - what it listed,
hashed, read, reused and removed, the references it found, how many files it could not read (`Unreadable`) and, for one
that failed or a view a moved base could not be held against, why (`Failed`); the store's appends
to it take turns within the process. An extract is named by its path too: an implementation's answer may read the path - its generated
names, its test directories, a file's own names - so a renamed file is read again. The last sync to end with none under
way removes each extract neither the manifest nor a view names, where one may have been left: at a process's first
sync, after a record was written that no longer names an extract the one it replaced named - or in place of one the
sync did not hold, a view's first, a seeded base, a rebuild - after a sync that did not end, and after a view was
dropped - a sync that changed nothing does not look. A sync that failed, not one stopped, also leaves the process
holding no tree of the graph, so the next sync takes each tree as its records say (`CheckAsync` syncs it first, as it
does a tree this process holds neither a link nor a link result of). A record that does not read is refused, its reason
kept: a whole sync builds it again, saying why, and a sync by paths takes nothing and says why; one that could not be read
at all fails the sync. Extraction runs on one of every
`CodebaseGraphService.ReadShare` (2) of the processors.

An agent's view is its worktree listed the same way and held against the base - the main checkout's manifest, synced
first where the run has none - as the overlay of each file the worktree holds otherwise and each of the base's it does
not hold, the digest of the base it stands on with it: a file whose extract the base or an earlier sync of the view made
is not read. A `graphify-codebase` step with `in` syncs that agent's view, or the base for an agent that only reads.
Every agent with a tree of its own is served the view of the tree it reads (`FlowGraphSyncs.WorktreeOf`): an agent that
only reads as well, whose tree holds what the main checkout committed - or the commit its step names (`commit`) - and not
the main checkout's uncommitted changes nor a fold landed since, so its reason step is served its own tree's view
(`FlowGraphSyncs.ViewsOwnTree`), synced by a whole listing once the step's runner brought the tree there - or, for an
attempt an answer goes on with (`ReasonStepRunner.GoingOnOf`), found it as that attempt left it, what it wrote there among
it (`FlowGraphSyncs.ReadiedAsync`) - held against the base, so it reads only what differs - and never at the step's start
before it, when the tree may stand as the agent's last step left it. What its reads are told of a file, their narrowing and
the working set its reads are placed by are then of the tree it reads: one rule matches a file to the view, relative to
the tree the view is of (`CodebaseGraphQueries.PathOf`, which `CodebaseGraphTool.PathOf` and `FullOf` and the working
set read), so a file of the main checkout a reader reads beside its tree is no file of its view. Each tree has its gate: syncs of one wait for each other, syncs of different trees run side by side, and a view takes the base
as one snapshot, which a view reads without the base's gate and never puts back older than a sync left it
(`Graph.Adopt`). When the base moves, every view - one whose first sync is under way among them - is held against it
again under its gate with no file read, from the earlier manifest it stood on, until a newer sync of the base holds them
all, so no view is put back on an older base; a view that could not be held - its record not read or not written, or
the views not listed - is said, a line of `sync.jsonl` and a warning, and made again by its next whole sync: the base's
sync stands, the process lets go of nothing but what it held of that view, and while the base any view stands on is
not known no earlier manifest is let go; a view whose record does not read, or is gone, is let go too, so nothing
this process holds of it stands on a manifest let go. A view's first sync makes the run's first base
before it takes its own gate, and a sync that waited for the base's gate for that makes none where another made it
meanwhile: no gate is held while another view's is waited for, so no two syncs wait on each other. `SyncPathsAsync`
brings a tree up to date by the paths given alone, git asked of those paths (`--literal-pathspecs`), with no listing of
the rest, after its reads either - and, where the tree's HEAD moved since its last sync, by every path git names changed
between the commit that sync recorded and the one HEAD names now (`IGitClient.ListNamesChangedBetweenAsync`), HEAD asked
before anything is listed, so a commit made in the tree meanwhile that touched no path given leaves no file as the older
commit held it under the newer head; where git cannot name them - that commit no longer held, or either naming none - the
tree is synced whole; `CheckAsync` is the check an answer of the graph makes of the files it names before it is given - the `graph` tool's, once a step is
given it (below) - a `stat` against what the view recorded, or against what an earlier check found of a file
whose time alone moved, trusted only where that time is older than the tree's last whole sync's record (`Tree.Written`),
as git trusts an index entry older than its index; a file either moved, whose time is not older, or that could not be
read listed again by its path, as a sync by paths lists it - so it is held to the blob a listing gives it, never to a
hash git's listing would not give - and one whose blob moved read again, one that is a link now kept as one, and one
that could not be read read again, taken where it reads now and changing nothing where it still does not; its tree,
where any of them changed, linked again and written - its head as its last sync recorded it, since a check does not ask
it, and dirty where a file moved or went, since a check cannot tell a change committed since from one not, as a sync by
paths records it; a whole sync alone records the tree clean again - and each extract the answer names read, before the
answer is made - no sweep comes between - and a tree this process holds neither a link nor a link result of synced
first, so the answer is its own link's; `DropViewAsync` takes a view out. What a process linked of each tree is held in memory,
with the base's link result, and the next sync links again from it (`Relink`) - or keeps it, unread and unwritten,
where nothing changed; a process begun again links its first sync whole, from the extracts.

The engine syncs on its own, through `FlowGraphSyncs`, only where the run has a graph and under the claim its step already
holds: `FlowStepRunners` syncs the view of a step that reads it where it starts (`FlowStepRunners.ReadsViewAtStart`: a
reason step, and a `class-closure` check, which reads what the worktree still declares) - its agent's, the one the step it
goes on with works in (`FlowCoordinator.WorkingOf`, which its claims are read through too), and a reader's own tree's once
its runner readied the tree or found it as the attempt an answer goes on with left it, never at its start, and again
where such a check judges a reason step's answer at the answer (`FlowStepRunners.CorrectionsOf`), for it reads the tree
that answer leaves; `fold` and
`delete-agent` sync the base by every path the run's folds changed that the graph has not taken yet
(`FoldLedger.Ungraphed`, `FoldLedger.Changed`) - before each attempt does anything and after its apply - and record each
fold it took (`graphed` in `folds.json`), so a sync that failed, was stopped or was cut off by a crash is owed until one
goes through - a graph whose manifest does not read takes none of them, which is said with why, and they stay owed until a
whole sync builds it again; `refresh` and `rebase` sync their target's view where it has one; every one of these first drops the view
of each agent that is no longer live, `delete-agent`'s own after its deletion among them, so a drop that failed is tried
again. A sync of these that fails, for any cause but a stop, is said - a line of `sync.jsonl` that says why, where it
names the view, and a warning that says what takes it up again - and never fails its step - nor does a reason step's repository that does not read where
the hook looks for it, which its runner finds as it does.
`delete-orchestrator` removes the graph with its run, outside what `--delete-evidence` guards.

What an agent asks of the graph is one tool, `graph` (`Agents\Runtime\CodebaseGraphTool`), whose `op` is `find`, `node`,
`related`, `outline`, `around`, `impact`, `body`, `sites`, `pack`, `changes`, `map`, `edit` or `wholeFile`, over the lookups of `CodebaseGraphQueries` - each node by its id,
handle, qualified name (one written with its language's `::` or `\` read as the model's `.`, or with only its last
parts, `Order.Total`) and simple name and `path:line`, each file's nodes, each node's edges in and out by kind, the words its
name splits into weighed by how rare they are - built once
from a `CodebaseGraphRead`. Every node an answer names is one line with its handle, kind, signature and `path:start-end
#hash` (the first eight characters of its digest); `find` ranks a whole qualified name, then a simple name, then a
prefix, then the share of the query's words weighed by their rarity, a summary's and a path's words a twentieth as much,
generated code after every other, a tie by how near the step's own work each node is (`GraphNearness`: its context
pack or a working set it was given, a file its `writes` covers, a file its agent changed, a path or a name its prompt
holds) and then by id; `related` walks one relation (`GraphRelations.Described`, the one list of each relation and what it
reaches, which the schema's `relation` and the help say: `callers`, `callees`, `derived`, `implementations`, `references`,
`tests`, `includedBy`, `styledBy`, `styles`, and `bases`, `overrides`, `overriddenBy`, `dispatchers`, `users`, `uses`, `parts`
and `tested`, which reach the edges the `node` operation groups - inheritance, implementation and mixins out of a type,
overrides both ways, dispatches into a member, uses both ways, the parts of a declaration, a test's own `tests` edges) as
many hops as asked, from 1, by distance, going through every node it reaches: it keeps the nodes it reached and never
reaches one again, so it is linear in the edges it follows, cycles among them, and a hop that reaches nothing new ends it -
every other part of a declaration walked as the node itself (`CodebaseGraphQueries.OneDeclaration`) but by `parts`, which
walks to them (`GraphRelations.WalksPartsAsOne`); `body` serves each node named once and reads each file once, again only where an extract of it
found its lines moved, and reads a file whole whatever it holds. Three operations answer in one call what an agent
otherwise reads and searches many files for. `outline` of a directory (`CodebaseGraphQueries.FilesUnder`, the directory as
`CodebaseGraphQueries.DirectoryNamed` reads it - either separator, a leading `./` and a trailing separator read as none,
`.` the tree's root - in another case where the tree's file system finds a name in any case) gives every file under it, its
subdirectories' too, a section for each directory that holds any directly, by path - each file one result whose block is
its own node's line with the language that read it, or the state none read it in, and `test` where it is test code
(`CodebaseGraphQueries.TestFile`, the view's one rule of a file that declares a test, `ExtractNode.Test` or one the link
finds by its type), then each of its top declarations (`CodebaseGraphQueries.TopDeclarations`: every type and member no
type or member of the file holds, a namespace's among them, each with what it and the declarations inside it exercise by
the link's `tests` edges, each declaration read once - the outermost it is or is inside found from its parent's); the
repository's `outline` outlines the root's own files so too. `around` gives a node's place: what it is declared in,
outermost first - its file, its namespace's part there, its type (`CodebaseGraphQueries.Containers`, by each extract's
`ExtractNode.Parent`) - its siblings, every other declaration directly inside the nearest of those
(`CodebaseGraphQueries.Siblings`, `CodebaseGraphQueries.Inside`: a file's top, or what a node contains with its other
parts), its members, the declarations just before and just after it in its file (`CodebaseGraphQueries.Beside`, the
outermost on each side), and its callers and callees as `node` groups them, each a section counted in its caption at
`CodebaseGraphTool.NodeLinesAKind` a page. `impact` gives what a change of a node reaches, by the one walk of a change's
impact the change-first pack leads with (`CodebaseContextPack.Impact`, over `CodebaseContextPack.Impacted`, the edges of
`GraphRelations.Impact`) from the node and every other part of its declaration: each node it settles under the relation
whose edge reached it - its callers at every distance, `overrides`, `overriddenBy`, `implementations`, `dispatchers`,
`derived`, and its `tests` last, every test that reaches any of them - with how many edges its best path has and the path
itself, each edge said as the pack says one (`CodebaseContextPack.Phrase`) with the node it leaves by its handle, nearest
first and then best first, at `CodebaseGraphTool.RelatedLines` of each a page; a node the step may not read is neither
listed nor gone through, only counted, and a hub is gone through, its many neighbours ranked down, never cut. `sites` answers "every place that decides this" of one datum
(`data`: a symbol as `symbol` takes one - a handle, an id or a `path:line`, which names its one node, or a qualified or simple
name - a key path, dotted - a name holding a dot or a bracket quoted in brackets, `Logging.LogLevel["Microsoft.AspNetCore"]`
or `Logging.LogLevel['Microsoft.AspNetCore']`, or with its names' own dots as they are - or as .NET's configuration spells
one (`Payments:TimeoutSeconds`, `Payments__TimeoutSeconds`), a
diagnostic id, a rule's selector as a rule writes it, or a quoted literal, asked by its value alone and never by the symbols):
every definer of it across files and languages (`CodebaseGraphQueries.DefinersOf`, by the one reading of what an agent writes
`Resolve` reads too - the node a handle, an id or a `path:line` names alone, else every node any rule of a name finds, a
qualified name, a simple one, one written with a language's `::` or `\` outside a quoted name, one spelt as the one owner of a
key path's spellings reads it (`CodeKeyPaths.Dotted`) - a path typed with single quotes, with both quote marks or with quotes a
name needs not read first as the writer writes it (`CodeKeyPaths.Canonical`), every rule after reading that form - or with some
of its scopes, of a key path every key whose own name spells it as .NET's configuration reads a key's name - an environment
variable's, a settings file's flat key (`CodeKeyPaths.Spellings`: `Payments__TimeoutSeconds` under a compose file's
`environment`) - so a key path in any spelling finds the same keys, and, last of the rules, the loose form of a dotted path,
its names' own dots written as they are, naming every key whose path so written is that text (`CodeKeyPaths.Unescaped`, one
index built once a view, in the queries alone and never the linker, for code splits a dotted literal), where `Resolve` takes
the first rule that finds one - a selector's own leading dot kept, so `.header` is never the element rule `header` or a key of
that name), then one hop off every definer's own edges, a definer the step's reads do not reach among
them, each place it reaches held to the reads where it stands (`CodebaseGraphQueries.SitesOf`, each way a group read from the
relations' own edges - `GraphRelations.Edges` - and the `node` operation's): their callers, their users, what makes them, what
names them by their kind - a type mention, an `isinstance`, an `instanceof`, a `catch` or an `except` - what inherits them or
mixes them in, what implements them or answers an interface's member for a type through its dispatches, what overrides them
and what they override, a part of a declaration walked as the node itself, each node with how sure the surest edge that
reaches it is - and no site's own edges walked, so a hub is listed and never gone through; every literal whose value is the datum or holds
it as a whole word (`CodebaseGraphQueries.LiteralSites`, read once an ask over the literals of every extract the view holds -
no node of the graph is a literal's, so the read is the one index of them) - the datum searched for by the name of the node it
names by itself, by a selector whole, else by its last name (`CodebaseGraphQueries.SitesSearch`, `CodeKeyPaths.LastName`, a
path's places read by `CodeKeyPaths.Places`, which reads a place in brackets only as a key's path writes one - an item's digits,
a quoted name, whose dot parts nothing and whose own text is the last name (`Microsoft.AspNetCore` of
`Logging.LogLevel["Microsoft.AspNetCore"]`) - so `this[]` of `Canvas.this[]` and `operator[]` of `Vec::operator[]` are names; and
a name written with some of its places ends a path only where one of the path's places begins (`CodeKeyPaths.EndsWithPlaces`),
as the context pack reads a class's site too - for a
name written with its scopes and a key path in any spelling are written in code and in data by their last name (`shape.Area()`,
`"TimeoutSeconds": 30`) - a datum spelt as .NET's configuration spells a key path read as one where it names a key, where
only the path it spells finds its definers, code's members, none a key (`Secret` of `JwtSettings:Secret`, a member the
options pattern binds a section to), or where nothing names it and it is written as no node's id and no file's line, and as
the name code declares where a definer, none of them a key, is found by it as it is written - by its name, its qualified

come file by file, each file's in order - and where a file's moved, writes nothing more and only finds the rest: every
moved file of the call is checked again in one check (`CodebaseGraphTool.ReadAgainAsync`), the answer begun again and the
files that held a hit searched again, so a search pays for the files that moved and one view, never a view a file, and
its hits still stand under the declarations as the files stand now, in the listing's order. It writes each hit inside one under that
declaration's line, as `GraphLines.Of` names a node, the innermost a type, a member or a section that holds the hit's line
(`GraphFileDeclarations.Holding`, by `CodebaseGraphQueries.AtLine`; a namespace or a project heads no hit), its hits and
their context lines indented beneath it, the separator between two of its hits indented with them and the line said again
only where a hit outside it came between; a hit outside every declaration, or of a file the graph does not parse, is
written as it is, and a step with no graph answers as it always has. The answer is written a line at a time - the
declaration's line a block's head (`ResultLines.HeadAsync`), each line beneath it a line of its block - and paged as
every answer is, by `read_result`, each line whole, a page that begins among a declaration's lines beginning with its line
again (`TextBlocks`). A range of `view_file` (`AgentToolRuntime.RangeAsync`) is headed
(`AgentToolRuntime.RangeDeclarations`) by the declarations the lines it gives meet (`GraphFileDeclarations.Meeting`), each
joining the head once a line given reaches its first line, the head charged with the lines to a page's room
(`KeptResults.Room`), the first line's among them - the lines stopping where the two would pass it, the rest asked for by
its next start as any is, and a head that passes the room with the first line written with that line as the call's
answer a line at a time, the head a block (`AgentToolRuntime.PagedRangeAsync`), kept and given a page at a time by
`read_result` as every answer longer than a page is, so no range is sent over a page however many declarations begin on
its first line. `AgentTools.InAGraphStep` says so in the two tools' own descriptions where the step's graph was
built. Its reads narrowed (`graphReads: narrow`, the default) answer a whole `view_file` of a file the view holds as parsed
over `CodebaseGraphTool.NarrowLines` lines with the file's outline in its place (`CodebaseGraphTool.WholeReadAsync`): a line
saying how to read its lines - a range, a page, a body, or `wholeFile` with why - then the outline as `outline` with its
path gives it, every declaration as the file stands, all of it, paged as every answer is - so the step learns the
structure in the call it read by, and no turn is spent on a refusal; a range, a page, a search and a write pass; a file the
graph is not sure of (`CodebaseGraphQueries.UnsureOfFile`: a `dynamic` mark, generated, or more than a quarter of its
references `candidates`) passes as an escape `lowConfidence`, and `graph`'s `wholeFile` lifts the narrowing for one file
the view holds as parsed for the rest of the step, an escape `stated` with the agent's reason and the lines and tokens the
view read the file as - a path it holds no parsed file at a usage line, nothing read. An outline shows the agent the file's
declarations and none of its lines: it is no view an edit may follow, nor a read of the run's.
The working set (`CodebaseWorkingSet`) is what a reason step that has a graph worked with, kept in its
directory as `working-set.json` (`OrchestrationStore.WriteWorkingSet`): each node it edited, served, read or found
(`WorkingSetUses`), with how often it was touched and its handle, file, lines and hash at the step's end - every one,
however many - edited first, then by how often - and a node the view no longer
holds kept by its id, marked gone. `CodebaseWorkingSet.Make` reads it from the step's `graph.jsonl` (`GraphStepLine`,
one `GraphCallLine` for each call of the tool, from the facts its answer carries, `GraphToolFacts`: each node a call
asked about by name is found, each a line of which a `body`'s answer gives, within its cap, is served, and an `edit` is
matched by the lines it wrote, as every write is, the node it named edited where they no longer declare it; the nodes
a `pack` answer's page lists, `GraphToolFacts.Listed`, are kept on its line, `GraphCallLine.Listed`, and are no use - a
line of each, never its lines - so none is found or served, and a line an earlier build wrote without them still reads) and from
the tool calls its stored stream holds (`OrchestrationStore.ReadStepStream`; a call is named by its `ToolCallStarted` or
the `AssistantMessage` that made it), on every client's form: a read (`Read`, `view_file`) by where the lines its answer
gave stand once in the file as the step left it, else by the first and the last number it gave them, a write (`Edit`,
`replace_in_file`, `insert_in_file`) where its new text stands once there - every place, with `replace_all` - else by
the lines it names, else counted unplaced with a deletion, which writes no lines, and a whole file's write (`Write`,
`create_file`) by every line, counted unplaced where its file does not read as the step left it; text is found line by line, each line's trailing blanks aside, as a client may strip
them where it writes - each matched to the declarations whose own lines it meets (`CodeOwnLines`, a member's
lines never its type's), as the view at the step's end holds them. The coordinator names in each reason step's
`FlowStepRun.WorkedFrom` the instances whose sets seed its pack: the step it goes on with (`resume`), each step it
depends on directly - its own `dependsOn` and `on` and each enclosing group's, a group by each reason step in it -
then its own earlier visits of the same work item (`FlowInstanceId.SameStep`: the same id but for the visits and
iterations after its innermost item - and within the recovery, of visits for the same failure or issue,
`FlowCoordinator.EarlierVisitsOf`), newest first, each that began, once; `FlowWorkingSets.SeedsOf` reads their sets
into `ContextPackRequest.Worked` (`CodebaseWorkingSet.Seeds`: each node once, edited where any set says so, none
gone). A reason step that has a graph writes both files as it ends (`FlowStepGraph.Ended`: the working set made from
the view at the step's end, its `graph.jsonl` and its stored stream) and its pack is given the seeds; its `graph.jsonl`
holds a line for each launch's first message, written as the message is and before any line of that launch's calls
(`GraphPromptLine`: the pushed map's tokens and the pushed pack's seeds, nodes, tokens and what was left out, or the tokens of the
changes a conversation gone on with was told in their place, or why no pack was given, by one rule (`FlowStepGraph.NoPackOf`) -
`FlowStepGraph.NoPackHeld` where the pack made held nothing, said first, since such a step is offered no `pack` to ask,
and `FlowStepGraph.NoPackPushed` for a step at `tools` that pushes none), one line for each call of the tool (`GraphCallLine`, with its answer's estimated tokens and its text hits), and
one for each escape of its narrowing and each whole read the narrowing answered with the file's outline
(`GraphEscapeLine`, `GraphOutlinedLine`: the file, its lines, what reading it whole would have cost and what the outline
cost) - a line an earlier build wrote of a read the narrowing refused (`GraphDeniedLine`) still read, and counted in no
figure - and its figures - mode, view, `mapTokens`, the pack with how many of its nodes the step then used,
`changesTokens` (the three its last launch was pushed: a pack made and not pushed counts 0, for its first message held
none of it), `pulled` (the pages of the `map` and of the `pack` its tool was asked for and gave, each `pages` and
`tokens`, counted from its `graph.jsonl`'s answered calls and among the served tokens, the `pack`'s with `nodes`, the
nodes its pages listed, each once, and `used`, how many of them the step then used - by the one rule the pushed pack's
`used` is counted by, `CodebaseWorkingSet.Used`: its working set's nodes the view still holds that they list), calls,
served tokens, bodies, text hits, edits made and refused,
whole-file reads counted from the stored stream on every client's form as the working set reads its calls - neither a
page nor a range, its answer the file's numbered lines, so an outline given is none (`CodebaseWorkingSet.WholeFileReads`)
- the outlined reads (`outlinedReads`: how many, `tokens` what reading them whole would have cost, `outlineTokens` what
the outlines given in their place cost) and escapes - are held in its `step.json` under `graph` and summed for the run's
report (`FlowRunReport`: its `totals.graph`, the pushed pack's `packTokens` beside the `pulled` map's pages and tokens
and the pulled pack's pages, tokens, nodes and used).
`query-codebase-graph` (`CodebaseGraphQueryService`) runs its read operations by hand - `--find`, `--node`, `--related`,
`--outline` (a file the view holds; a path that names no node and is written as a file is, or is a directory the view holds
files under; a symbol else), `--around`, `--impact`, `--body` and `--sites` - on the base or an agent's view
through `ICodebaseGraphService.ReadOnlyAsync` - the records as they stand on disk, no gate, no sync, nothing written, a
view linked in memory from the base's files and its record, and a link result another linker made linked again in
memory - with a read rule that refuses what no graph lists (`CodebaseGraphService.NeverListed`: the credential slots,
the tool's own state and the workflows' own files, whose prompts a pack would match first), the main checkout's run
and configuration wherever it is typed (`MainTree`); a misuse is told by `CodebaseGraphTool.Misused` before anything is
read, and a view not made yet is said and the base answered; `--page` asks any page of the answer, its document answering
the digest of the graph answered from (`CodebaseGraphQueries.Graph`), the page, the pages, the whole answer's total and the
page's entries, each with what it counts toward the total, its section's caption and its node; it keeps nothing between
calls, each counting its page on the graph as it stands, so a script reading page after page compares the digest; it ends
0, 13 where the run has no graph and 10 for a usage error, and no host is asked to run it.

## Anchor registries

An anchor is a named piece of deferred work, kept as one row of a markdown registry. Two
registries hold every anchor, and each anchor lives in exactly one of them:
`anchors.pendingAnchorsPath` holds the live anchors, and `anchors.doneAnchorsPath` is the
archive of closed ones. `init` creates each registry that is missing from a skeleton
embedded in the tool, and never touches one that exists.

### One table, six cells, one verdict

A registry is an introduction and exactly one anchor table, recognised by its header row,
`| Anchor | Priority | Status | Trigger | Closing work | Cross-refs |`. A file with no
anchor table or a second one, or with an anchor row outside the table or inside some other
table, is malformed: where a new row belongs would be a guess, and a stray row is counted by
nothing. Every command that reads or changes anchors refuses a malformed registry (exit 20)
rather than answer from rows it cannot trust, while `read-anchors --lint`,
`check-anchor-balance` and `check-anchor-arms` report the problem among their findings
(exit 1). A directory where a
registry's file belongs, or a file that cannot be read, is refused by every command, `init`
included (exit 20): taken for no registry, a directory sent its reader to `init`, which then failed
to write over it.

The Status cell is the only verdict that decides: `🟠 OPEN`, `⏳ GATED`, `🔵 DISCLOSED` or `✅ CLOSED`. A
row is closed exactly when its Status cell starts with ✅, and every other glyph, including
one nobody anticipated, reads as open: a row wrongly read as open stays visible as work,
while a row wrongly read as closed disappears from every count. Nothing is inferred from
the prose cells to decide a verdict or a count. A registry whose rows open a closed Trigger
with the closure itself can say
so with `anchors.triggerCarriesVerdict`: a closed row's Trigger then opens with ✅ and no
other row's does, the writing commands refuse a row whose two cells disagree, a fold weighs
the two as the one verdict they state (see "Seeding and folding", above), and the lint
and the balance report one, so that a row states its verdict once, even where it states it
twice. A closed row's Trigger may open with ✅ and then 🧾 instead, the bookkeeping pair, when
its closure only repairs the mark of work done before the change that closes it (see the
balance, below). Whatever the setting, a closed row whose Trigger opens with the two marks where
they are not read as the pair - the setting is off, or emphasis stands between them - is noted,
failing nothing, since only its writer knows whether they meant it: by the lint wherever it is, and
by the balance where it is a closure the change made.

### Writing a row

Commands take fields, never rows. Line breaks collapse and pipes are escaped, because a raw
`|` adds a column and shifts every later cell, and a wrapped row hides its id from every
search. Only the breaks go - each, with the whitespace either side of it, as one space, at
every boundary a reader of the file might split a line at - and so does whitespace at the
value's very start and end; every other character is kept as given: a run of spaces or a tab
inside a line is often a cell's evidence, quoted tool output or aligned figures. A value that already holds an escaped pipe is refused: escaping it
again would double the backslash, and it usually means someone copied a raw table line. A
cell given in a file is read as UTF-8, and a file that is not, or that opens with a byte-order
mark, is refused by name rather than cleaned. Every composed row is read back through the same
parser before anything is written. Every value a command shows or quotes - a cell, the words a
change adds or takes away, a refusal's own text - is given whole, never cut to an excerpt; a
change of a cell is said word by word however long the cell, compared by the one diff of two
sequences (`SequenceDiff`); an id `read-anchor` does not find names every id of its namespace a
registry holds; and a row with no id in its Anchor cell is told from another by the whole of that
cell's text.

A value the door would store cut is refused (`AnchorCellCuts`, exit 10): an id cut where a line ends, found as
check-anchor-citations finds one (`AnchorIdScanner`: at a hyphen that ends the line, or where the next line carries it
on into a row's id); an id with a space after one of its hyphens, across the segments a citation carries; a path's
directory ending a line before a file's name; and a path with a space after a `/` before a file's name, where it starts at
a directory at the top of the tree - read as the write runs. A value that newly cites an id no row holds is refused
too (exit 13): every id a new row cites, and every id a changed cell cites that its stored text did not, read as
check-anchor-citations reads a citation, the ids of the batch a row is applied in resolving too. A cut or a citation the
stored cell already held is history, and is not judged again.

`set-anchor` rebuilds only the cells it was given and writes every other cell back byte for
byte; a row whose cell count is wrong is refused rather than guessed at. A new id must match
the minting rule (`D-` and at least three segments by default), while an id already in a
registry only has to be well formed and is never rewritten.

### Where a row goes

The destination is derived from the status, never named by a caller: a closed anchor goes to
the done registry and every other status to the pending one, so a live anchor can never be
filed where nothing reads it as work. New rows are appended at the end of the table; tables
are never sorted.

A move is two file writes and cannot be atomic. The destination is written first and the
source second, so an interruption leaves the row in both registries, where the next change
refuses the duplicate loudly, and never in neither, which every count would read as a
closure. Each file is replaced whole through a rename, so a reader never sees a torn file.

### Which copy, and who may write

A registry git tracks is read and changed in the tree the command runs in, so the change
travels with that branch. A registry git ignores has no copy in a worktree, and is resolved
in the main checkout, where ignored harness state always lives. `init` resolves registries
the same way, so one it creates from inside a worktree is where every later command looks.

Every change holds a machine-wide named mutex, keyed by the two registry paths, for the whole
of its read, decide and write. .NET supports named mutexes on Windows, Linux and macOS alike,
and named semaphores on Windows only. A mutex must be released by the thread that took it, so
the locked work is synchronous by construction. A change that finds the lock held waits for it
while its holder lives, through the hold every machine-wide lock of the tool is waited for by
(`MachineWideMutex.HoldAsync`): a holder that ends holding it lets it go as it ends, so the wait
ends when the holder does, however long its work. The wait is said as it begins, naming what
holds the lock, and every five minutes while it lasts, under `anchors`, so a change waiting on a
long one reads as waiting and never as hung; the person's interruption ends it, nothing read or
written. A read takes the lock too, for as long
as reading the two files takes, and waits for it the same way. A lock that belongs to another
user writes nothing and exits 13, and one the system
will not open stops the command (exit 15) - an open the system fails is tried again through
`Retrying` while it says something new, and given up once it says the same twice. The mutex's
name keeps its 128-bit digest (`MachineWideMutex.NameFor`'s `[..16]`) for good: a version naming
a subject another way would take a lock beside the one an older version holds. One file needs no lock, since every write replaces a
whole file in one rename. Two do: a move never leaves its row in neither file, but a read of the
destination before the move's first write and of the source after its second finds it in
neither, which reads as an anchor closed or lost, and a read the other way round finds it in
both, a duplicate.

### The balance

`check-anchor-balance` compares the working tree with a base commit (`--base`, default
`HEAD`), measured from where HEAD's history left the base's (`git merge-base`), as
`check-anchor-citations --current-pr` measures a branch: the base itself where it is an
ancestor of HEAD. Compared with directly, a base that had moved on counted its own later
